title: Damaged DXF opens with exit 0 and keeps 5 of 1,504 recoverable entities, with no warning
author: gozzy-nwogbo
body:
**Version:** cadcraft-cli 0.6.2 (release build), macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon

**What happens**

A damaged DXF loads as an almost empty drawing. Nothing in the output says records were skipped, and `convert` then writes the 5-entity drawing out as if it were complete.

**Repro** (public file: [mozman/ezdxf `integration_tests/data/recover01.dxf`](https://github.com/mozman/ezdxf/blob/master/integration_tests/data/recover01.dxf), a deliberately damaged test file)

```sh
cadcraft-cli info recover01.dxf    # "entityCount": 5, all LINE, exit 0
```

For comparison, ezdxf's recover mode reads 1,441 LINE and 63 TEXT entities from the same file:

```python
from ezdxf import recover
doc, auditor = recover.readfile("recover01.dxf")
```

The built-in recovery path does not change this: `cadcraft-cli run --cmd 'recover {"path":"recover01.dxf"}'` reports `0 errors found, 0 fixed.` and the drawing still has 5 entities.

**Expected:** recover more of the file, or at least warn (and exit non-zero, or report a count of skipped records) when large parts of the entity section could not be read.
**Actual:** 5 entities, exit 0, no warning. `convert` to DXF writes the 5-entity file.

**Related:** #406 (closed; added AUDIT and RECOVER). **Possibly related:** #863 (a drawing that opens almost empty). That report has a different trigger (a valid drawing that renders mostly blank), so I am filing this separately with a public repro file.

*Found with an automated test harness (Claude Code agents, ezdxf as an independent check) while evaluating the Craft apps for local agent use. I re-ran the repro above by hand.*

title: Web build: open DWG files (gaps.md FF12)
author: tnorverto
body:
Web build: open DWG files (gaps.md FF12)

Thanks for CADCraft. We’re testing the 0.6.2 web build as the drawing viewer inside our architecture studio’s internal web app, embedded through the new host bridge (?host=parent, cadcraft:open). The bridge works well, and DXF drawings open fine.

The problem: our files are DWG. The desktop app and cadcraft-cli read them, but the web build refuses them:

invalid parameters for open: DWG files can’t be opened in the web build yet, save as DXF

Our workaround and its cost: the server converts each DWG first with cadcraft-cli run X.dwg --cmd 'saveas {"path":"X.dxf","binary":true,"version":2018}'. On real project plans:

binary DXF is about 4× the DWG, ASCII DXF about 8× (a 44 MB DWG becomes 176 MB binary / 352 MB ASCII);
so plans that are about 45 MB as DWG already reach the 256 MB browser limit;
conversion takes 5–30 s per plan before the viewer can start.

Request: read DWG in the web build (the FF12 row of docs/gaps.md), so cadcraft:open accepts DWG bytes directly, like a file picked or dropped in the desktop app.

Related, smaller: when an open sent through the host bridge is refused (format or size), the reason only appears in the status bar. Posting cadcraft:failed (or a dedicated open-failed message) to the parent would let the host page tell the user.

title: feat(mtext): Add editable rotation property for MTEXT entities (AutoCAD parity)
author: mittooboy
body:
Description

AutoCAD supports arbitrary rotation of MTEXT entities through the Properties palette and the ROTATE command.

CADCraft should provide equivalent functionality so that multiline text can be oriented at any angle within a drawing.

Expected functionality

Selecting an MTEXT entity should expose a numeric Rotation property in the Properties palette.

Rotation should support arbitrary angles, including 0°, 45°, 90°, 180°, and 270°.

The entire MTEXT block, including its bounding box, alignment, and word wrapping, should rotate together.

The ROTATE command should operate correctly on MTEXT entities.

Rotation must be preserved when saving and reopening drawings.

DXF import/export should correctly interpret and preserve MTEXT rotation, including the applicable DXF rotation/direction-vector representations.

Acceptance criteria

MTEXT rotation is independently editable without modifying text content or formatting.

Rendering, selection boundaries, and hit-testing respect the rotation angle.

Existing text justification and attachment points behave consistently after rotation.

DXF round-trip testing confirms that MTEXT orientation is retained.

Reference: AutoCAD MTEXT entity rotation behaviour.

This is important for architectural, engineering, and technical drawings where multiline annotations frequently need to follow angled geometry.

title: Implement AutoCAD-style editing interfaces for TEXT and MTEXT
author: mittooboy
body:
CADCraft should support distinct editing interfaces for single-line TEXT and multiline MTEXT entities, consistent with AutoCAD's established editing workflows.

Expected Behaviour

1. TEXT (Single-Line Text)

Double-clicking a TEXT entity should open a small Edit Text dialog box.

The dialog should display the existing text content.

Users should be able to modify the text without interacting directly with the drawing canvas.

Confirming the dialog should update the TEXT entity.

Cancelling should preserve the original text.

2. MTEXT (Multiline Text)

Double-clicking an MTEXT entity should activate an in-place text editor.

Editing should occur directly within the drawing canvas, at the MTEXT entity's position.

The editor should support multiline content, text selection, paragraph formatting, and existing text properties.

The editing boundary should reflect the MTEXT entity's width and alignment.

Finishing or cancelling editing should behave consistently with standard CAD workflows.

Acceptance Criteria

TEXT opens a compact Edit Text dialog.

MTEXT opens an in-place multiline editor.

Existing text properties, including position, rotation, height, alignment, and formatting, are preserved.

Editing does not unintentionally alter entity geometry or formatting.

Undo/Redo works correctly for both editing workflows.

Reference

AutoCAD supports dialog-based editing for single-line TEXT through its configurable text-editor settings, while MTEXT normally uses an in-place multiline editor.

title: fix(file): predictable save staging file permits concurrent corruption and follows symlinks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
- Severity: **High** (provisional audit triage).
- Confidence: **high in the source-level defect**.
- Baseline: upstream `main` at e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa.
- Validation: static source inspection only; Rust tooling was unavailable. The scenarios below are proposed regression cases, **not executed reproductions**. No destructive testing was performed.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:399–406](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L399-L406) builds `format!("{path}.cadcraft-tmp")`, writes it with `std::fs::write`, then renames it over the destination. Staging is neither unique nor exclusively created. Replacement also uses the staging file permissions rather than preserving the existing destination mode.

## Trigger conditions
Two CADCraft processes save the same destination concurrently. Separately, another principal with write access to the destination directory can pre-create the predictable staging path as a symlink. On Unix, replacing a restricted destination can also change its mode according to the staging creation mode/umask.

## Realistic impact
Concurrent saves can truncate/write the same staging inode and publish interleaved or partial content. A pre-existing staging symlink is followed by the write, potentially overwriting another file accessible to the saving process. The symlink risk requires directory control; this is not a default remote vulnerability. Permission widening is conditional on the original mode and umask.

## Recommended remediation
Use a unique, exclusively created same-directory staging file, preserve intended permissions, write and synchronize it, then atomically replace the destination with appropriate platform semantics. Clean up only the staging file owned by this operation. Do not rely on a prior existence check.

## Suggested regression tests
In disposable directories, check concurrent saves lea…

title: fix(cli): --save overwrites the destination directly and can destroy the previous drawing on write failure
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
- Severity: **High** (provisional audit triage).
- Confidence: **high in the source-level defect**.
- Baseline: upstream `main` at e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa.
- Validation: static source inspection only; Rust tooling was unavailable. The scenarios below are proposed regression cases, **not executed reproductions**. No destructive testing was performed.

## Root cause and source evidence
[apps/cadcraft-cli/src/main.rs:221–228](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/apps/cadcraft-cli/src/main.rs#L221-L228) serializes to memory and calls `std::fs::write(out, &bytes)` directly. [apps/cadcraft-cli/src/main.rs:343–349](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/apps/cadcraft-cli/src/main.rs#L343-L349) routes `run --save` through this export helper rather than a staged replacement.

## Trigger conditions
Save over an existing drawing using the CLI and encounter a filesystem write failure or process interruption after the file is opened/truncated.

## Realistic impact
Returning an I/O error does not restore the previous valid destination. It may have already been replaced by an empty or partial file. Serialization failure before the write does not have this problem.

## Recommended remediation
Use a shared safe-write implementation with unique exclusive same-directory staging and atomic replacement. Preserve the existing destination on all pre-replacement failures; do not copy the engine helper unchanged because its fixed temporary path has separate races.

## Suggested regression tests
With a fault-injectable writer and disposable output, fail after a partial write and verify the original bytes remain intact; test successful overwrite, new file creation, and serialization-error controls.

## Related reports
Related: #540. This is the CLI write path, distinct from the engine staging-file race.

[crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs:1559–1583](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs#L1559-L1583) flattens selected open polylines into segments and records an owner as used as soon as one segment joins. [crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs:1612–1619](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs#L1612-L1619) removes each used owner in its entirety, without requiring all of its segments to be consumed.

## Trigger conditions
Select first a line from (1,0) to (1,1), then an open polyline through (0,0), (1,0), (2,0), and JOIN. The first horizontal segment can attach to the line; after that, the other horizontal branch no longer touches a chain endpoint.

## Realistic impact
The resulting chain omits the remaining branch, but the whole original polyline is removed. This is successful-command drawing data loss, not a claim that undo cannot recover it.

title: fix(table): editing an imported large table silently truncates rows and columns
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
- Severity: **High** (provisional audit triage).
- Confidence: **high in the source-level defect**.
- Baseline: upstream `main` at e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa.
- Validation: static source inspection only; Rust tooling was unavailable. The scenarios below are proposed regression cases, **not executed reproductions**. No destructive testing was performed.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:145–173](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L145-L173) invokes `normalize` before every edit; it truncates dimensions/cells to `MAX_ROWS=2000` and `MAX_COLS=200`. [crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs:529–547](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/io/src/dxf_read.rs#L529-L547) accepts larger imported dimensions, subject to its separate cell budget.

## Trigger conditions
Import a valid table with 2001 rows and one column, or one row and 201 columns, then successfully edit a cell inside the first row/column.

## Realistic impact
Unrelated trailing rows/columns and their data are removed as a side effect of the edit. The import and edit limits disagree.

## Recommended remediation
Do not silently apply creation limits to existing tables. Preserve their complete grid during supported edits, or reject the operation explicitly before mutation if the existing table is too large.

## Suggested regression tests
Import tables just above each edit limit with sentinel values at the end, edit the first cell and verify either complete preservation or a nonmutating explicit refusal. Cover at-limit tables and undo/redo.

## Related reports
Related closed #534 implemented table editing; no exact truncation report found.

title: fix(geom): circle intersection tolerance collapses valid disparate-radius secants to a false tangent
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
- Severity: **Medium** (provisional audit triage).
- Confidence: **High in the source-level mechanism; runtime impact is unmeasured**.
- Baseline: upstream `main` at e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa.
- Validation: static source inspection only; Rust tooling was unavailable. Proposed regression scenarios below were not executed. No resource-exhaustion workload or destructive test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/geom/src/intersect.rs:65–83](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/geom/src/intersect.rs#L65-L83) normalizes by the largest radius/distance and treats every `h2 <= 1e-12` as tangent, returning the chord foot.

## Trigger conditions
Intersect circles with very different radii, for example radii 10000000 and 1 whose centers are 10000000 apart. The small circle crosses the large circle, but the normalized squared half-chord is below the fixed threshold.

## Realistic impact
The function returns a single chord-foot point rather than the two intersections. That point need not lie on the small circle, affecting intersection-dependent snapping/editing. This is an analytic source case, not a Rust runtime reproduction.

## Recommended remediation
Use stable chord construction and an error-aware tangency predicate that accounts for the smaller circle/chord scale rather than a fixed normalized squared threshold.

## Suggested regression tests
Check independently derived two-circle intersections over disparate radii and both sides of the threshold, asserting residuals on both circles. Include true tangency, separation, containment, swapped arguments and uniform scaling.

## Related reports
No exact matching issue found in the open/closed issue review.

- Baseline: upstream `main` at e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa.
- Validation: static source inspection only; Rust tooling was unavailable. Proposed regression scenarios below were not executed. No resource-exhaustion workload or destructive test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/render/src/fill.rs:26–54](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/render/src/fill.rs#L26-L54) uses vertex y values as slab boundaries, sorts edge intersections only at each slab midpoint, and extends that ordering to both boundaries when emitting triangles.

## Trigger conditions
A self-crossing contour, such as a bowtie, or separate crossing loops have an intersection strictly inside a slab.

## Realistic impact
Edge ordering changes inside the slab, so emitted trapezoids/triangles do not represent the requested even-odd region. Fill can overlap or cover the wrong area.

## Recommended remediation
Split slabs/edges at crossing events or use a bounded triangulator that correctly supports self-intersecting even-odd contours.

## Suggested regression tests
For a small bowtie, assert point coverage/parity on both sides of the crossing using an independent oracle, not triangle count alone. Include simple contours, holes, reversed winding and crossings between loops.

## Related reports
No exact matching issue found in the open/closed issue review.

[crates/render/src/fill.rs:65–71](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/render/src/fill.rs#L65-L71) and [crates/render/src/wide.rs:19–25](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/render/src/wide.rs#L19-L25) use compacted indices to fetch source widths. title: fix(region): coarse long-segment registration can omit real boundary intersections
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
- Severity: **Medium** (provisional audit triage).
- Confidence: **High in the nonconservative indexing; medium in specific user-visible drawing impact until runtime verification**.
- Baseline: upstream `main` at e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa.
- Validation: static source inspection only; Rust tooling was unavailable. Proposed regression scenarios below were not executed. No resource-exhaustion workload or destructive test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/geom/src/region.rs:100–120](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/geom/src/region.rs#L100-L120) registers a long segment only in sampled grid cells when its bounding box covers more than 4096 cells; exact pair testing occurs only for segments sharing a registered cell. The coarse branch uses strides greater than one for sufficiently wide/tall cell spans.

## Trigger conditions
A short segment intersects a long diagonal within an unsampled cell and does not occupy any of the long segment's sampled cells.

## Realistic impact
The pair is never sent to exact intersection testing, so boundary graph topology can be wrong and region/hatch discovery can miss a boundary. The indexing omission is source-confirmed; a complete drawing-level reproduction remains to be run.

## Recommended remediation
Use conservative broad-phase coverage, such as exact segment-cell traversal, or test long segments through a separate conservative index/list. Do not trade correctness for silent pair omission when applying work limits.

## Suggested regression tests
Under test-only reduced grid thresholds, compare the candidate pairs/regions against a brute-force small-graph oracle with a crossing in an omitted cell. Include long-long, long-short, translated and scaled controls.

## Related reports
Related closed #106 concerns island detection and #723 concerns command-level budgets, not this broad-phase omission.

title: fix(lisp): blocking input resumptions bypass the routine execution cap
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
- Severity: **High** (provisional audit triage).
- Confidence: **high in the source-level defect**.
- Baseline: upstream `main` at e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa.
- Validation: static source inspection only; Rust tooling was unavailable. Proposed regression scenarios below were not executed. No destructive testing or external-system probing was performed.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/lisp/eval.rs:195–223](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/lisp/eval.rs#L195-L223) initializes a fresh step counter on every `Machine::run`. [crates/engine/src/lisp/mod.rs:344–383](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/lisp/mod.rs#L344-L383) charges `run.steps` only for `Need::Yield`; blocking Get/Pause outcomes resume and continue without accounting for the consumed steps.

## Trigger conditions
A blocking routine repeatedly reaches a Get or resumable Pause before any individual Machine invocation exhausts its slice.

## Realistic impact
The routine can exceed the advertised total blocking cap indefinitely while retaining the synchronous caller. UI invocation can threaten responsiveness. Normal nonblocking interactive waiting is not itself a defect.

## Recommended remediation
Charge actual transitions on every machine outcome and carry cumulative/remaining budgets across input resumptions.

## Suggested regression tests
With a deliberately small test cap, verify bounded termination of repeated blocking Get/Pause resumptions, ordinary computation and cancellation. Retain finite input success and nonblocking wait/resume controls; do not run production-scale runaway workloads.

## Related reports
Related #648 and closed #758 cover Lisp conformance/integration rather than this accounting defect.

title: fix(lisp): CLOSE reports success after discarding buffered output on filesystem errors
author: PierrunoYT
body:

- Baseline: upstream `main` at e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa.

[crates/engine/src/lisp/builtins.rs:934–941](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/lisp/builtins.rs#L934-L941) removes the file record, calls a nonfallible helper, and returns normal Nil. [crates/engine/src/lisp/builtins.rs:986–991](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/lisp/builtins.rs#L986-L991) silently ignores destination-open and write_all errors.

Native Lisp closes a buffered output stream when opening or writing the destination fails.

The routine gets no error, and its buffered output is discarded. Failure after opening with truncation can also leave incomplete output. Normal successful CLOSE returning nil is intentional, not the defect.

## Recommended remediation
Return I/O errors through LispError and define recoverable buffer behavior on failure. Consider safe staged replacement for nonappend writes.

## Suggested regression tests

[crates/engine/src/cmd/array/edit.rs:350–358](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/cmd/array/edit.rs#L350-L358) rejects counts below one. Validate the entire compound request before mutation, or stage its changes transactionally and restore on ordinary errors.

author: PierrunoYT

title: fix(dxf): unknown-entity round trips strip custom application 102 groups
author: PierrunoYT
body:

title: feat(io): Nextcloud integration — open and save drawings over WebDAV
author: filforce95
body:
## TL;DR
Let people open and save CADCraft drawings directly on their **Nextcloud** by entering the server URL, so a drawing lives in their cloud folder and syncs like any other file. Nextcloud is widely used in the open-source community; this would be a native, opt-in, vendor-neutral integration.

This is a Nextcloud-focused slice of the storage work in #540 (which proposes a generic `StorageBackend` with WebDAV among others). It should reuse that abstraction rather than compete with it.

## Today
- There is no network code in the workspace (no HTTP client, no WebDAV).
- Without any change, users can already save into a folder kept in sync by the Nextcloud desktop client (File ▸ Open / Save As). A direct integration adds: no desktop client needed, conflict detection, and web-build support.

## Proposal (staged)
**Stage 1 – synced-folder ergonomics (no network code):** a configurable default drawing folder, plus a warning when the file changed on disk since it was opened (typical Nextcloud conflict case).

**Stage 2 – native WebDAV (desktop):**
- WebDAV client against `<server>/remote.php/dav/files/<user>/` (PROPFIND, GET, PUT with `If-Match`, MKCOL, DELETE).
- Login via Nextcloud Login Flow v2 or an app password; credentials stored in the OS keychain, never in config files.
- Commands in `crates/engine/src/cmd/file/` (e.g. `cloudconnect`, `cloudopen`, `cloudsave`) with JSON params and no dialogs, so CLI, MCP and the control channel can use them; UI stays a thin dialog in `ui-egui`.
- Network/WebDAV logic in a layer at or below `io` (L3), with no egui/rfd dependency (`cargo xtask layers`).
- Autosave/recovery files must not land in the cloud folder.

**Stage 3 – web build:** depends on what browsers and CORS allow; must not break `cargo xtask wasm` (feature-gate the transport if needed).

- Never-crash: network responses are hostile input — timeouts, size caps, `Result` everywhere, regression tests against a mock WebDAV server.

title: HATCH Fails in Complex DWG Files – "Valid hatch boundary not found"
author: emrahoksak
body:
I've encountered an issue with the **HATCH** command when working with large or complex DWG files.

The HATCH command works correctly in a new, empty drawing. However, when I open an existing DWG file containing many objects, the command fails to detect valid hatch boundaries.

To test this, I created a completely new rectangle using CADCraft's own **RECTANGLE** command inside the existing drawing.

Despite the rectangle being closed and its layer being active, attempting to apply a hatch inside it results in the following error:

`Valid hatch boundary not found.`

The same operation works without any issues in a new, empty drawing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an existing large or complex DWG file containing many objects.
2. Create a new rectangle using CADCraft's RECTANGLE command.
3. Make sure the rectangle is closed and its layer is active.
4. Run the HATCH command.
5. Select a hatch pattern (such as SOLID or ANSI31).
6. Click inside the newly created rectangle.
7. The command fails with the message: `Valid hatch boundary not found.`

## Expected Behavior

The HATCH command should correctly detect closed boundaries and apply the selected hatch pattern, regardless of the size or complexity of the drawing.

A rectangle created directly within CADCraft should be recognized as a valid hatch boundary.

## Actual Behavior

- HATCH works correctly in a new, empty drawing.
- HATCH fails in existing drawings containing many objects.
- Even newly created rectangles are not recognized as valid boundaries.
- The command repeatedly displays `Valid hatch boundary not found.`
- Changing the hatch pattern does not resolve the issue.

## Additional Notes

The attached screenshot shows the issue occurring in a complex DWG file.

title: QSAVE Cannot Preserve REGION Objects in DWG Files – Potential Data Loss
author: emrahoksak
body:
I encountered an issue when trying to save a large and complex DWG file using the **QSAVE** command in CADCraft.

The drawing contains multiple REGION objects, and when attempting to save it, CADCraft displays the following message:

```text
Command: QSAVE
Not saved in the DWG file (its writer can't write these object types yet; DXF keeps them): 72 REGION
```

According to this message, the DWG writer does not currently support saving REGION objects, even though they can be preserved in DXF format.

This is a significant issue because it means that saving an existing DWG file may result in **data loss**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a large or complex DWG file containing REGION objects.
2. Run the `QSAVE` command.
3. Check the command-line output.
4. CADCraft reports that 72 REGION objects cannot be saved in DWG format.

## Expected Behavior

- All supported drawing objects should be preserved when saving a DWG file.
- REGION objects should not be silently omitted from the saved file.
- If certain object types are not supported, the application should clearly warn users before saving.
- Ideally, CADCraft should support reading and writing REGION objects without losing any geometry or drawing data.

## Actual Behavior

The application reports:

`Not saved in the DWG file (its writer can't write these object types yet; DXF keeps them): 72 REGION`

This indicates that 72 REGION objects are excluded from the DWG output.

## Why This Matters

This is particularly concerning when working with existing architectural, structural, or engineering drawings.

Users may open a DWG file, make minor modifications, and save it without realizing that certain objects will not be preserved.

**Potential data loss during saving is a critical issue for a CAD application.**

title: fix(dxf): hostile-input hardening in the DXF reader and writer (NaN reals, BOM/CR lines, mixed encodings, hex and integer groups)
author: vangel76
body:
Audit of `crates/dxf` (reader and writer) against hostile or merely unusual input. Findings, all in `crates/dxf/src/lib.rs` / `codepage.rs`:

1. **Binary reals are not finite-filtered.** `parse_binary` keeps NaN/inf as `Value::Real`, the ASCII reader maps them to 0.0.
2. **ASCII: UTF-8 BOM and CR-only line endings are rejected**; the up-front `TooLarge` tag count only counts `\n`, so a CR-only file bypasses the precheck.
3. **One invalid UTF-8 byte makes the whole ASCII file fall back to the code page**, and the binary path decides differently from the ASCII path for UTF-8 bytes in an ANSI_1252 file. Decode per line/string instead: valid UTF-8 first, otherwise the file's code page, for both readers.
4. **Trailing whitespace on code-0 / section-name values** breaks SECTION / ENDSEC / EOF detection.
5. **Integer groups accept `inf` / `1e30`** via the f64 fallback and become `i64::MAX`.
6. **Hex groups (310..319, 1004)** with odd length or non-hex characters are silently shifted or truncated; the ASCII reader does not validate them.
7. **ASCII writer writes `Value::Hex` raw**, so `Hex("AB\r\n0\r\nEOF")` injects tags; it also does not split long chunks at 254 hex digits like the DXF Reference.
8. **`write_binary` clamps 16/32-bit integers** instead of wrapping: `Tag::i(70, 65535)` becomes 32767.

Plan: one PR with a regression test per finding.

title: fix(fonts): paragraph direction looks inside bidi isolates; harakat block the Lam-Alef ligature
author: vangel76
body:
Two defects in `crates/fonts/src/bidi.rs`, found in a source review of the text engine (follow-up to #315). Both re-checked on current `main`.

## 1. `base_rtl` lets text inside a bidi isolate decide the paragraph direction

`base_rtl` (the paragraph direction from the first strong character, UBA rules P2/P3) takes the first L/R/AL character anywhere in the string. P2 says to skip characters between an isolate initiator (LRI, RLI, FSI) and its matching PDI, or to the end of the paragraph when there is no matching PDI.

Example: `"\u{2067}שלום\u{2069} abc"` (RLI, Hebrew, PDI, Latin) returns `Some(true)`. The first strong character outside the isolate is `a`, so it should be `Some(false)`. A line like this is laid out right to left when it should be left to right.

## 2. Harakat between Lam and Alef block the Lam-Alef ligature

`presentation_forms` only forms the ligature when the Alef is the very next code point after the Lam. Combining marks are transparent for joining (`joining_forms` already skips them), so `ل` + fatha (U+064E) + `ا` should still give the ligature (U+FEFB, or U+FEFC in final form). Today it prints a plain Lam form and a separate Alef form.

## Fix

- `base_rtl`: track isolate depth and only look at strong characters at depth 0. An unmatched initiator hides the rest of the string. A stray PDI is ignored.
- `presentation_forms`: after a Lam, look past marks for the Alef. Emit the ligature, then the skipped marks (same logical order, each keeping its source index), then continue after the Alef.

Tests go next to the existing ones in `bidi.rs`.

## Not in this issue

Word-by-word shaping base direction, and the other items from the review of `crates/fonts` (including everything in `mtext*`), are separate.

title: fix(fonts): MTEXT drops the rest of the text after an unterminated code; NaN oblique/line spacing and runaway relative heights
author: vangel76
body:
Found in a source review of `crates/fonts` (MTEXT parsing and layout). Three defects, all in `crates/fonts/src/mtext.rs` and `mtext/para.rs`.

## 1. An unterminated code drops the rest of the text

`plain_mtext`, `parse` and `Paragraphs::scan` treat every code they do not know as a code with an argument "up to `;`". `\U+hhhh` and `\M+nhhhh` (the escapes pre-R2007 files use for non-ASCII characters) and any other unknown code fall into that arm. When no `;` follows, the whole rest of the text is dropped:

```
A\U+00B0 B C;D   ->  "AD"      (expected "A° B C;D")
A\Zbc d          ->  ""  after "A"  (expected "Abc d")
```

Expected behaviour:
- `\U+hhhh` (four hex digits) is decoded; a surrogate pair `\U+D83D\U+DE00` becomes one character, a lone surrogate U+FFFD. `\M+nhhhh` is decoded like the DXF reader does. Same result in all three parsers.
- An unknown code without an argument loses only the backslash and the code character.
- Codes that take a `;`-terminated argument (`\H \W \T \Q \A \f \F \C \c \p \S`) keep their behaviour.

## 2. NaN oblique and line spacing

`layout_mtext_with` checks height, width factor, width and rotation for finiteness, but not `MTextParams::oblique` and `line_spacing`. A NaN oblique gives NaN coordinates; line spacing is not limited.

Expected: a non-finite oblique is 0, a non-finite or non-positive line spacing is 1.0, and line spacing is clamped to 0.25..=4 (AutoCAD's range).

## 3. Runaway relative heights

Relative `\H…x` factors multiply without a bound: sixty times `\H999999x;` gives a height of 1e360 = infinity and the glyphs disappear.

Expected: after each multiplication the height stays within 1e-3..1e3 times the MTEXT's own height. An absolute `\H` keeps its existing cap.

A fix with regression tests follows.

title: Scope question: should CADCraft read IFC (BIM), going beyond AutoCAD the way BricsCAD does?
author: STE1200
body:
Before anyone writes code, a scope question for the maintainers.

CADCraft targets AutoCAD 2027 parity. AutoCAD itself does not read IFC: Autodesk's BIM path is Revit, and IFC comes only with the Architecture toolset (IFC2x3 certified, IFC4 without a Reference View or Design Transfer View guarantee). BricsCAD took the other route: its BIM edition reads and writes IFC natively, next to DWG.

Many architecture and structural-steel offices hand in PDF, DWG *and* IFC, and they receive IFC models from other trades every week. Several issues ask for BIM authoring (#748, #897, #985), which goes far beyond this; reading IFC is the small part of it. Today CADCraft has no IFC path, so those users need a second program beside it. IFC is an open buildingSMART/ISO standard, so unlike RVT or DWG nothing has to be reverse-engineered.

**The question:** is it OK for CADCraft to follow BricsCAD BIM here rather than AutoCAD, and add IFC support beyond AutoCAD parity? Or would you rather keep CADCraft at AutoCAD scope and see IFC in a separate crate or repo?

If yes, this is the small first step we'd propose. It doesn't touch `Drawing` and adds no 3D:

1. A new L0 crate `crates/ifc`: an ISO 10303-21 (STEP) reader with caps for hostile input, and a hand-written subset of IFC2X3/IFC4/IFC4X3 (spatial structure, elements, property sets, quantities, units, materials, types). No geometry, no new dependencies, and it must build for wasm.
2. Commands `ifc.open`, `ifc.tree`, `ifc.query`, `ifc.element`, `ifc.quantities` and matching MCP tools. The IFC model sits beside the drawing; nothing is merged into it. An agent could then answer "which beams are on level 2, with which profiles and lengths" or check a drawing's door schedule against the model.
3. Later, as a separate PR: IMPORT an `.ifc` as a 2D reference (a section of each storey, one layer per storey and class).
4. Export waits for the 3D foundations and its own decision.

Licences: no IfcOpenShell (LGPL), Bonsai (GPL) or openbimrs (AGPL…

title: Agent interface: a contract agents can rely on (addressing, coordinates, errors, output size)
author: STE1200
body:
CADCraft's MCP server and control channel already give an agent a typed way into the drawing. We work with LLM agents on real office drawings in another CAD program through a COM/AutoLISP bridge, and most of the time lost there goes to the same few things: an agent addresses something that isn't there and gets no error, it can't tell what coordinate system or unit a value is in, it gets a free-text error it can't act on, or it gets a reply too large to read. CADCraft can get these right now, while the interface is young and before more tools build on it.

Proposed contract, each point small and separate:

- [ ] **1. Addressing is strict.** A handle that names nothing is an error that lists it, and nothing changes. #331 and #934/#970 reject malformed handles; a well-formed handle that names nothing is still silent: `move {handles: ["FFFFF"], …}` returns `{"moved": 0}`. (PR: #1043)
- [ ] **2. Coordinates say what they are.** Geometry is WCS. The DXF reader already maps mirrored objects (extrusion 0,0,−1, common in architectural drawings) to WCS since #277, but an agent can't see that an object was mirrored in the source file, nor which unit a drawing uses. The PR adds `extrusion` to entity output when it isn't (0,0,1) and a WCS `bbox`, has `inspect` report `insunits`, and documents the unit of every angle field in docs/mcp.md. (PR: #1040)
- [ ] **3. Output is sized for a context window.** Compact JSON plus `structuredContent`, and no full entity dump by default from `inspect_drawing` (about 72 KB of text, 81 KB on the wire, for the 58-entity `examples/apartment.dxf`); `query_entities` and `find_text` serve entities, paged as they already are. (PR: #1040)
- [ ] **4. Errors are data.** The engine already has a typed error (`EngineError`). At the MCP and control boundary it becomes free text. Return `{code, command, param, message}` alongside the text, so an agent can tell a bad parameter from a missing object from "not available yet". (PR: #1047; a separate `not_found` …

title: DWG: justified TEXT is saved with insertion point equal to alignment point, so AutoCAD draws it left-aligned
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.6.2 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.6.2`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy, never saving) — black-box observation only. All test drawings are synthetic and generated by CADCraft itself; no AutoCAD-produced file is attached.

_Commands below are bash (Linux/macOS, or Git Bash on Windows); in Windows PowerShell 5.1 the inner double quotes are stripped and the CLI answers "key must be a string". On this machine the MSI did not put `cadcraft-cli` on PATH._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'text {"at": [100, 50], "text": "MIDDLE CENTER", "height": 5, "justify": "MC"}' \
  --cmd 'text {"at": [100, 30], "text": "BOTTOM RIGHT", "height": 5, "justify": "BR"}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path": "case.dwg", "version": 2018}' --save case.dxf
```
Observe in AutoCAD: `entget` on each TEXT (groups 10 and 11) and `(textbox (entget e))` for the drawn extents; `REGENALL` does not change them.

## Expected
AutoCAD shows "MIDDLE CENTER" centred on (100,50) and "BOTTOM RIGHT" ending at (100,30), as CADCraft does.

## Actual (AutoCAD 2026)
| file | text | group 10 | group 11 | where AutoCAD draws it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| case.dwg | MIDDLE CENTER | 100,50 | 100,50 | x 100 to 161.7: starts at the centre point |
| case.dwg | BOTTOM RIGHT | 100,30 | 100,30 | x 100 to 156.7: starts at the right point |
| case.dxf | MIDDLE CENTER | 69.17,47.5 (recomputed by AutoCAD) | 100,50 | x 69.2 to 130.8, correct |

The DXF also has group 10 = group 11, but AutoCAD recomputes group 10 on DXF import; it does not do so when it reads a DWG. So every centred or right-aligned TEXT in a CADCraft DWG is displaced, and title-block texts spill out of their frames.

## Hint
In the writer, store the computed first alignment point (group 10 = where the text actually starts, from the font metrics) instead of copying group 11 (even an approximate value is far better than group 11).

title: DWG loses $DIMSTYLE, and neither DXF nor DWG writes the current style's DIM* header variables, so AutoCAD draws new or updated dimensions with 0.18 text and 4 decimals
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.6.2 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.6.2`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy, never saving) — black-box observation only. All test drawings are synthetic and generated by CADCraft itself; no AutoCAD-produced file is attached.

_Commands below are bash (Linux/macOS, or Git Bash on Windows); in Windows PowerShell 5.1 the inner double quotes are stripped and the CLI answers "key must be a string". On this machine the MSI did not put `cadcraft-cli` on PATH._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'dimstyle {"name": "S25", "current": true, "DIMSCALE": 25, "DIMTXT": 0.25}' \
  --cmd 'dimlinear {"p1": [0, 0], "p2": [100, 0], "at": [50, -20]}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path": "case.dwg", "version": 2018}' --save case.dxf
```
Observe in AutoCAD: `(getvar "DIMSTYLE")`, `(getvar "DIMTXT")`, `(getvar "DIMDEC")`; then draw a `DIMLINEAR` and run `-DIMSTYLE` Apply on the existing dimension.

## Expected
Opening either file, the current dimension style is S25 and new or updated dimensions use S25's values (text 0.25 × 25, 2 decimals as in S25).

## Actual
| | current style | DIMTXT / DIMDEC in effect | new DIMLINEAR / Apply on the "100" |
|---|---|---|---|
| case.dxf in AutoCAD | S25 | 0.18 / 4 (the header has only `$DIMSCALE` and `$DIMSTYLE`) | "20.0000" / "100.0000", text height 4.5 |
| case.dwg in AutoCAD | **Standard** | 0.18 / 4 | same result |
| case.dwg reopened in CADCraft | **Standard** (`getvar` returned S25 before `saveas`) | DIMTXT 0.18 | — |

The S25 style table entry itself has the right values in both files (DIMTXT 0.25, DIMSCALE 25, DIMDEC 2). The header DIM* variables are not written from the current style, so AutoCAD falls back to its defaults and applies them as overrides of S25; in the DWG, `$DIMSTYLE` is lost as well. Writing only `$DIMSTYLE` in the DWG would not remove the "100.0000".

title: DWG: the stored measurement of a rotated linear dimension is the aligned distance (210.0595 instead of 210)
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.6.2 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.6.2`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy, never saving) — black-box observation only. All test drawings are synthetic and generated by CADCraft itself; no AutoCAD-produced file is attached.

_Commands below are bash (Linux/macOS, or Git Bash on Windows); in Windows PowerShell 5.1 the inner double quotes are stripped and the CLI answers "key must be a string". On this machine the MSI did not put `cadcraft-cli` on PATH._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'dimlinear {"p1": [-5, 0], "p2": [0, 210], "at": [-40, 105], "rotation": 90}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path": "case.dwg", "version": 2018}' --save case.dxf
```
Observe in AutoCAD: `(cdr (assoc 42 (entget <dimension>)))` on case.dwg.

## Expected
Group 42 (actual measurement) is 210: the projection on the 90° direction, which is also what CADCraft displays.

## Actual
`42 = 210.0595` = sqrt(5² + 210²), i.e. the aligned distance. AutoCAD corrects it after a regen, but anything that reads the stored value before then (LISP, data extraction, other tools) gets the wrong number. In DXF the group is omitted, which is allowed: AutoCAD reads -1 and recomputes.

cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'dimstyle {"name": "S25", "current": true, "DIMSCALE": 25, "DIMTXT": 0.25, "DIMTAD": 1}' \
  --cmd 'dimlinear {"p1": [200, 0], "p2": [200, 40], "at": [230, 20], "rotation": 90, "text": "30 MIN.\\X50 MAX."}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path": "case.dwg", "version": 2018}' --save case.dxf
```
Observe in AutoCAD: list the MTEXT entities of the dimension's *D block before and after `-DIMSTYLE` Restore S25 + Apply.

## Expected
"30 MIN." above the dimension line and "50 MAX." below it, as AutoCAD draws it (`\X` = text below the dimension line, per the DXF reference).

## Actual
The dimension keeps the override string, but the *D block CADCraft writes contains only one MTEXT, "30 MIN.". "50 MAX." is drawn neither in CADCraft nor in its PDF. After AutoCAD regenerates the dimension, the DXF gets the two MTEXTs ("30 MIN." and "50 MAX.").

In case.dwg the dimension is written with flag 70 = 128 ("user-defined text position"; the DXF has 70 = 32); with that flag even AutoCAD's regen keeps "30 MIN.\P50 MAX." as one MTEXT. Clearing bit 128 gives the two lines. Probably worth its own issue (seen on the 2 DWG dimensions we checked).

title: LEADER annotation text height ignores DIMSCALE (0.25 instead of 6.25)
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.6.2 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.6.2`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy, never saving) — black-box observation only. All test drawings are synthetic and generated by CADCraft itself; no AutoCAD-produced file is attached.

_Commands below are bash (Linux/macOS, or Git Bash on Windows); in Windows PowerShell 5.1 the inner double quotes are stripped and the CLI answers "key must be a string". On this machine the MSI did not put `cadcraft-cli` on PATH._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'dimstyle {"name": "S25", "current": true, "DIMSCALE": 25, "DIMTXT": 0.25, "DIMASZ": 0.2}' \
  --cmd 'leader {"points": [[0, 0], [20, 20], [30, 20]], "text": "NOTE"}' \
  --cmd 'dimlinear {"p1": [0, -20], "p2": [100, -20], "at": [50, -40]}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path": "case.dwg", "version": 2018}' --save case.dxf
```
Observe in AutoCAD: group 40 of the MTEXT "NOTE".

## Expected
The leader's MTEXT height is DIMTXT × DIMSCALE = 6.25, the same text size as the dimension next to it. With the same DIMSCALE 25 / DIMTXT 0.25, AutoCAD's own LEADER command creates the annotation at 6.25.

## Actual
The MTEXT height is **0.25** in the DXF and in the DWG, so the note is 25 times smaller than the dimension texts. #313 made leader *arrows* honour DIMSCALE; the annotation text still does not.

title: Plot builds (PDF, PNG, Plot Preview) hold every display primitive in memory: 379 M primitives and more than 8 GB footprint on a 985k-entity drawing
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
The full-detail build used by PDF and PNG export keeps every display primitive of the drawing in memory before the output is written. Plot Preview showed the same growth in a capped run (8,399 MB, 20.9 s after the request). For the test drawing (985,250 entities) that build creates **379,020,060 primitives** and takes **175.7 s on one thread**. A PDF export started from the desktop app passed **8 GB of physical footprint** about 21 s after the request (8,560 MB at 20.7 s, when a guard stopped the process). Without a cap the same export reached **32 GB** after about 8.5 minutes. Most of the count is linetype dash expansion: every dash of every dashed line becomes a separate primitive, and the only limit is per entity, so the total grows with the number of dashed entities.

## Background
- The renderer (`crates/render`) turns a space into a `DisplayList` of primitives. `build` is used for the screen and honours a level-of-detail setting (`min_dash`) and a view hint (`view`). `build_plot` is used for output and turns both off (`min_dash: 0`, `view: None`).
- The PDF writer (`crates/io/src/pdf.rs`) builds each sheet with `build_plot` and writes it only after the list is complete.
- Dashed linetypes are expanded into geometry: one primitive per dash and per dot.

## Environment

|---|---|
| Repository | `storytold/cadcraft` |
| Commit under test | `e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa` (`main`, committed 2026-10-13 06:58:50 -0400) |
| Toolchain | rustc and cargo 1.95.0 |

title: Dashed lines longer than 50,000 pattern periods are drawn as a single solid line
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
When a polyline is longer than 50,000 times its linetype pattern length, the renderer stops expanding the dashes and draws the whole polyline as one continuous (solid) line. The code comment says the rule is for display "zoomed out a lot". Plot builds turn zoom-level detail off (`min_dash: 0`), so the rule also applies to plots at any zoom. In a controlled test, a line with 49,999 pattern periods prints dashed, and a line with 50,001 periods prints solid.

## Background
- A linetype such as `DASHED` is a repeating pattern of dash, gap and dot elements. The renderer expands a polyline into one primitive per dash and per dot.
- For on-screen drawing the renderer uses a level of detail: dashes shorter than about two screen pixels are drawn continuous. For plots and exports the level of detail is off.
- The 50,000-period rule is a guard against runaway expansion. It is evaluated per polyline.

title: Block contents stop being drawn after 2,000,000 expansion units per display list, with no warning
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
Every display-list build may expand at most `MAX_BLOCK_EXPANSION = 2,000,000` units of block content. Each block reference, each copy in an array, and each entity drawn inside a block counts one unit. When the budget is spent, the builder stops drawing block contents, silently: the screen build, the plot build and the PNG export all omit them, and no message is shown. In a controlled test with 3,000 references of a 1,000-line block, only 1,997,999 of the 3,000,000 expected primitives are drawn. For the test drawing, the same counting rule gives about 17.5 million units, roughly 8.8 times the budget.

## Background
- A block reference (`INSERT`) draws the entities of a block definition at a position, rotation and scale. Arrays (`MINSERT`) draw several copies.
- The builder (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`) expands references into the display list. The expansion budget exists to stop nested or arrayed references from expanding without bound (see the doc comment at the constant). Its counting is per build.
- Other limits in the same builder, such as the depth limit for nested blocks, are documented next to the constant.

title: Zoom and pan rebuild the display list for the whole drawing; nothing is culled to the visible area
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
The on-screen display list does not depend on the view, except for hatch patterns. For the test drawing, the list holds about 4.44 million primitives at every zoom level from 1× to 256×, so zooming in does not make it smaller. In the desktop app, each zoom or pan step is followed by a background rebuild of 1.0–3.4 s on the test drawing. At deep zoom, dashed linetypes are expanded for every dashed entity in the drawing, not only for the visible ones.

## Background
- The canvas keeps one display list for the visible space. It rebuilds when the drawing changes, when the zoom changes by more than a factor of two (the level-of-detail band), or when the view leaves the area the list was built for.
- A rebuild runs on a worker thread while the previous list is drawn with a view transform. The new list replaces it when ready.
- The renderer's `view` option only limits hatch-pattern generation. Every other entity is emitted for the whole space.
- The GPU canvas draws the whole list; its only clip is the window's scissor rectangle.

title: Each edit (colour, layer, move, copy, undo, redo) rebuilds the whole display list: 1 to 5 s per edit on a 985k-entity drawing
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
After an edit to a selection of about 60,000 entities in the test drawing, the desktop app acknowledges the command in 0.1–0.8 s, but the canvas then waits 1.2–5.3 s for a full display-list rebuild. The rebuild covers the whole drawing, not only the edited entities. Changing only the colour or the layer, which does not move geometry, pays the same cost as a geometry change. Undo and redo follow the same pattern.

## Background
- Each command changes the drawing's revision. The canvas rebuilds its display list when the revision changes, and a rebuild converts every entity in the space to primitives. The list is not culled to the view, so its size is the same at every zoom level (about 4.44 million primitives for the test drawing).
- The rebuild notes state that edits rebuild at once, so that a change is never drawn late ("Edits still rebuild at once, so a change is never drawn late"). The window therefore shows the new state once the rebuild has finished.
- The selection and property commands are reachable through the control channel with `engine.execute`.

title: Select All on a large drawing takes about 19 s to settle and clearing takes about 10 s: the Properties palette does per-frame work that grows with the selection
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
In the test drawing, selecting everything (905,000 entities) settles after about 19 s, and clearing that selection blocks the control channel for about 10 s. A stack sample during the operation puts most main-thread time in the Properties palette, which looks up every selected entity on each frame while the palette is shown. The per-frame cost therefore grows with the size of the selection, not with the size of the change.

## Background
- The desktop app shows a Properties palette for the current selection, and a quick-properties panel for the same selection. Both compute summaries over the selected entities (colour, layer and so on, shown as `*VARIES*` when entities differ).
- A selection is a list of entity handles held by the session. The palette is redrawn on every frame.
- The control channel's `ui.inspect` reply includes the full selection list (as hexadecimal handles), so polling it while a huge selection exists is itself expensive.

title: Zoom Extents and Zoom All recompute every entity's bounds on the UI thread on each call (about 2.5 to 3 s on the test drawing; splines are tessellated every time)
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
`zoom extents` and `zoom all` compute the bounds of the whole drawing from scratch on every call, on the UI thread, with no cache. On the test drawing a call takes 2.5–3.0 s. A stack sample attributes most of the time to the bounds of spline entities, which are tessellated just to find their extent, every time.

## Background
- The extents of a space is the axis-aligned box that contains all its visible entities. Zoom extents fits the view to it.
- Entity bounds are computed by `entity_bounds`, which also descends into block references. Other features (such as the spatial index used for picking) compute entity bounds too.
- The UI thread is the thread that answers control requests and draws the window, so any long call on it freezes both.

title: Opening a file through the engine command (app.open or engine.execute open) blocks the UI thread for the whole read: 20 s on the test drawing
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
The desktop app has two ways to open a file. Opening from the window (menu, drag and drop, command-line argument, recent files, picker) reads the file on a worker thread, and the window keeps answering. The engine's `open` command with a `path` argument, which the control channel exposes as `app.open` and `engine.execute open`, reads and decodes the file on the calling thread. Through the control channel that thread is the UI thread, so the window stops answering for the whole read. On the test drawing the control call took 20.3 s and the control channel did not answer pings for 19.8 s.

## Background
- The control channel answers requests from the UI thread. A request that starts a long operation on that thread blocks every other request and the window's redraws until it finishes.
- The window-level open was moved to a background thread so that large files do not freeze the window (the code comments refer to a tracking item for this change).
- Automation tools (scripts, the MCP server, the control channel) call the engine command directly and receive its reply only after the work is done.

title: Opening the 47.8 MB test DWG takes 16 to 28 s and peaks at 4.5 GB resident memory: the whole DWG-to-DXF conversion is held as text before parsing
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
Opening the 47.8 MB test DWG takes 16–28 s and peaks at 4.54 GB of resident memory (5.08 GB peak footprint) on the reference machine. The DWG is first converted to DXF text, the whole text (276,378,677 bytes, 5.78 times the DWG size) is held in one in-memory buffer, and only then is it parsed into the drawing model. The whole input file is also read into memory first.

## Background
- DWG files are read by an external crate (`acadrust`) and converted to DXF bytes; CADCraft's own DXF reader then builds the drawing. The bridge module describes this design: [`crates/dwg/src/lib.rs` L1–L6](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/dwg/src/lib.rs#L1-L6).
- The bridge limits the input file to 512 MB of DWG and the DXF text to 1 GiB: [`crates/dwg/src/lib.rs` L24–L39](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/dwg/src/lib.rs#L24-L39). The comment in that block says the DXF text is "about 6x" the DWG size.
- The top-level read function sends DWG input through the bridge and then to the DXF reader: [`crates/io/src/lib.rs` L62–L68](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/io/src/lib.rs#L62-L68).

title: Saving the 985k-entity test drawing as DXF takes 46 to 56 s; most of the time is hash-map construction inside dxf_raw::finish
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
Saving the test drawing as DXF takes 46–56 s in a fresh session (about 3 minutes in a session that had already run other operations). Stack samples taken during a save put most main-thread time under the DXF writer's finishing step, `dxf_raw::finish`, in hash-map inserts and table rehashing. The finishing step builds several whole-drawing hash maps before it checks whether there is any foreign data to preserve, so the cost is paid even when there is nothing to preserve.

## Background
- The DXF writer serialises the drawing model into tagged records. It also keeps data that CADCraft does not model (foreign records, extended data) so that a round trip does not lose it. That preservation happens in `finish`, after the main records are written.
- The finishing step first builds two whole-drawing maps (unknown entity handles and extended data for every entity), and only then returns early when there is nothing to preserve.
- Saves go through the engine's save path, which builds the complete output in memory and then writes it atomically.

title: Save As (DWG and DXF) and PDF export run on the UI thread: the window stops answering for 46 to 58 s per save, and queued control requests time out or are cancelled
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
Saving a drawing to DWG or DXF, and exporting it to PDF, run on the UI thread that also answers the control channel and draws the window. For the test drawing the window does not answer for the whole operation: 46–58 s per DWG or DXF save, and more than 8 minutes for a PDF export that had to be stopped. Requests sent during the operation wait behind it, time out after 60 s, or are cancelled before they start (state `not-run`).

## Background
- The control channel's requests are handled inside the UI update loop (`CadApp::logic` calls the control handler). A request that does long work blocks that loop, and with it the window's redraws.
- The engine's save builds the complete output in memory and then writes it through a temporary file that is renamed on success, so a failed save does not leave a partial file.
- Autosave in the same code base already writes on a worker thread, which shows the pattern is available.

title: drawing.inspect recomputes the whole drawing's extents on every call: about 2.5 s per call on a 985k-entity drawing, versus 11 to 33 ms for ui.inspect
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary
The control channel's `drawing.inspect` call (also exposed through the MCP server) reports entity counts, extents and the selection. Its implementation computes the drawing's extents by walking every entity, on the UI thread, on every call. On the test drawing each call takes about 2.5 s, and the window does not answer during that time. `ui.inspect`, the other diagnostic call, takes 11–33 ms on the same drawing.

## Background
- Automation clients and agents use `drawing.inspect` to read counts and state, often in a loop while they wait for an operation.
- The extents are not stored with the drawing; they are computed when asked for. The zoom commands use the same extents computation.
- `ui.inspect` reports the window state and the session summary, and does not compute extents.

title: A first pick or window selection on a large drawing builds the spatial index on the UI thread: about 2.6 s on the 985k-entity test drawing
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

On the test drawing (985,250 entities), the first query that needs the spatial index blocks the desktop app's UI thread for about 2.6 s while the index is built. Such a query is a point pick, a window or crossing selection, or an object-snap test. Once built, the index is cached, and later window selections take about 0.23–0.25 s. The build cost therefore lands on whichever action comes first. In the observed runs, the build also appeared during pointer movement over the canvas, as described in Limitations.

## Background

- The engine keeps an R-tree over the bounds of every entity in a space ([`crates/engine/src/spatial.rs` L1–L2](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/spatial.rs#L1-L2)). Point picking, window, crossing, fence and polygon selection, object snapping and snap tracking all query it. The module documentation states that indexed and brute-force results are identical ([L12–L13](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/spatial.rs#L12-L13)), and the parity tests check that ([L371–L427](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/spatial.rs#L371-L427)).
- An index is built on demand the first time a space with at least 256 entities is queried (`MIN_INDEXED`, [L24](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/spatial.rs#L24)). Four built indexes are kept (`CACHE_SIZE`, [L26](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/engine/src/spatial.rs#L26)).
- A build measures the bounds of every entity in the space.
- Control-channel requests such as `engine.execute` are run from the app's frame loop, which is the UI thread ([`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` L564](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/e707ab4d7cc10102e550ad4c5bcecef1084a9baa/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L564), […

title: DWG: dimensions are written with bit 128 of group 70 ("user-defined text position") and without bit 32, so AutoCAD leaves the text behind when the dimension changes
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.6.2 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.6.2`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy, never saving) — black-box observation only. The test drawing is synthetic and generated by CADCraft itself; no AutoCAD-produced file is attached.

_Commands below are bash (Linux/macOS, or Git Bash on Windows)._

Follow-up suggested in #1084 (side note from #1055). For context, #389 made CADCraft write a user text position as group 11 with flag 128; the DXF writer only sets it when the text was really placed by hand, but the DWG files have it on every dimension.

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'dimlinear {"p1": [0, 0], "p2": [100, 0], "at": [50, -20]}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path": "case.dwg", "version": 2018}' --save case.dxf

A real `STRETCH` of the point (100,0) by (100,0) gives the same result.

Group 70 without bit 128 (the DXF writes 32). When the dimension grows to 200, the text recentres at x = 100.

title: Add Alternate Construction Modes for Rectangle, Circle, and Other Shape Tools
author: SolarTara
body:
It would be useful if the basic shape tools supported multiple construction modes instead of using one fixed starting point for every shape.

For example, the **Rectangle tool** currently treats the first selected point as a corner. An alternate **Center Rectangle** mode would let the first point define the center, then build the rectangle outward from that point. This is useful for symmetrical layouts and for geometry that needs to stay centered on an origin, guide, or existing object.

The **Circle** tool could use the same general system. Instead of only using a center point and radius, it could support alternate construction methods such as:

**_Circle_**:
- Center + Radius
- Center + Diameter
- 2-Point Diameter
- 3-Point Circle


**_Rectangle_**: 
- Corner
- Center


For reference, these types of alternate construction methods are common in other CAD software. Autodesk Fusion supports separate 2-Point, 3-Point, and Center Rectangle tools, while AutoCAD supports several different circle construction methods.

Ideally, CADCraft could use a consistent way to switch between these modes while a drawing tool is active, such as a modifier key, shortcut, or mode control in the tool options.

This would make it much easier to build geometry from existing snap points, corners, intersections, origins, and symmetrical reference points without needing extra construction geometry or manual calculations.
