title: Saving a drawing with an AutoCAD arc-length dimension (ARC_DIMENSION) drops its *D block, and AutoCAD refuses the file
author: EP995LAB
body:
CADCraft keeps the ARC_DIMENSION entity as it is, as an unknown entity (#528/#545), and the entity still names its anonymous block (group 2, e.g. `*D1`). On save, though, the `*D` blocks that look unused are removed (#495/#508), and the unknown entity is not counted as a user: the block goes and the reference stays.

In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with a test drawing: a drawing made in AutoCAD with an arc-length dimension, opened in CADCraft (DWG 2018 or DXF 2018) and saved as DXF with no edits, is refused as a whole. AutoCAD stops while reading the ARC_DIMENSION, saying the dimension's block name is not valid, and loads nothing.

To reproduce without AutoCAD files, with a DXF written by hand from the DXF Reference:
```
printf '%s\n' 0 SECTION 2 BLOCKS 0 BLOCK 8 0 2 '*D1' 70 1 10 0 20 0 30 0 3 '*D1' 0 LINE 8 0 10 320 20 150 11 330 21 175 0 ENDBLK 0 ENDSEC 0 SECTION 2 ENTITIES 0 ARC 8 0 10 300 20 150 40 20 50 0 51 90 0 ARC_DIMENSION 5 41 100 AcDbEntity 8 0 100 AcDbDimension 2 '*D1' 10 333.8 20 169.5 11 327.6 21 177.6 70 5 42 31.4159 100 AcDbArcDimension 13 320 23 150 14 300 24 170 15 300 25 150 40 0 41 1.5708 0 ENDSEC 0 EOF > arcdim.dxf
cadcraft-cli convert arcdim.dxf out.dxf
```
`arcdim.dxf` defines the block `*D1`. In `out.dxf` the only blocks are `*Model_Space` and `*Paper_Space`, while the ARC_DIMENSION still names `*D1`.

A possible fix: when the `*D` blocks are cleaned up, also count as used the block names (group 2) of the unknown entities that are kept.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: ACAD_TABLE saved as DXF 2007 or later: the cells are empty in AutoCAD
author: EP995LAB
body:
A 2×2 table made with
`table {"at":[0,0],"rows":2,"cols":2,"cells":[["a","b"],["c","d"]],"title":"T","header":["H1","H2"]}`
and saved as DXF 2007, 2013 or 2018 (2018 is the default) reaches AutoCAD with all its cells empty.

In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same test drawing: with the DXF 2007, 2013 and 2018 files the table is there, but its 8 cells have empty text, and AutoCAD rebuilds the table's block with lines only. With DXF 2004 and with DWG 2018 the cells have their text (T, H1, H2, a, b, c, d). AUDIT reports 0 errors, so nobody is warned.

The content is right; it is the DXF 2007+ encoding that AutoCAD doesn't read. On the CADCraft side: comparing the ACAD_TABLE entity of `saveas {"path":"t2004.dxf","version":2004}` and of `saveas {"path":"t2018.dxf","version":2018}`, the two are identical, with the cell text only in group 1 as before 2007. Perhaps from 2007 on the text also has to be written in the cell-value structure the DXF Reference describes for those versions.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: Plotting a layout ignores the scale saved in its page setup
author: EP995LAB
body:
When a layout is plotted without a scale in the command, the scale saved in its page setup is not used, and the plot is made at scale 1. With a page scale of 0.1 almost all of the drawing falls off the sheet.

To reproduce:
```
cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'layout.new {"name":"Tavola","viewport":false}' --cmd 'layout.set {"name":"Tavola"}' --cmd 'pagesetup {"layout":"Tavola","device":"CADCraft PDF","paper":"A3","landscape":true,"scale":0.1,"margins":[0,0,0,0]}' --cmd 'rectang {"p1":[100,100],"p2":[4100,2870]}' --cmd 'plot {"path":"a.pdf","layout":"Tavola"}'
```
- Expected: a rectangle from 10 to 410 mm on an A3 sheet (420×297 mm).
- Got: from 100 to 4100 mm (scale 1).
- With `"scale":0.1` also written in the `plot`: from 10 to 410 mm, right.

In the code `run_plot` passes to `plot_scale` only the command's scale. #490/#598 fixed the scale written in the command, not the one saved in the page setup. The paper units of layouts (drawings with MEASUREMENT 0) are already in #1058/#1085, and the page setup's window and extents in #1157.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: TRIM replaces the line, and its associated dimension keeps the old measurement
author: EP995LAB
body:
Trimming a line that has an associated dimension, the dimension loses the association and keeps showing the old length.
```
cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'line {"points":[[0,0],[100,0]]}' --cmd 'line {"points":[[60,-10],[60,10]]}' --cmd 'dimlinear {"object":"100","at":[50,-20]}' --cmd 'trim {"handle":"100","pick":[90,0],"edges":["101"]}' --cmd 'entities {"type":"Dimension"}' --cmd 'entities {"type":"Line"}'
```
After the trim the line runs from 0,0 to 60,0, but it is a new object (handle 103). The dimension still has `p14` at 100,0 and no longer has `assoc`.

With `lengthen {"handle":"100","pick":[90,0],"total":80}` instead of `trim`, the dimension follows: `p14` goes to 80,0 and `assoc` stays.

TRIM replaces the object with new pieces (`trimextend.rs`). When only one piece is left, keeping the same object (same handle) would keep associated dimensions, associative hatches, xdata and links. When there are two pieces, perhaps at least the first could keep the handle.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: AutoLISP: `entget` returns angles in degrees instead of radians
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
ARC C 0,0 10,0 0,10
(princ (list (cdr (assoc 50 (entget (entlast)))) (cdr (assoc 51 (entget (entlast))))))
```
CADCraft prints `(0.0 90.0)`. In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same arc, the result is 50 = 0 and 51 = 1.5708: in `entget` lists angles are in radians, even though the DXF file stores them in degrees. The same happens with the line angle of a hatch: an ANSI31 at angle 0 (`CIRCLE 0,0 10`, `-HATCH P ANSI31`, internal point 0,0) gives 53 = 45.0; in AutoCAD the same ANSI31 at angle 0 gives 53 = 0.785398. In CADCraft a TEXT rotated 30° also gives 50 = 30.0.

docs/autolisp.md says `entget` returns the groups as they are in the DXF. Angles would need a conversion, when reading (`entget`) and when writing (`entmake`/`entmod`). I haven't tested the writing direction.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: Arc-length dimensions: the ARC_DIMENSION entity is neither read nor written (not shown when read; AutoCAD shows the chord when written)
author: EP995LAB
body:
In DXF, arc-length dimensions are a separate entity, `ARC_DIMENSION` (subclass `AcDbArcDimension`), not a DIMENSION. CADCraft already has its own arc-length dimensions (#100/#140), but doesn't use this entity:

1. **When reading** it keeps it as an unknown entity: it is not drawn, `entities` shows it only as raw tags, and it can't be edited. With the test DXF of #1161 (an ARC plus an ARC_DIMENSION), `cadcraft-cli info arcdim.dxf` gives `Arc: 1, Proxy: 1` and `convert arcdim.dxf a.png` shows only the arc. In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box, a drawing made there with 6 ordinary dimensions and 1 arc-length dimension is read by CADCraft with the 6 dimensions right and without the arc-length one (31.4159 on an arc of radius 20 and 90°).
2. **When writing**, CADCraft's arc-length dimension becomes an aligned dimension:
   ```
   cadcraft-cli run --metric --script "ARC C 300,150 320,150 300,170\n" --cmd 'dimarc {"handle":"100","at":[330,175]}' --save dimarc.dxf
   ```
   The file has a `DIMENSION` with `AcDbAlignedDimension`, 70 = 33 and 42 = 31.4159, plus the centre in the `CADCRAFT` / `ARCLEN` xdata. In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box, the same dimension just inserted is an aligned dimension between the arc's ends and shows 28.28 (the chord) instead of 31.42.

Reading and writing `ARC_DIMENSION` as in the DXF Reference (13/14 extension line points, 15 arc centre, 40/41 angles) would solve both directions.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: HATCH with an internal point: an outer boundary made of arcs or a circle is saved as straight segments
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
CIRCLE 50,50 40
-HATCH P SOLID
50,50

(princ (cdr (assoc 93 (entget (entlast)))))
AREA O 50,50
```
The hatch boundary has 158 straight edges and `AREA` gives 5025.2235 instead of 5026.5482 (π·40²). With a 100×50 rectangle that has a semicircular side (`PLINE 0,0 100,0 A 100,50 L 0,50 C`, internal point 50,25) the boundary has 63 edges and the area is 5981.2992, while the polyline measures 5981.7477.

In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same circle, the boundary stays exact: 2 vertices with bulge 1. In CADCraft the same circle used as an island, or a hatch made by selecting the object, stays exact. It looks as if `loops_at` (`cmd/hatch.rs`) keeps the flattened version as the outer boundary instead of the bulge vertices of the source objects.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: AREA, Object on an open polyline: the perimeter includes the closing side
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
PLINE 0,0 100,0 100,60

AREA O 50,0
```
CADCraft prints `Area = 3000.0000, Perimeter = 276.6190`. The polyline is 160 long: 276.619 is its length plus the closing side between 100,60 and 0,0. In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same polyline, the area is 3000 (computed as if closed) and the perimeter 160, that is the object's length alone.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: MIRROR and text: a TEXT doesn't take the mirrored extent, MTEXT comes out upside down, MIRRTEXT 1 has no effect
author: EP995LAB
body:
Three behaviours, all in `transform_text` (`doc/src/entity.rs`):

1. **MIRRTEXT 0, left-justified TEXT.** `TEXT 10,10 5 0 ABC`, then `MIRROR L` about the axis x = 0, keeping the source. The copy stays readable (right), but its insertion point is −10,10: the text starts at −10 and runs to the right, back towards the axis. In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same text, the copy's insertion point is at −24.0757, that is −(10 + width): it takes the mirrored extent.
2. **MTEXT.** `mtext {"at":[10,30],"text":"MTEXT","height":5,"width":50}` mirrored about x = 0 comes out with `rotation` 180, upside down, with both MIRRTEXT 0 and MIRRTEXT 1. A TEXT mirrored in the same command stays readable (rotation 0). It looks as if the MText branch adds the matrix rotation even when the matrix is a mirror.
3. **MIRRTEXT 1.** The same TEXT as in point 1 with `MIRRTEXT 1` comes out readable, as with 0: `(assoc 71 (entget (entlast)))` gives nil. In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box, the copy has 71 = 2 (backwards). The variable is saved and read back (#349), but MIRROR doesn't read it. It also depends on the per-text group 71 field, which comes with #1136.

To reproduce points 2 and 3:
```
cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'setvar {"name":"MIRRTEXT","value":1}' --cmd 'text {"at":[10,10],"text":"TEXT","height":5}' --cmd 'mtext {"at":[10,30],"text":"MTEXT","height":5,"width":50}' --cmd 'mirror {"handles":["100","101"],"p1":[0,0],"p2":[0,100]}' --cmd 'texts {}'
```

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: DIMRADIUS and DIMDIAMETER: a point outside the circle doesn't move the text
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
CIRCLE 50,50 25
DIMRADIUS 75,50 100,80
(princ (cdr (assoc 11 (entget (entlast)))))
```
The text midpoint (11) goes to (72.5934 63.1402), just outside the circle, instead of 100,80, the point given. The same happens with DIMDIAMETER (circle 300,50 radius 25, `DIMDIAMETER 325,50 350,80`: 11 = 322.593, 63.1402) and with the radius of an arc. The measurement is right.

In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same circle, the text point is exactly 100,80, and flag 70 has bit 128 (user-positioned text): 164 for the radius, 163 for the diameter. #385/#389 fixed the position inside the circle; this is the case of a point outside.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: New metric drawing: the Standard multileader and table styles still have 0.18 text
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'mleaderstyle {}' --cmd 'tablestyle {}' --cmd 'getvar {"name":"DIMTXT"}' --cmd 'getvar {"name":"TEXTSIZE"}'
```
DIMTXT and TEXTSIZE are 2.5, but the Standard styles give `textHeight: 0.18` (multileader and table), `arrowSize: 0.18` and `dogleg: 0.36`, the inch values. In a millimetre drawing a new multileader or table therefore has almost invisible text. Perhaps the metric values of these two styles should match those of the dimensions. For tables read from AutoCAD the same value was already fixed with #802/#806.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: Select objects rejects keywords with a leading underscore (`_L`, `_ALL`, `_P`, `_W`…)
author: EP995LAB
body:
Since #855 keywords with a leading underscore work at command prompts, but not at "Select objects".
```
LINE 0,0 100,0

MOVE _L  0,0 0,5
```
`_L` gives "*Invalid selection*", the Enter ends MOVE with no objects and `0,0` becomes "unknown command". With `ERASE _ALL` the line stays. Without the underscore (`MOVE L`) the line goes to y = 5. The same happens with `_P`, `_F`, `_CP` and `_WP`. With `_W`, `_C` and `_BOX` the selection only works by chance, because the two points that follow make an implicit window.

In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box, `MOVE _L` moves the line to y = 5. Scripts and routines meant for every language write exactly `_L`, `_ALL`, `_W`.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: BREAK on a closed polyline: "Cannot break that object."
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
PLINE 0,0 100,0 100,60 0,60 C
BREAK 50,0 100,30
```
CADCraft refuses and the polyline stays closed. In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same polyline, the stretch between the two points is removed and an open polyline of 5 vertices remains: 100,30 → 100,60 → 0,60 → 0,0 → 50,0. On open polylines BREAK already works in CADCraft, and docs/geometry-parity.md lists BREAK as supported on "polyline".

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: JOIN: collinear lines and arcs of the same circle with a gap between them are refused
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
LINE 0,0 50,0

LINE 120,0 150,0

JOIN 25,0 130,0

```
CADCraft answers "Objects are not connected." and two lines remain. The same happens with two arcs of the same circle (`ARC C 50,50 80,50 50,80` and `ARC C 50,50 20,50 50,20`, then `JOIN 80,50 20,50`).

In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same objects, the lines become one LINE from 0,0 to 150,0 and the arcs one ARC from 0 to 4.71239 rad (270°). For elliptical arcs CADCraft already closes the gaps (docs/geometry-parity.md).

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: JOIN with a single arc: the cLose option is missing
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
ARC C 50,50 80,50 50,80
JOIN 80,50

```
CADCraft answers "Select at least two objects to join.". In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box, with the same arc selected the Close keyword (`JOIN`, the arc, `_L`) turns it into a CIRCLE with centre 50,50 and radius 30. In CADCraft, `L` at that point means "last object", and then the same refusal comes. For ellipses something similar already exists ("the full ellipse").

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: A wide polyline is picked only on its centre line, not on the edges of the band
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
PLINE 0,0 W 10 10 50,0 50,50

ERASE 25,5

(princ (sslength (ssget "X")))
```
The click at 25,5, on the edge of the band, picks nothing (1 object remains). With `ERASE 25,0`, on the centre line, the polyline is picked.

In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same wide polyline, it is picked on the edges of the band (all along y = 5 and y = −5 of the first segment, x = 45 and x = 55 of the second, and on both ends), on the joint between the segments and on the diagonal of each segment, not inside the band. It is the same with the polyline inside a block.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: With a table in the drawing every save changes the handles and $HANDSEED grows by 0x1057
author: EP995LAB
body:
#495/#508 make CADCraft's files keep their handles from one save to the next. With an ACAD_TABLE in the drawing, though, every open and save renumbers the table records, the objects and the block contents.
```
cadcraft-cli run --cmd 'table {"at":[0,0],"rows":2,"cols":2}' --save t0.dxf
cadcraft-cli convert t0.dxf t1.dxf
cadcraft-cli convert t1.dxf t2.dxf
cadcraft-cli convert t2.dxf t3.dxf
```
`$HANDSEED`: 115B → 21B2 → 3209 → 4260. Handle of layer "0": 113D → 2194 → 31EB → 4242. The objects and their data don't change. With a single line instead of the table, `$HANDSEED` stays 1152 every round.

A guess: the table's anonymous `*T` block is rebuilt on read, its new entities raise the seed above the saved one, and the structural handles move with it.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: FILLET (and CHAMFER) swap the start and end of the second line
author: EP995LAB
body:
```
LINE 0,0 100,0

LINE 120,20 120,100

FILLET R 10 50,0 120,60
(princ (list (cdr (assoc 10 (entget (handent "101")))) (cdr (assoc 11 (entget (handent "101"))))))
```
The second line comes out with 10 = (120,100) and 11 = (120,10). In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box with the same lines, it comes out with 10 = (120,10) and 11 = (120,100): only the end near the corner moves and the direction stays as it was. The shape and the arc are the same in both programs. In CADCraft `CHAMFER D 10 10 50,0 120,60` swaps the second line the same way (not compared in AutoCAD).

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: Fit-point splines from AutoCAD DWGs: CADCraft rebuilds a different curve
author: EP995LAB
body:
In AutoCAD 2027 for Mac, observed black-box: a SPLINE drawn through the points 0,100 / 30,130 / 60,90 / 100,120 (chord knots), saved as DXF 2018 and DWG 2018. CADCraft reads the DXF exactly as AutoCAD has it (6 control points, knots 0,0,0,0,42.43,92.43,142.43×4). From the DWG, instead, it rebuilds 4 control points with knots 0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1: the curve still passes through the four points, but between them it has a different shape, and `fit_opts.knots` still says Chord.

In the DWG such a spline has only its fit points, so the control net has to be computed on read. It looks as if the DWG path rebuilds it differently from CADCraft's own SPLINE command, which with the same points gives the same knots as AutoCAD. I can't attach the DWG (clean-room). One way to see it: draw a fit-point spline in AutoCAD and compare `entities` of the DWG and of the DXF that AutoCAD saves from the same drawing.

_(Tested and written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: Proposal: named materials for HATCH, and an automatic legend
author: EP995LAB
body:
People who draw building and services sections use the same materials over and over (earth, concrete, reinforced concrete, masonry, insulation, wood, steel, gravel).

Would it make sense to have:
- a named material = pattern + scale + angle + colour/lineweight, in an editable file, starting from CADCraft's 23 original patterns;
- picking it by name in the Hatch dialog;
- a command that puts a legend of the materials used into the drawing (box + name)?

Only original definitions, no patterns copied from other programs.

title: Proposal: a "Calibrate scale" command with a clear name
author: EP995LAB

For surveys from a PDF or a scan you need to say "this distance is X long". Today this is done with SCALE → Reference and it works well (tested: a segment of 5 brought to 1250 gives 1250.0000). A command with a clear name would be easier to find: two points, the true length, then "apply to: everything / selection / underlay PDF". title: Proposal: choose the drawing's template (and its units) on the start page, with a visible default
author: EP995LAB
body:
Today "New" and Cmd+N create a drawing in inches (MEASUREMENT 0, DIMTXT 0.18), and "New (metric)" is only on the start page. A drawing born in inches then plots in inches (see #1163).

Units are a property of the drawing, so the place to choose them is when the drawing is made, from a template (reworked with @grandixximo's suggestions below):

- The application opens on the start page. It shows the default template and starts a drawing from it in one click, or lets you pick another one (at least metric and imperial).
- The default template is visible on the start page and easy to change there. Picking a different template for one drawing does not change the default.
- "New" and Cmd+N use the default template.
- Skipping the start page ("start in a new drawing") is an option you switch on deliberately in the settings, not a one-time pop-up.
- Later: a simple template manager on the start page.

Paper size and plotter stay in the layout and the plot, because a drawing may never be plotted or may have several sheets.

_(Written by Claude Code, an AI agent, on behalf of @EP995LAB.)_

title: Proposal: "new layout from template" and a form to fill in the title block
author: EP995LAB
body:
Today there are layouts, page setups, PUBLISH, `.dwt` templates for a new drawing (#552) and attributes that can be edited globally too. Two pieces could make preparing sheets much faster:
- "New layout from template": paper size, viewport and title block taken from a `.dwt`;
- a small "Fill in title block" form that lists the title block's attributes (title, date, scale, revision) and writes them into every sheet.

title: Proposal: data-driven tables, reports and connectors — automation of drawing documentation
author: asimfali
body:
## Who and why

I write AutoCAD add-ins for electrical documentation: wire lists, terminal tables, bills of materials that go to an ERP system. In AutoCAD every one of these needs custom .NET code. My add-in builds a table as a stack of row blocks, picks each row's visibility state by rules from XML files, reads wire lengths from XRECORDs and maps parts to ERP codes through lookup tables. Every company that does this writes the same code again, and it breaks with each AutoCAD release.

CADCraft can make this a built-in feature, and it fits its stated goal of going beyond parity: speed, openness and agent control. Every behaviour is already a command with a JSON form, so a table that is fed from the drawing becomes something a script, the CLI, MCP or an AI agent can produce in one call.

## The idea: four layers

The core knows no standard. GOST, DIN, ISO and ASME are data.

1. **Table core (mechanics).** Cells that hold text or a block (TINSERT), including dynamic block visibility states. Each cell edge can have its own lineweight. Cells can set alignment, margins and text rotation, so vertical header text works. Also: text height per cell, merges, rows that grow for their text, and cut, copy and paste of cells (also from and to a spreadsheet). *Prototype done, PR to follow.*
2. **Data schema (fields).** Values read from drawing objects: block attributes, dynamic properties, layer, colour, xdata/XRECORD values, the length of a connector, and computed fields.
3. **Table template (look), JSON.** Columns, header layout, line roles (outline 0.7, inner 0.25), text heights, and the row height rule ("multiples of 8 mm" for GOST 2.106, free growth elsewhere). A template for GOST 2.106 specifications, a DIN/ISO parts list or an ASME BOM is a file, not code.
4. **Report (which rows), JSON.** Objects (a selection, layers, blocks by name) become rows. Rows can be grouped, sorted, counted, summed and split into sections. Lookups through CSV/JSON tables (part → ERP code, wire typ…

title: convert silently omits Proxy entities (meshes, REGION, PDF underlays) and exits 0
author: MauroSalvadori
body:
**Version:** cadcraft-cli 0.6.2, `linux-aarch64` release binary.

**Reproduce** with public test files from LibreDWG `test/test-data` (commit `f860b0fb76d5f8effb5a70769a3389cb1e0308c8`), e.g. `example_2018.dwg`, `2000/TS1.dxf`, `2004/Underlay.dxf`:

```
cadcraft-cli info example_2018.dwg      # counts.Proxy = 5
cadcraft-cli convert example_2018.dwg out.svg
```

**Expected:** every model-space entity is drawn, or the conversion reports that some could not be.
**Actual:** entities reported as `Proxy` by `info` are silently left out of `convert` to svg/png/pdf, exit code 0. In this corpus that covers polyface/polygon mesh `POLYLINE`s, `REGION` and `PDFUNDERLAY` (`Underlay.dxf` contains only underlays and produces an empty SVG with exit 0).

Across 117 public drawings, 39 contained such entities. For a server-side preview a silent partial drawing is the dangerous case; even a warning on stderr or a non-zero exit (opt-in flag) would let callers decide. Related: #1019 (REGION preservation on save).

title: DXF export writes $INSUNITS = 1 (inches) for drawings that declare no units
author: MauroSalvadori
body:
**Version:** cadcraft-cli 0.6.2, `linux-aarch64` release binary.

**Reproduce** with public test files from LibreDWG `test/test-data` (commit `f860b0fb76d5f8effb5a70769a3389cb1e0308c8`), e.g. `r12/Leader.dxf`, `r14/Leader.dxf`, `example_r14.dxf`:

```
cadcraft-cli convert r12/Leader.dxf out.dxf
```

**Expected:** a drawing with no declared units (`$INSUNITS` absent or 0 = unitless) stays unitless.
**Actual:** the written DXF declares `$INSUNITS = 1` (inches). 17 files from R2.6 to R14 behave this way. Downstream tools then scale the drawing as inches. Related: #1182 (asking for units only on the first New).

title: Mouse/canvas lag on Linux (Rocky 10), both PhotoCraft 0.5.0 and CADCraft 0.4.0
author: LightTrack
body:
OS: Rocky Linux 10 (GNOME, Wayland), kernel 6.12
GPU: Intel Iris Xe + NVIDIA RTX 3050 Mobile (driver 580.178.04), Vulkan lists all adapters in vulkaninfo

title: Fonts activated through Adobe Fonts are not found; styles fall back to the stroke font

A text style with a font activated through Adobe Fonts (for example Neue Haas Grotesk Text Pro) falls back to the stroke font: `style.list` reports `trueType: false`, the same as a font name that does not exist. macOS lists the family as available (CTFontManagerCopyAvailableFontFamilyNames). CADCraft 0.6.2, CLI, macOS universal, macOS 26.1 (25B78)

title: dxf: audit follow-ups (B10, B14, S1, S2, O2-O5)
author: vangel76
body:
Follow-up to #1025 / #1026 (crates/dxf audit). The findings below were deliberately left out of that PR. Each was checked again on current `main`.

## Bug
- **B10**: the binary reader treats group code 255 as an R12 escape (`FF 00 <code>`) and reads the next two bytes as the real code. Code 255 is not a DXF group, but `write_binary(&[Tag::s(255, "x"), Tag::s(0, "EOF")])` does not read back (`Err(Eof)`), and hostile input can make the reader skip a code. CADCraft reads R13+ binary DXF only, so the branch is dead weight.
- **B14**: `$DWGCODEPAGE` values with no decoder (DOS 855, 857, 860, 861, 863, 864, 865, 869, 720, 737, 775 and ISO8859_15) fall back to Windows-1252 with a warning, so accented or Greek/Cyrillic/Arabic text comes out as wrong characters. (ANSI_1361/Johab stays unsupported: `encoding_rs` has no Johab decoder.)

## Simplification
- **S1**: `format_real` has dead branches (`{v}` of a finite `f64` never uses an exponent; non-finite values are returned one line earlier).
- **S2**: `is_utf8_version` in `codepage.rs` duplicates `Version::for_acadver(..).utf8()`.

## Optimization
- **O2**: ASCII reader copies every string value once more in `unescape_unicode` even when it has no escape.
- **O3**: `unescape_unicode` collects the whole string into a `Vec<char>` (4 bytes per char) whenever it holds one escape; a 100 MB hostile string needs ~400 MB extra.
- **O4**: `Cur::cstr` scans byte by byte with two bounds checks per byte (the writer temporaries turned out not measurable and were dropped in the PR).
- **O5**: the binary reader formats each hex byte through `write!`.

## Not in this issue
B6, S3, S4, O1 wait for #988/#839 (same lines). B11-B13 stay as they are. S5 (second UTF-8 check in `decode_ascii_file`) and the EOF-test allocation of O2 sit on lines #1026 rewrites; they are not changed here.

title: fonts: MTEXT \W…x is relative; document the 200000-atom cap
author: vangel76
body:
Found in an audit of the text engine in `crates/fonts`.

## MTEXT `\W...x` is read as an absolute width factor

The public DXF reference says a trailing `x` on the width code (`\W2x;`) makes the value relative: it multiplies the current width factor. `parse` in `crates/fonts/src/mtext.rs` strips the `x` and stores the number as an absolute factor (`f.wf = v`). `\H...x` already handles this correctly. Example: inside `\W2;...\W2x;` the second run should be 4 times the base factor, but it is 2.

Only the `x` handling is in scope. `\K`, `\T` and `\A` are not touched.

## The 200 000-atom cap is not documented

`parse` stops after `MAX_ATOMS` (200 000) words, spaces and paragraph breaks and silently drops the rest. The constant's comment only says "hostile contents". Behaviour stays as it is (no warning channel); the limit should be written down at the constant and in `docs/` where it fits.

## Plan

- `\W...x` multiplies the current width factor; the result stays within the 0.01..100 range an absolute `\W` accepts.
- Doc comment on `MAX_ATOMS` and a short note in docs.
- Regression test for relative, absolute and hostile values.

title: Point cloud support: E57 import, non-destructive crop, movable slice, section extraction to 2D
author: silaghis
body:
## Summary

Support for point clouds in the style of AutoCAD: attach a scan (E57), crop it non-destructively, slice it with a movable section plane of adjustable thickness, and extract 2D linework from the slice. This is a standard workflow for as-built plans, façades and sections from terrestrial laser scans.

I know 3D is not started yet (M11). The 2D-projected parts (top/side view of the cloud, slice, extraction) don't strictly need a 3D viewport, so they may be worth considering earlier.

## Requested features

1. **Import**: E57 (the common export format of terrestrial scanners). AutoCAD itself only attaches RCS/RCP (E57 must go through ReCap first), so native E57 would be an improvement. LAS/LAZ and XYZ/PTS would be nice follow-ups.
2. **Display**: point size and density controls; colour modes: scan RGB, intensity, elevation, single colour. Must stay usable with very large scans (tens/hundreds of millions of points).
3. **Crop** (AutoCAD: `POINTCLOUDCROP`): rectangular, polygonal and circular crop; keep inside or outside; invert; show/hide; uncrop last / uncrop all; multiple crops per cloud. Crop is view-only: the point data is never deleted.
4. **Slice** (AutoCAD: `SECTIONPLANE`, type Slice): a section plane with adjustable thickness that can be moved through the cloud, showing only the points inside the slab. Orientation settable (horizontal for plans, vertical for elevations/sections).
5. **Extract to 2D** (AutoCAD: `PCEXTRACTSECTION`): generate lines/polylines from the points on the slice. Options: entire cross-section or perimeter only, target layer and colour, line vs polyline, minimum line length, connect-lines tolerance, collinear angle tolerance, preview before creating. As a first step, even exporting the slice as a point/density underlay to trace over would be useful.
6. **Large coordinates**: scans in national grid coordinates (hundreds of thousands to millions of units) should display without jitter.

title: Report: a real-world corpus run of 13 DWG drawings (R2004–R2010) against 0.7.0 — open, DXF and DWG round trip checked with ezdxf, PDF/PNG export on Windows 11
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
docs/gaps.md lists "No real-file test corpus and no check in AutoCAD" as an alpha blocker ("All 36 file tests are synthetic; nobody has verified a CADCraft DWG/DXF opens cleanly in AutoCAD"). There is no AutoCAD on this machine, so the independent reader here is ezdxf 1.4 for the DXF side; for the DWG side only CADCraft itself reads its output. This is a run over real-world DWG files on Windows 11. I repeat it on every CADCraft release; the delta to the previous release will be posted here as a comment, and any finding goes into its own issue with a synthetic fixture (https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures).

**Corpus.** 13 DWG drawings from the files of a German property-management office. They are private and can't be published, not even in part; real files are used to *find* problems only.

| | drawings |
|---|---|
| Version | AC1018 (R2004) 7 · AC1021 (R2007) 5 · AC1024 (R2010) 1 |
| File size | < 256 KB 5 · 256 KB – 1 MB 6 · 1.4 MB 1 · 8.2 MB 1 |
| Entities (`info`) | 179 – 90,008, median 1,802 |
| Layers · blocks | 20 – 253 · 24 – 633 |
| Entity types (drawings) | Line, Block Reference, MText (13) · Text, Polyline, Circle (12) · Arc, Hatch (11) · Point (9) · Spline (8) · Raster Image (7, external image not in the corpus) · Ellipse (3) · 2D Solid, Attribute Definition (2) · 3D Polyline, Dimension, Leader, Trace (1) |

**Checks.** Per drawing, each as its own `cadcraft-cli` process with wall time and exact peak working set: `info`; `convert` to DXF, PDF and PNG; `info` of the DXF; `convert` to DWG and `info` of that DWG. ezdxf 1.4.4 reads the exported DXF (`readfile`, `audit`, model-space entities per type, layers). PDF page 1 (pypdfium2) and the PNG must have more than 0.1 % non-background pixels.

title: Add PDFIMPORT command for direct PDF vector conversion
author: one67
body:
### Issue 1: Add `PDFIMPORT` command for direct PDF vector conversion

**Problem:**
Currently, users must open AutoCAD in parallel solely to import vector PDFs into a drawing. Switching applications breaks the drafting flow and introduces file-lock sync issues when working on the same DXF/DWG file.

**Proposed Solution:**
Implement a `PDFIMPORT` command using a Rust PDF parsing library (e.g., `pdfium-render` bindings or `pdf-rs`).

**Key Requirements:**

* Extract path primitives (lines, polylines, curves) directly into native CADCraft vector entities.
* Support layer assignment and scale-to-fit options during import.
* Basic text extraction from embedded PDF fonts into single-line text entities.

title: VIEWPORT view twist and per-viewport UCS are dropped on read and lost on save (rotated plans on every sheet
author: Foothold9795
body:
### Summary
Paper-space viewports that use a view twist (AutoCAD: `UCS` → rotate, then `PLAN` inside the viewport,
or `DVIEW TWist`) display unrotated in CADCraft, and the twist is lost when the drawing is saved.
For architectural sheet sets where the building is drawn on true site bearing and each viewport is
twisted to square the building to the sheet, every plan, RCP and site viewport comes out rotated.
Saving the DWG from CADCraft then writes the viewports without the twist, so the sheets open rotated
in AutoCAD as well.

### Environment
- CADCraft 0.7.0 (ArtCraft Launcher), Windows 11 x64
- Source drawings: AutoCAD 2021 (AC1032), eTransmit set of 21 A1 sheets with xrefs

### Steps to reproduce
1. In AutoCAD, create a layout viewport over model geometry drawn at an angle (e.g. 6°).
2. Inside the viewport: `UCS` → `Z` → rotate to align with the geometry, then `PLAN` → `Current`.
   The viewport's view twist is now non-zero and `UCSVP` = 1.
3. Save, then open the drawing in CADCraft and switch to the layout.
4. Save as DWG from CADCraft and reopen in AutoCAD.

### Expected
- Step 3: the viewport shows the geometry rotated by the twist angle, as AutoCAD does.
- Step 4: twist and viewport UCS survive the round trip unchanged.

### Actual
- Step 3: geometry is shown unrotated (at its model-space bearing).
- Step 4: the twist is gone, so the viewport shows the unrotated view in AutoCAD too.

### Cause (from reading the source at fc4e983)
- `doc::entity::Viewport` has no twist or UCS fields, so the values are never read.
- DXF VIEWPORT groups that need keeping: 51 (view twist angle), 16/17 (view direction/target),

  flag), 79 (orthographic type), 146 (elevation).
- `docs/gaps.md` U11 says "view twist is kept but not shown", but that covers named views (VIEW table)
  only. It does not apply to VIEWPORT entities.

title: Project Proposal: NestCraft - Standalone Cross-Platform CAM, DXF Nesting, HVAC, and RS-232 DNC Suite
author: Alberto-1976
body:
Hi Brandon and community,

Unlike 3D printing, which was born open-source, the industrial CNC, routing, and plasma cutting sector has been closed and locked behind proprietary Windows monopolies for decades. We need to change this with a modern, cross-platform solution.

I propose a brand new, standalone application named NestCraft (or ForgeCraft). It should not be a module inside CADCraft, but a dedicated workflow software that sits between the CAD and the physical machine. 

Here is how this standalone suite should work:

1. DXF Part Library & Sheet Nesting: The user imports multiple DXF files from CAD into a local library, then arranges and nests them together onto a virtual sheet of metal to optimize material usage.
2. Parametric HVAC & Shape Generator: Directly inside the app, users can generate flat patterns for sheet metal transitions (elbows, hoppers, curves, raccordi) just by typing in dimensional values, adding them instantly to the sheet layout.
3. CAM & G-Code Processing: Once the layout is ready, the software processes the geometry, applies kerf compensation (lead-in/lead-out), and generates the final G-Code.
4. DNC RS-232 Serial Transmission: A built-in serial directory/transmission utility to send the generated G-Code file directly to legacy industrial CNC consoles using native serial communication (handling baud rates and XON/XOFF protocols).

This is a niche, yet vital industry that has never seen a true open-source, agent-native revolution. Building this in pure Rust would finally give workshops and fabricators total platform freedom.

Thank you!

title: Critical CAD Fillet Solver Defect: Arc Tangency Branch Failure Overwrites Base Geometry
author: one67
body:
**### Critical CAD Fillet Solver Defect: Arc Tangency Branch Failure Overwrites Base Geometry**

System: CADCraft
Severity: High / Critical
Impact: Geometry Corruption & Data Loss

**### SUMMARY**
The fillet command fails to compute the correct tangent solution between a circle and a line when specified with a radius of 30. Instead of constructing an exterior tangent fillet arc, the geometric solver selects an invalid solution branch and destructively modifies the base circle, altering its radius and replacing original geometry.

**### REPRODUCING STEPS**

1. Draw a circle and an intersecting or adjacent horizontal line segment.
2. Run the FILLET command and set the radius to 30.
3. Select the outer edge of the circle and the horizontal line as fillet targets.

**EXPECTED BEHAVIOR (AutoCAD)**
The solver constructs a distinct tangent arc of R=30 connecting the circle perimeter to the line, leaving the original circle intact.

**ACTUAL BEHAVIOR (CADCraft)**
The solver evaluates the wrong center point for the R=30 tangent arc and overwrites the primary circle's boundary curve, distorting the base geometry.

**ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS**

1. Tangency Branch Selection: The 2D constraint solver miscalculates the pick-point vector, defaulting to an interior/complementary tangent circle center rather than the exterior solution.
2. Entity Trim/Replace Logic: The fillet routine executes a destructive entity-replacement operation on the circle rather than inserting a discrete arc entity and performing standard curve trimming.

**URGENCY**
This bug causes silent geometric distortion and model corruption during basic drafting workflows. Immediate patch required.

title: Feature request: Geospatial and civil workflows (AutoCAD Map 3D / Civil 3D parity)
author: landodragon141
body:
Summary

Please add a geospatial and civil layer to CADCraft, modeled on what AutoCAD Map 3D and Civil 3D offer. A lot of people in utility, telecom, survey and municipal work only pay for Map 3D or Civil 3D for a few core features: coordinate systems, attribute data on objects, GIS import/export, and basic surfaces/COGO. An open-source tool that covers these would be very useful to that group, especially since many of us also work in ArcGIS/QGIS.

Use case

I do GIS for fiber/telecom outside-plant work. My daily work moves data between DWG design files and GIS (ArcGIS Pro / ArcGIS Online). Today that means georeferencing drawings, attaching attributes to linework (cable, conduit, vaults, poles), and exporting to shapefile/geodatabase. All of that needs Map 3D.

Proposed features (in priority order)

Phase 1: Map 3D core

1. Coordinate systems. Let users assign a coordinate system to a drawing (EPSG codes, State Plane, UTM), stored in the DWG the same way Map 3D does it so it stays compatible. Add on-the-fly reprojection when inserting or attaching drawings. A good fit would be the proj crate (Rust bindings for PROJ).
2. Object data tables. Define attribute tables (fields with types) and attach records to entities. Users should be able to view and edit them in a properties or table panel. Ideally these read and write Map 3D Object Data, so existing drawings keep their attributes.
3. GIS import/export. Shapefile, GeoJSON, GeoPackage and KML/KMZ in both directions, with attributes mapped to and from object data. File geodatabase export would be a strong stretch goal (GDAL supports it).
4. Attribute-based selection and query. Select or filter entities by layer, location (inside a boundary or buffer) or attribute value, similar to Map 3D’s Define Query.

Phase 2: Map 3D extended

5. Live connections to feature sources (WFS, ArcGIS REST Feature Services, PostGIS) as read-only overlays, similar to Map 3D’s FDO Data Connect.
6. Thematic styling by attribute in the style of…

title: Assign a coordinate system to a drawing and reproject on insert/attach
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Drawings have no coordinate system, so there’s no reliable way to know where linework sits in the real world. You also can’t combine drawings or data that use different projections. In utility, telecom and survey work, the drawing’s units and location have to match the GIS data exactly.

Proposed behavior

A command (e.g. ASSIGNCS) sets the drawing’s coordinate system by EPSG code, with a searchable picker for common systems (State Plane, UTM, WGS84).
The CS is saved in the DWG/DXF. Ideally it reads and writes the same storage Map 3D uses, so the CS survives a round-trip through Map 3D.
When a drawing or block with a different CS is inserted or attached, its geometry is reprojected into the host drawing’s CS.
The status bar shows the current CS. Optionally it also shows the cursor position in lat/long.

Acceptance criteria

Assign EPSG:6342 (NAD83(2011) / UTM 13N), save, reopen, and the CS is still there.
Insert a drawing in State Plane into a UTM drawing and it lands in the right place (within the projection library’s tolerance).
A DWG with a Map 3D–assigned CS shows that CS when opened.

Implementation notes
The proj crate (PROJ bindings) handles the transforms. Without a CS assigned, the drawing behaves exactly as it does today.

title: Object data: define attribute tables and attach records to entities
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
CAD entities can’t carry structured attributes, such as a cable’s fiber count, install date, owner or status. Block attributes and XDATA only cover part of this. Map 3D’s Object Data is what many existing DWGs use in practice.

Proposed behavior

Define tables with typed fields (text, integer, real, date) and default values.
Attach one or more records to any entity: lines, polylines, blocks, points, etc.
A properties or table panel lets you view and edit records for the current selection.
Records are kept when entities are copied, moved or mirrored. They’re removed with the entity when it’s deleted.
Records are saved in the DWG. Ideally the format is compatible with Map 3D Object Data, so existing attributed drawings open with their data intact.

Acceptance criteria

Create a table FIBER_CABLE (CABLE_ID text, COUNT integer, STATUS text), attach it to a polyline, save, reopen, and the values are still there.
Copying the polyline copies the record.
A DWG with existing Map 3D Object Data shows those records, read-only at minimum.

Related
This is the attribute source for GIS export (#1350 ), queries (#1351 ) and thematic styling (#1353 ).

title: Import and export GIS formats (Shapefile, GeoJSON, GeoPackage, KML/KMZ)
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Moving data between CAD and GIS (ArcGIS, QGIS, Google Earth) currently needs a separate paid tool or a multi-step conversion.

Proposed behavior

Export: choose layers or a selection, a format, and the attribute source (object data, block attributes, or none). Points, lines and polygons each go to their own matching geometry type.
Import: read features into chosen layers, and optionally write their attributes as object data.
Reproject to and from the drawing’s CS on import and export, if one is assigned.
Both commands are scriptable through the CLI and MCP, e.g. cadcraft export --layers "FIBER*" --format gpkg --out routes.gpkg.

Acceptance criteria

An exported GeoPackage opens in QGIS and ArcGIS Pro with the right geometry, location and attributes.
A shapefile round-trip (export, then import) keeps geometry and attribute values.
Closed polylines export as polygons. Open ones export as lines.
KMZ opens in Google Earth in the right place (WGS84).

Related
Attributes come from object data (#OD). Reprojection uses the coordinate system support (#CS). Export without attributes can ship without either.

Implementation notes
The gdal crate covers all four formats. A pure-Rust option is geozero plus format-specific crates.

title: Select and filter entities by attribute, layer and location
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
In large drawings it’s slow to find “all cables with STATUS = Planned” or “all vaults inside this boundary” without a query tool. Map 3D’s Define Query is the reference.

Proposed behavior

A query builder that combines conditions:
Property: layer, color, linetype, entity type, block name
Data: object data field values (=, <>, <, >, LIKE, IN)
Location: inside or crossing a boundary, or within a buffer distance of a selected entity
Results become the active selection, or can be isolated or hidden.
Saved, named queries that can be re-run.
Available through CLI and MCP.

Acceptance criteria

FIBER_CABLE.STATUS = 'Planned' AND layer LIKE 'FIBER*' selects exactly the matching entities.
“Inside polygon” works correctly on concave boundaries.
Saved queries are still there after the drawing is reopened.

Related
Data conditions need object data (#1349 ). Property and location queries can ship without it.

title: Connect to live feature services as read-only overlays (ArcGIS REST, WFS, PostGIS)
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Design work often has to line up with authoritative GIS data that changes, such as existing utilities, parcels or right-of-way. Exporting and re-importing snapshots goes stale quickly.

Proposed behavior

A data connection manager for:
ArcGIS REST Feature Services (public endpoints, plus token auth)
OGC WFS
PostGIS
Features appear as read-only overlay layers, kept separate from drawing entities.
Filter by the current view extent and an optional attribute filter, to keep requests small.
Manual refresh, plus an optional refresh interval.
Connection settings are saved with the drawing. Credentials are not saved in the DWG.
An optional “copy to drawing” command turns selected overlay features into regular entities.

Acceptance criteria

Connect to a public ArcGIS Feature Service and the features show up in the right place in a drawing with an assigned CS.
Panning or zooming loads only the features in view.
Overlay features can be snapped to but not edited.
A saved and reopened drawing restores the connection, prompting for credentials if needed.

Related
Reprojection depends on the coordinate system support (#1348 ).

title: Thematic styling: display entities by attribute value
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Users need to see data visually, e.g. color fiber routes by status or vary line weight by fiber count, without changing the entities’ real layer and color properties.

Proposed behavior

Style rules per layer or per query:
Categorical: unique value → color, linetype or lineweight
Ranged: numeric bins → color or lineweight
Display-only by default: the entities’ own properties don’t change. An optional “bake” command applies the styling permanently.
A legend that can be placed in model space or paper space.
Rules can be saved as reusable style definitions.

Acceptance criteria

A categorical rule on STATUS colors Planned, Constructed and Abandoned cables differently, without changing their layer or color properties.
Turning the theme off returns the drawing to its normal display.
The legend shows every category and range.
Plot/print output matches what’s on screen.

Related
Attribute values come from object data (#1349 ). Styling by block attributes or layer could ship first.

title: COGO points with point groups and CSV/PNEZD import/export
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Survey and field data usually comes in as point files: point number, northing, easting, elevation and description. CADCraft has no smart point object that keeps these values, labels itself and can be grouped. Plain POINT entities with text labels next to them don’t stay in sync.

Proposed behavior

A COGO point entity that stores point number, N/E/Z, raw description and full description.
Label styles that can show any of those fields, and that update when the point moves or its data changes.
Import and export of CSV/TXT in common orders (PNEZD, PENZD, NEZ, comma or space delimited), with a preview before importing.
Point groups: named sets defined by number range, description match (wildcards), layer, or a manual list. Each group can override display and label style.
Duplicate point-number handling on import: renumber, overwrite, merge, or skip.
Available through CLI and MCP, e.g. cadcraft points import survey.csv --format PNEZD --group "Topo".

Acceptance criteria

Import a 1,000-point PNEZD file; all points land at the right N/E/Z with labels.
Moving a point updates its label and stored coordinates.
A group defined as desc LIKE 'MH*' picks up new matching points automatically.
Export, then re-import, gives the same values.

Related
Location and units follow the drawing CS when one is assigned (#1348 ).

title: Description keys: map point codes to layers, symbols and labels automatically
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Field crews code points (MH, VLT, PP, EP). Without automatic mapping, someone has to fix the layer and symbol on every point by hand after import.

Proposed behavior

Description key sets: code pattern (wildcards) → layer, block/symbol, label style, and optional full-description format, e.g. $0 $1 using parameters from the raw description.
Optional symbol scale or rotation driven by a parameter, e.g. PP 45 sets a 45° rotation.
Keys apply on import and can be re-applied to existing points.
Key sets can be exported and imported as JSON or CSV, so they can be shared across projects.

Acceptance criteria

With key VLT* → layer V-COMM-VAULT + block VAULT, imported points coded VLT1 get that layer and symbol.
Changing a key and re-applying it updates existing points.
Codes with no match go to a default layer and are listed in an import report.

Related
Depends on #1354.

title: TIN surfaces from points and breaklines, with contours and analysis
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Existing-ground and design work needs a terrain model. Without one there are no contours, no spot elevations and no profiles, and that’s most civil and site work.

Proposed behavior

Build a TIN from point groups, 3D polylines and blocks/points with elevation.
Constraints: breaklines (standard and proposed), outer boundary, hide boundaries, and a maximum triangle edge length.
Display: triangles, major/minor contours at a set interval, smoothing, and elevation/slope banding.
Labels: spot elevation at a picked point, contour labels, and slope arrows.
The surface updates when source data changes (a manual rebuild is fine as a first step).
Import and export of LandXML surfaces. Optionally DEM/GeoTIFF import.

Acceptance criteria

A surface built from #POINTS data and breaklines makes contours that don’t cross breaklines.
Spot elevation at any point inside the TIN matches linear interpolation on that triangle.
Contours with a 1 ft / 5 ft interval look right and label correctly.
A LandXML surface from Civil 3D imports with the same triangle count and elevations.

Implementation notes
spade (a Rust constrained Delaunay crate) can handle triangulation with breaklines.

title: Horizontal alignments: tangents, curves, spirals and station labels
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Roads, utility routes and pipelines are designed and staked along a stationed centerline. Plain polylines don’t carry stationing, and their curve geometry isn’t defined the way design standards expect.

Proposed behavior

An alignment entity made of tangents, circular curves and (stretch goal) clothoid spirals.
Create from a polyline, or with a layout toolbar (fixed, floating and free elements).
Set a starting station and add station equations.
Labels: major/minor station ticks, geometry points (PC, PT, PI), and curve data (R, L, Δ, chord).
Station-offset readout on the cursor, and a “point at station/offset” command.
Import and export as LandXML.

Acceptance criteria

Turning a polyline with arcs into an alignment keeps the geometry and gives continuous stationing.
Station-offset readout matches computed values within 0.001 units.
Editing a curve radius updates downstream stationing and labels.
A LandXML alignment from Civil 3D imports with the same geometry and stations.

Telecom/utility note
Fiber and conduit routes are often staked by station-offset. This alone is valuable even without profiles.

title: Profiles: sample a surface along an alignment and design vertical geometry
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Grades, cover depth and crossings need a vertical view along the route. Without profiles, people draw them by hand in a separate grid.

Proposed behavior

Profile view: a grid with station and elevation axes, a vertical exaggeration setting, and data bands (stations, elevations).
Existing-ground profile sampled from a surface along an alignment, updating when the surface changes.
Design profile: PVIs with vertical curves (parabolic), and grade/K-value labels.
Show crossing objects (pipes, other alignments) in the profile view.
Export profile data as CSV.

Acceptance criteria

An EG profile sampled from #SURFACE along #ALIGN matches spot elevations at the sampled stations.
A design profile with a 200 ft vertical curve gives correct elevations at sampled stations.
Changing the alignment or surface updates the EG profile.

Related
Depends on #1357 and #1356.

title: Pipe/structure networks for gravity, pressure and conduit systems
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Underground utilities (storm, sanitary, water, and also telecom conduit and duct banks) are modeled as connected pipes and structures. Right now they’re just lines and blocks with no connection, size, invert or depth.

Proposed behavior

Network entity: structures (manholes, vaults, handholes, pull boxes) and pipes/conduits connected between them.
Parts catalog: shapes, sizes and materials, editable and stored as JSON. Include conduit sizes and duct bank configurations, not just gravity pipe.
Properties: start/end invert, slope, cover depth (from a surface), length, and part attributes.
Layout from plan: pick a structure, then draw pipe to the next structure. Or convert existing linework plus blocks into a network.
Show the network in profile views with correct inverts.
Reports: a pipe and structure table, plus a minimum-cover check against a surface.

Acceptance criteria

Moving a structure stretches the connected pipes and updates lengths and slopes.
Cover depth updates when the reference surface changes.
Converting a polyline plus vault blocks gives a connected network with the right topology.
The structure table exports to CSV.

Related
Cover and profile features depend on #1356 and #1358. Plan-only layout can ship first.

title: COGO commands: bearing-distance input, inverse, traverse and curve calculator
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Legal descriptions, plats and field notes describe geometry by bearings, distances and curve data. Drafting from them without COGO tools is slow and easy to get wrong.

Proposed behavior

Bearing/distance and azimuth/distance line input, e.g. N 45°30'15" E 250.00.
Curve input by any two of R, L, Δ, chord or chord bearing, with tangent-in/tangent-out options.
Inverse between two points: bearing, distance, ΔN/ΔE.
Traverse entry with closure report (linear misclosure, precision ratio), plus compass rule and transit rule adjustment.
Unit and angle settings: feet/US survey feet/meters; DMS, decimal degrees and gons; quadrant bearings or azimuth.
Line and curve tables that update as the geometry changes.

Acceptance criteria

Entering a closed parcel from a legal description reports closure, and adjusts it correctly with compass rule.
Inverse values match hand calculation.
A curve defined by R=500, Δ=30° gives the correct L, chord and chord bearing.
Line/curve tables update when a line is edited.

title: Preserve Civil 3D and Map 3D custom objects when opening and saving DWGs
author: landodragon141
body:
Problem
Civil 3D and Map 3D store their objects (surfaces, alignments, points, object data, CS) as custom DWG objects. If CADCraft drops or corrupts them on save, it can’t safely be used on shared files, even for simple drafting edits.

Proposed behavior

Keep unknown custom objects and their proxy graphics unchanged on save.
Show proxy graphics so Civil 3D objects are at least visible, read-only.
Warn when an edit could invalidate a custom object, e.g. deleting its layer.
Optional “explode to basic entities” for users who want plain geometry.

Acceptance criteria

Open a Civil 3D DWG with a surface, alignment and points, edit some unrelated linework, save, and reopen in Civil 3D: all custom objects are intact and still work.
Proxy graphics for those objects display in CADCraft.

title: LAYISO should lock and fade unselected layers, not hide them.
author: Codec-Bro8
body: In autocad, when performing the **LAYISO** command on a specified layer, the selected layer maintains its full opacity while the "non selected" layers opacity decrease by about 50% thereabout, this is useful in cases where you want to shift things across the drawing without touching other elements. Current Behavior: Currently, when using the LAYISO command in CADCRAFT, all non-selected layers are completely hidden from the viewport. Expected Behavior: To match industry standards like AutoCAD, LAYISO should keep non-selected layers visible but lock them and reduce their opacity by approximately 50%. The selected (isolated) layer should maintain its full opacity. Use Case & Justification: Fading and locking unselected layers provides essential visual context. It allows users to use the rest of the drawing as a spatial reference to align or shift elements without the risk of accidentally modifying the locked background components. Completely turning off the layers removes this necessary context. ## AUTOCAD _Layers before LAYISO was applied_ _Layers after LAYISO was applied_ ## CADCRAFT _Layers before LAYISO_ _Layers after LAYISO_

title: Command line AutoComplete requires mouse click; Enter key fails to execute top suggestion
author: Codec-Bro8
body: Current Behavior: When typing a partial command (e.g., "LAYIS"), the AutoComplete dropdown menu successfully populates with relevant suggestions. However, pressing the Enter key attempts to run the exact incomplete text string rather than executing the top or highlighted suggestion. This results in a "command doesn't exist" error, forcing the user to stop typing and use the mouse to manually click the desired command from the list. Expected Behavior: To match standard drafting workflows (like AutoCAD), pressing Enter or the Spacebar while typing a partial command should automatically fill in and execute the top or currently highlighted suggestion in the AutoComplete list (e.g., typing "LAYIS" + Enter should execute LAYISO). Use Case & Justification: Standard CAD workflows rely heavily on keyboard shortcuts to maintain speed and efficiency. Forcing a user to switch from the keyboard to the mouse just to select an AutoComplete suggestion completely breaks drafting muscle memory and significantly slows down the drawing process. ## CADSCRAFT ## AUTOCAD tested on windows 11 25H2.

title: Proposal: a read-only drawing analysis command for agents (geometry facts, not labels)
author: ParadoxEthos
body:
### Problem

An agent working on a drawing can get counts and extents (`inspect_drawing`) and raw entity geometry (`query_entities`), but it has to compute everything else itself, and LLMs are bad at that: they miscount closed boundaries, guess areas from coordinates, miss that a boundary drawn as loose LINEs is open by 0.002, and don't notice the 40 copies of the same profile. AREA, LIST, MEASUREGEOM, BOUNDARY, PURGE and OVERKILL already compute much of this, but one object or selection at a time, and for a person at the command line.

### Proposal

One read-only command (working name `analyze`; happy to take a different name) that computes geometry facts across the whole drawing, or a window/layer/type filter, and returns them as JSON. Like every command it would reach MCP, the control channel, the CLI and scripts with no extra wiring; the MCP side would be a thin `analyze_drawing` tool.

**Design rule: facts, never labels.** It reports lengths, areas, closure and repetition, and never classifies anything ("wall", "duct", "decorative"). What a shape means is left to the agent, so the command works on any drawing in any discipline.

### Scope, split into small PRs

1. **Closed-shape analysis** for LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE (2D), CIRCLE and closed SPLINE/ELLIPSE: bulge-aware perimeter and area, centroid, winding, self-intersection, coincident and near-duplicate vertices. Reuses the AREA/LIST geometry.
2. **Implied loops from loose LINE and ARC chains:** chain endpoints within a tolerance into closed loops and analyse them as in (1), listing member handles. Open chains report their endpoint gap; branching junctions (three or more ends) are reported, not resolved.
3. **Size census and repetition:** entities binned by bounding-box size relative to the drawing, plus groups of congruent shapes (same type, matching dimensions within a relative tolerance), with counts and handles.
4. **Usage cross-reference:** which layers, blocks, styles and linetypes are used, including use i…

title: MOVE/COPY ignore a Z delta (the edit path drops Z)
author: cpmech
body:
## Summary

A translation that carries a Z offset silently drops it. `MOVE`/`COPY` with `{"delta":[1,2,3]}` move 1,2,0; a `3DPOLY` drawn at the command line is flat at z = 0; and a typed point's third number is parsed and thrown away. The Z **is** kept by a DXF round trip and by the planar ROTATE/SCALE/MIRROR, so this is a self-inflicted loss in the edit path, not a modelling limitation — and it corrupts data a 2D user already has (anything from a survey or Civil 3D).

Related but distinct: #917 is one instance of the same root cause (array Z offsets), #612 and #1106 ask for 3D *features*. This is the data-loss bug underneath them. `flatten` (the explicit command) is a deliberate user action and is not the issue here.

## Reproduced on main (9b2308b)

```rust
// 3DPOLY [[0,0,0],[10,0,5],[10,10,10]]  →  execute("move", {"delta": [1,2,3]})
as drawn:  [0.0, 5.0, 10.0]
after:     [0.0, 5.0, 10.0]        // Z unchanged; X/Y did move
```

```rust
// typed: 3dpoly → 0,0,0 → 10,0,5 → Enter
points:    [0.0, 0.0]              // the typed z is gone
```

Verified with temporary probes through `Session::execute`; DXF write→read of a `Polyline3d` (z = 0/5/10) and a `Face3d` (z = 1..4) returns all seven Z values intact, and `EntityKind::transform` leaves `p.z` alone for every planar matrix (see below).

## Root cause

`EntityKind::transform` takes a `Mat3`, but its point helper **keeps** Z:

```rust
// crates/doc/src/entity.rs:1180-1185
pub fn transform(&mut self, m: &Mat3) {
    let t3 = |p: &mut Vec3| { let q = m.apply(p.xy()); p.x = q.x; p.y = q.y; };
```

That is correct for the planar operations — rotating/scaling/mirroring the XY projection of `(x,y,z)` about the origin gives `(x',y',z)`, and Z passes through untouched. The only thing a `Mat3` cannot express is a translation along Z, and that is exactly what the callers need:

| # | Path | Today |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `crates/engine/src/cmd/modify.rs:147` `delta_of()` returns `Vec2`, and `:159`/`:169`/`:279`/`:462`/`:1976`… …

title: Typed points lose their third number: parse_point_with parses Z and discards it
author: cpmech
body:
Split out of #1407 (the same root cause: a coordinate's Z is dropped while an edit or an input is processed).

## Symptom

A typed point's third number is parsed and then thrown away:

```rust
// Session::cmdline("line") then typing "0,0,0" and "10,0,5"
```

`prompt::parse_point_with` accepts two **or three** comma-separated numbers (`crates/engine/src/prompt.rs:271-280`) but validates the third and discards it:

```rust
if let Some(z) = parts.get(2) {
    crate::units::parse_distance(z)?;   // parsed, then unused
}
Vec2::new(x, y)
```

So `1,2,3`, `@0,0,5` and `#10,20,30` all behave as `1,2`, `@0,0` and `#10,20`, silently. That is the input-side reason no typed Z can reach any command — `MOVE`/`COPY` displacement points included (see the MOVE half, #1407).

## Where it bites

- Every typed point anywhere, since `parse_point_with` is the single entry point.
- `MOVE`/`COPY` displacement: `@0,0,5` cannot express a pure Z move.
- `3DPOLY` typed at the command line, which is the third part of the split (companion issue).

## Verified

- `parse_point_with` returns `Vec2`; the third component is read (`parse_distance(z)?`) and dropped — source inspection on `main` (9b2308b).
- Typing `0,0,0` / `10,0,5` at `3dpoly` produces points at z = 0 (executed probe, see #1407).

## Proposed fix

A `parse_point3` sibling returning `Vec3` (or an `Option<f64>` Z alongside the existing point), used by the prompts that can carry a Z — `3DPOLY` and the `MOVE`/`COPY` displacement. `parse_point_with` keeps its `Vec2` signature so the many existing callers are untouched. Alternatives welcome: the shape here is the maintainer's call, and it is the same decision raised in #1407.

## Tests

- A typed `x,y,z` at a point prompt reaches a `Vec3`-carrying command with all three coordinates.
- `parse_point3` on `1,2`, `1,2,3`, `@0,0,5`, `#10,20,30` and the hostile forms (extra components, non-finite) with no panic.

title: Interactive 3DPOLY is drawn flat at z = 0 (the JSON form is correct)
author: cpmech
body:
Split out of #1407 (the same root cause: a coordinate's Z is dropped while an edit or an input is processed).

## Symptom

`3DPOLY` drawn at the command line is flat at z = 0, while the JSON form is correct:

```rust
// typed: 3dpoly → 0,0,0 → 10,0,5 → Enter
points: [0.0, 0.0]        // both z = 0
```

Executed probe on `main` (9b2308b). The JSON form is not affected — `run_3dpoly` reads all three components through `point3_value` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/draw2.rs:1814`), so `engine.execute("3dpoly", {"points": [[0,0,0],[10,0,5]]})` keeps Z. Only typing loses it.

## Root cause

`Poly3dM` (the interactive machine) collects `Vec2` and lifts each point with `v3(*p)`, which sets z = 0:

```rust
// crates/engine/src/cmd/draw2.rs:1838-1839
fn sync(&mut self, s: &mut Session, closed: bool) -> Result<()> {
    let k = EntityKind::Polyline3d(Polyline3d { points: self.pts.iter().map(|p| v3(*p)).collect(), closed });
```

Downstream, the typed third number never arrives anyway: `parse_point_with` parses it and discards it (`crates/engine/src/prompt.rs:278`) — that is the companion issue, and it has to land for this one to be observable end to end.

## Proposed fix

`Poly3dM` stores `Vec3` and accumulates from the Z-carrying point prompt (companion issue), with the JSON form and the `3dpoly` params doc unchanged. Point entry stays a 2D pick on screen; the typed third coordinate is what carries Z.

## Tests

- Typed `3dpoly` with a third coordinate on each point round-trips the Z into the entity.
- `3dpoly` with two coordinates still gives z = 0 (no behaviour change for the flat case).

title: LWPOLYLINE/HATCH elevation is read, written and then ignored: the display, extents, snaps and picking are all 2D
author: cpmech
body:
## Summary

`LWPOLYLINE` and `HATCH` carry an **elevation** (DXF group 38, or the Z of the first group 10) and CADCraft reads it from the file and writes it back — but **nothing ever uses it**. The whole display path is 2D (`Prim`, `DisplayList::verts` are `Vec2`), so an outline at elevation 6000 draws exactly on top of one at 0. A drawing with stacked floors, a ceiling plan and a foundation plan look like one flat drawing even though the file kept every Z value.

This is very likely the mechanism behind #612 ("DXF files I am opening have all the Z values flattened to zero") — for LWPOLYLINE-based drawings the data is not flattened, the *display* is.

## Reproduced on main (9b2308b)

Two identical closed 10×10 outlines, one `elevation: 0.0`, one `elevation: 6000.0`:

```
extents  = Bounds2 { min: (0,0), max: (10,10) }            // no notion of height
elevation 0    -> prims [Seg(a:(0,0) b:(10,0)), …]          // identical
elevation 6000 -> prims [Seg(a:(0,0) b:(10,0)), …]          // identical
display list   -> prim 0 verts [(0,0),(10,0),(10,10),(0,10),(0,0)]
                  prim 1 verts [(0,0),(10,0),(10,10),(0,10),(0,0)]   // coincident
```

And the file half already works, so this is display-only:

```
read  a minimal DXF with 38 = 6000.0 → LwPolyline { …, elevation: 6000.0 }
write that drawing and read it back   → LwPolyline { …, elevation: 6000.0 }
```

## Root cause

Nothing between the entity and the screen carries Z:

| Stage | Code | Elevation |
|---|---|---|
| Entity primitives | `crates/doc/src/entity.rs:1146` `EntityKind::LwPolyline(p) => Polyline { vertices: p.vertices.clone(), … }` and `:1440` for `Hatch` | not applied; returns `Vec2` segments |
| Document extents | `crates/doc/src/extents.rs` (everything is `Bounds2`) | no height, so `ZOOM E` cannot see it |
| Display list | `crates/render/src/lib.rs:1146` `LwPolyline` branch; `DPrim`/`verts`/`tris` are 2D | not applied |
| Picking, snaps, selection | R-tree in `crates/engine/src/spatial.rs`, all X…

title: ARC: "hold Ctrl to switch direction" prompt exists, but Ctrl never reaches the command
author: william-wwh
body:
### Summary

The ARC command shows the prompt `Specify end point of arc (hold Ctrl to switch direction)`, but pressing Ctrl has no effect. Arcs are always drawn counter-clockwise. The modifier key is dropped in the UI before any engine command sees it — this is not a case of "wrong key", the feature was never implemented.

### Steps to reproduce

**Path A — Center, Start, End**
1. `a` Space `c` Space
2. `40` Space, then pick the center
3. Pick the arc's start point
4. At "Specify end point of arc", hold Ctrl and pick
5. The arc is drawn counter-clockwise; Ctrl changes nothing

**Path B — Continue**
1. Draw a line
2. `a` Space Space
3. The prompt reads `Specify end point of arc (hold Ctrl to switch direction)`
4. Hold Ctrl and pick the end point
5. The arc is drawn counter-clockwise; Ctrl changes nothing

### Expected

Pressing Ctrl at the end-point prompt should flip the arc to clockwise, matching AutoCAD. Releasing Ctrl before the pick should return to the default counter-clockwise preview. The preview and the placed arc must agree.

### Actual

Ctrl is ignored. Every arc is counter-clockwise.

### Environment

- Reproduced against `main` at `9b2308b` (2026-10-16).
- The prompt string `Specify end point of arc (hold Ctrl to switch direction)` has been in the codebase since PR #407 (merged 2026-10-10). The same string is present in all 12 i18n catalogs under `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/`, so this false prompt has shipped to users of every supported language.
- The feature has never worked at any point in this repository's history: `Input` carries no modifier state, and the UI reads `mods.ctrl` only for the grip-editing "Copy" shortcut.

`Input::Point(Vec2)` only carries a bare coordinate; `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` constructs it without reading `mods.ctrl` (the only place Ctrl is read is the grip-editing "Copy" shortcut at ~line 1505). The engine therefore never knows whether Ctrl was held.

title: [FR] Detect drawing frames in model space and publish each frame as a page of one multi-page PDF
author: skywalker-35
body:
## Use case

In Chinese engineering practice (telecom/construction completion drawings), a single DWG usually contains **all sheets tiled in model space**, separated by drawing frames (图框, typically 420×297 A3 blocks). A real-world file often holds 3–100+ frames.

Today `exportpdf` can only fit all frames onto one page (`plotArea: extents`) or requires manually computed `window` coordinates per frame. There is no way to get **one multi-page PDF with one sheet per frame** — the equivalent of AutoCAD's PUBLISH / batch plot.

## Requested

Detect drawing frames in model space automatically and export each frame as one page of a single multi-page PDF, e.g.:

```
cadcraft-cli run drawing.dwg --cmd 'exportpdf {"path":"out.pdf","paper":"A3","frames":"auto"}'
```

## Suggested detection strategy (from a working implementation)

I built a working prototype on top of `cadcraft-cli` (Python + ezdxf, ~400 lines) that processed 34 real telecom completion DWGs (250 frames, zero misses). The detection order that survived real-world data:

1. **Block references** whose name matches frame keywords (图框 / title block / border / frame) **and** whose frame rectangle matches an ISO A-series sheet (±8%).
2. Use the **largest closed 4-vertex axis-aligned rectangle inside the block** as the frame boundary — **not the block's bbox**. Real blocks often contain overflow content outside the border (sign-off panels): we measured bboxes of 439.6×297 and 453.2×297 over an actual 420×297 frame, which causes neighbor-frame bleed when plotted by bbox.
3. If the block has **no closed polyline** (border drawn as hundreds of small LINE segments), snap the bbox to the nearest ISO A-series size anchored at the block origin (0,0).
4. Fallback: closed 4-vertex axis-aligned polylines directly in model space, sheet-size filtered, with nested inner/outer frame dedup.
5. **Filter miniature references**: the same frame block is often reused as a legend icon at 0.3×–2× scale — require reference scale ≈ 1 (we use …
