title: Analysis: closed-shape geometry facts (perimeter, area, centroid, winding, self-intersection, duplicate vertices)
author: ParadoxEthos
body:
Part of #1377 (split per ticket-craft).

### Problem
An agent can read raw geometry with `query_entities`, but computing area, closure or winding from coordinates is where LLMs make mistakes, especially with polyline bulges. AREA and LIST compute some of this, but only for one picked object at a time.

### Proposal
A read-only analysis over every closed shape in the drawing (or a window/layer/type filter) that reports, per shape:
- bulge-aware perimeter and area, centroid, winding (CW/CCW)
- self-intersection (yes/no, with the first crossing point)
- coincident and near-duplicate vertices (indices and distance)

Entity types: LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE (2D), CIRCLE, closed SPLINE and ELLIPSE. Other types are counted and skipped with a reason. Reuses the AREA/LIST geometry; new geometry goes in `geom`.

### Tests
Hand-derived values on synthetic drawings generated in code: squares and bulged arcs with known areas, a bow-tie (self-intersecting), a polyline with a repeated vertex, CW and CCW copies of one shape.

### Contract
Follows #1039: bad options abort with a structured error, results are paged with `truncated` flags, and a `schema` version is included.

Drafted with Perplexity (Computer); I've reviewed it and I'm responsible for it.

title: Analysis: implied closed loops from loose LINE and ARC chains
author: ParadoxEthos
body:
Part of #1377 (split per ticket-craft).

### Problem
Boundaries are often drawn as separate LINEs and ARCs rather than one polyline. An agent can't tell whether they form a closed loop, or that a "closed" outline is actually open by 0.002.

### Proposal
Chain LINE and ARC endpoints that meet within a tolerance into loops and report:
- closed loops, with their member handles, analyzed as in #1436 (perimeter, area, winding)
- open chains, with the endpoint gap and its location
- branch junctions (three or more ends meeting), reported but not resolved

Tolerance is an option with a sensible default relative to the drawing size. O(n²) work is capped, and the cap is reported.

### Tests
Synthetic drawings: a closed rectangle of four LINEs, the same with one corner off by a known gap, a slot made of LINEs and ARCs, and a T-junction.

### Contract
Follows #1039. Depends on #1436 for the per-loop analysis.

Drafted with Perplexity (Computer); I've reviewed it and I'm responsible for it.

title: Analysis: size census and congruent shape groups
author: ParadoxEthos
body:
Part of #1377 (split per ticket-craft).

### Problem
An agent reading entity by entity doesn't notice that 40 entities are the same profile, or which shapes are tiny details next to the main outline. Counting and comparing them by hand uses a lot of context and is error-prone.

### Proposal
- **Size census:** entities binned by bounding-box size relative to the drawing extents, with a count per bin.
- **Congruent groups:** shapes of the same type with matching dimensions within a relative tolerance, grouped regardless of position and rotation, with a count and member handles per group.

Facts only, no labels: it reports "12 congruent closed shapes, 50 × 20", not what they are.

### Tests
Synthetic drawings: copies of one shape that are moved, rotated, and resized by a known amount, plus near-misses just outside the tolerance.

### Contract
Follows #1039. Large groups are paged.

Drafted with Perplexity (Computer); I've reviewed it and I'm responsible for it.

title: Analysis: usage cross-reference of layers, blocks, text styles and linetypes
author: ParadoxEthos
body:
Part of #1377 (split per ticket-craft).

### Problem
Before editing, an agent needs to know which layers, blocks, styles and linetypes are actually used, and where. PURGE finds unused items, but only as an interactive cleanup, not as a report.

### Proposal
A read-only report listing, for each layer, block, text style and linetype:
- the number of entities that use it
- whether it is used only inside block definitions
- empty and unused items

Reuses the PURGE usage scan without changing anything.

### Tests
A synthetic drawing with a used layer, an empty layer, a layer used only inside a block, an unreferenced block definition, and an unused text style and linetype.

### Contract
Follows #1039.

Drafted with Perplexity (Computer); I've reviewed it and I'm responsible for it.

title: Analysis: self-check — found/analysed/skipped counts with reasons and implausibility flags
author: ParadoxEthos
body:
Part of #1377 (split per ticket-craft).

### Problem
Agents treat "not reported" as "not there". If an analysis skips 3D meshes or hits a cap, the agent should be told, not left to infer it.

### Proposal
Every analysis result carries a self-check section:
- counts of entities found, analyzed and skipped, with a reason for each skip type (e.g. "3D mesh: present, not analyzed")
- caps that were hit, and their values
- implausibility flags, e.g. a perimeter more than 10× the bounding-box diagonal, or an area larger than the drawing extents

This is the piece I'd suggest landing first, alongside the closed-shape issue, so every later analysis reports what it covered from the start.

### Tests
Synthetic drawings that include unsupported entity types, enough entities to hit a cap, and a deliberately implausible shape.

### Contract
Follows #1039. The self-check carries the `schema` version.

Drafted with Perplexity (Computer); I've reviewed it and I'm responsible for it.

title: TK: the tracking run does not follow the cursor, and the guide / axis / marker are wrong
author: william-wwh
body:
### Summary

With `TK` (tracking), after the first pick the run does not follow the cursor at all: the point / guide stays where the first pick was put, no matter where the cursor moves. The guide also never stops at the cursor (it runs as a full ray through the base), the next leg does not alternate the axis, and the green `+` neither shows reliably on the first click nor clears after the first distance.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `line` Space
2. `tk` Space
3. Pick the first tracking point, e.g. (0,0)
4. Move the cursor

**Expected**: a green `+` at (0,0); the guide follows the cursor, on the axis the next leg will use, stopped at the cursor's projection.

**Actual**: the point / guide does not move at all — it stays at the first pick.

Continue:

title: [Perf] Per-window exportpdf rebuilds the whole drawing per window — batch frame export is O(frames × drawing size)
author: skywalker-35
body:
## Summary

Batch-exporting a tiled multi-frame drawing window-by-window (`exportpdf` with `plotArea: "window"`) scales as **O(frames × whole-drawing cost)**: each window export rebuilds the full-detail display list of the *entire* model space and only then clips to the window. Reusing one `run` session with multiple `--cmd` does **not** help — per-window cost is identical to a fresh process.

Split out from #1423 per the triage-bot suggestion (that ticket now tracks frame auto-detection + multi-page PDF only). The memory footprint of the full-detail plot build itself is #1068; this ticket is about that build being **repeated per window**, untouched by session reuse.

## Measurements

Real telecom completion drawing (v0.7.0, Windows x64): **1,519 model-space entities**, 8 A3 frames tiled in model space, heavy use of dashed linetypes (each exported page is ~23 MB of raw PDF vector data).

| Scenario | Time |
|---|---|
| DWG→DXF `convert` (pure parse proxy) | 1.1 s |
| One window, fresh CLI process | 9.2 s |
| One `run` session, 8 × `--cmd exportpdf {window}` | 71.4 s (**8.9 s/window**) |

Session reuse saves only ~0.3 s/window (the parse). The remaining ~8.9 s per window is consistent with `build_plot` tessellating every entity of the drawing — dash expansion included — before discarding everything outside the window.

On a 100-frame drawing this turns a ~2-minute job into ~15 minutes, and combined with #1068's memory growth it also makes large batches an OOM risk (we already cap batches at 15 windows per session for that reason).

## Suggested

1. **Spatial pre-filter before tessellation**: only run the full-detail build for entities whose bbox intersects the plot window (entity bboxes are cheap; dash-expanded primitives are what explode). Windowed export cost would then scale with window content, not drawing size.
2. If a frames-mode lands via #1423, the same pre-filter makes it cheap by construction.

Happy to share the sample DWG and the timing script if useful.

title: DWG written by convert puts every layout's paper-space entities on the first layout (ZWCAD 2025 shows the other sheets empty)
author: assamaraleman
body:
**Environment:** cadcraft-cli 0.7.0, Windows 11 Pro. Opened in ZWCAD 2025 (black-box: exported back to DXF with DXFOUT and inspected with ezdxf). Attached files are synthetic, generated with ezdxf (`make_repro.py`).

## Steps
```
cadcraft-cli convert repro.dxf repro_cadcraft.dwg
```
Open `repro_cadcraft.dwg` in ZWCAD 2025 and look at the layouts.

## Result
| layout | repro.dxf | CADCraft re-read of the .dwg | ZWCAD read of the .dwg |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | VIEWPORT×2, TEXT | same | VIEWPORT×6, TEXT×3 |
| S1A | VIEWPORT×2, TEXT | same | empty |
| S2 | VIEWPORT×2, TEXT | same | empty |

**Expected:** each layout keeps its own paper-space entities.
**Actual:** everything lands on the first layout; the other sheets open empty.

Model space is intact. On an 8-sheet production drawing, model space came through 1:1 (15,384 entities, layers, blocks, text styles and lineweights all matched) and only paper space broke. This looks like the layout ↔ paper-space block record linkage in the DWG writer. Possibly related: #1057 (similar symptom for layouts created with `layout.new`, observed in AutoCAD).

## Files
https://gist.github.com/assamaraleman/f3785b95cb09d7e9e95914abfc75ea44 — `make_repro.py`, `repro.dxf` and `repro_cadcraft.dwg` (the two drawings base64-encoded because gists reject binary; decode steps in README.txt).

title: DWG with ~888k orphaned DGN line style components won't open: "produced more than 1024 MB of drawing data"
author: gurparvez
body:
**Version:** CADCraft 0.7.0 (Flatpak, Linux x86_64). `main` at 9b2308b reads DWG the same way (acadrust 0.6.4, failsafe).

**What happens.** An 82.8 MB AC1032 site plan made in AutoCAD (a user's file, can't share) does not open:

```
invalid parameters for `open`: DWG: converting this 82.8 MB file produced more than 1024 MB of drawing data (the limit); the file is probably damaged, or uses objects the DWG reader misreads
```

**Diagnosis.** The file isn't damaged or misread. It carries MicroStation line style data (`AcDgnLS` classes), almost all of it orphaned, which is the same family as #800. Measured with acadrust 0.6.4 (failsafe read, as `crates/dwg` does), streaming its `DxfWriter` output through a byte counter:

- 1,633,713 object records, 11,746 skipped. The DXF rendition is **1,245.9 MB**.
- 83% of that is DGN line style components in OBJECTS:

| Record type | Count | DXF bytes |
|---|---|---|
| `LSINTERNALCOMPONENT` | 562,148 | 667.1 MB |
| `LSSTROKEPATTERNCOMPONENT` | 270,334 | 335.7 MB |
| `LSPOINTCOMPONENT` | 18,611 | 15.1 MB |
| `LSSYMBOLCOMPONENT` | 23,437 | 14.1 MB |
| `LSCOMPOUNDCOMPONENT` | 14,523 | 8.8 MB |
| everything else: 634,135 entities (in blocks and model space), tables, other objects | | ≈ 204 MB |

- **Almost all of the components are orphaned.** All 552 `LSDEFINITION`s are referenced by a line type (an `LTYPE` extension dictionary entry `DGNLSDEF`). Following each definition's `root_component`, then compound entries and point components' stroke and symbol references, reaches **570 of the 889,053 components**. The other **888,483 (99.94%)** are referenced by nothing. These are the copies that DGN imports and copy-pastes pile up, the kind AutoCAD's PURGE removes as orphaned data.
- CADCraft would throw them away anyway. Their owner, the `ACAD_DGNLINESTYLECOMP` dictionary, is itself one of the skipped records (type 42, `Truncated DWG stream at bit 1469120762`). So in `dxf_raw::read` (#528) their owner chain is broken and none of them is kep…

title: New Crafting App request: a clean-room, fully independent alternative to Autodesk Fusion (3D parametric CAD/CAM)
author: xXIlRizzoXx
body:
Hi ArtCraft team, and thanks for the Crafting Apps!

I would love to see a new app that works as much as possible like Autodesk Fusion, in the same clean-room, pure-Rust spirit as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft.

I could not find anything like it in the current lineup. The closest is CADCraft (AutoCAD-style 2D drafting), but Fusion is a different kind of tool: 3D parametric modelling.

**Key requirements**

- **Independent from the Autodesk system:** no Autodesk account, no sign-in, no cloud dependency, no subscription or licence check. It should run fully local and offline, with no Autodesk code or assets.
- **100% usable:** every feature available to everyone, with no locked, trial-only or paid-only functions.

**Core features that would matter most**

1. Sketches with constraints and dimensions.
2. Parametric solid modelling with a feature timeline/history (extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillet, chamfer, shell, patterns).
3. Components, assemblies and joints.
4. Import/export of common formats: STEP, STL, 3MF, OBJ, DXF.
5. Drawings / technical views.
6. Later: CAM toolpaths and simulation, and rendering.

If a separate app is out of scope for now, it could also grow from CADCraft with a 3D module. Happy to test early builds.

Thanks!

`cadcraft-cli --help` never returns: no output, no exit, killed it after 120 s. Running the

```console
$ timeout 120 cadcraft-cli --help
```

For an agent this is the first command it runs, and a hang is the worst possible answer —

guess that the binary is safe to run bare.

run continues, so the agent gets the 39 blocks that are fine and a precise pointer at the one
that is not.

mistake into a full retry, and there is nothing in the output to say which line caused it.

title: cadcraft-cli: --help / -h / help should exit 0 and print the usage to stdout
author: switch87
body:
Follow-up to the corrected report in #1520 — this part is real, and it was verified on the current development version before filing: **cadcraft-cli 0.8.0** (main, 714111d), built from source on this machine.

```console
$ cadcraft-cli --help >/dev/null; echo $?
1
$ cadcraft-cli --version; echo $?
cadcraft-cli 0.8.0
0
```

`--help`, `-h` and `help` all print the usage block to **stderr** and exit **1**, while `--version` prints to stdout and exits 0. (`cadcraft-cli` with no arguments at all behaving the same is fine — git does it too — but an explicit help request is not an error.)

Why it matters for scripted use: agents and scripts read stdout and branch on the exit code. A help request that looks like a failure forces every caller to special-case it, and the usage text never reaches the stream where tooling looks for it.

Expected:

- `--help`, `-h`, `help` → usage on **stdout**, exit **0**
- bare `cadcraft-cli` → unchanged (stderr, exit 1)

I'm working on this.

title: Crash on quit (SIGILL) on Intel MacBook Pro with Touch Bar — uncaught KVO exception in `_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate
author: danielebaldacci
body:
### Title
Crash on quit (SIGILL) on Intel MacBook Pro with Touch Bar — uncaught KVO exception in `_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate`

### Environment
- CADCraft 0.8.0 (ai.storyteller.cadcraft), x86_64 native
- macOS 26.2 (25C56)
- MacBookPro16,1 (16" 2019, Intel i9, Touch Bar), AMD Radeon Pro 5500M + Intel UHD 630

### Steps to reproduce
1. Launch CADCraft
2. Use it normally (or just open it)
3. Quit the app (Cmd+Q / close window)

### Expected
App exits cleanly.

### Actual
App crashes on exit with `EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION (SIGILL)`. macOS shows the crash reporter dialog. Reproducible on every quit.

### Analysis
The crash is an uncaught Objective-C exception rethrown by `+[NSApplication _crashOnException:]`. The exception originates in AppKit's Touch Bar responder-chain tracking, during the display-cycle flush after the window has been torn down:

    Foundation  -[NSObject(NSKeyValueObserverRegistration) _removeObserver:forProperty:]
    Foundation  -[NSObject(NSKeyValueObserverRegistration) removeObserver:forKeyPath:context:]
    AppKit      -[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]
    AppKit      ___NSTouchBarFinderSetNeedsUpdateOnMain_block_invoke_2
    AppKit      NSDisplayCycleFlush
    QuartzCore  CA::Transaction::commit()
    ...
    AppKit      -[NSApplication run]
    CADCraft    winit::platform_impl::macos::event_handler::EventHandler::set
                (run_app_on_demand / eframe::native::run::run_wgpu)

It looks like AppKit's `NSTouchBarFinder` tries to remove a KVO observer from a view/window (responder) that winit has already released or detached. This most likely happens because the `NSApplication` run loop keeps spinning one more display cycle after the eframe window is destroyed (`run_on_demand` path).

Possible fixes on the app side:
- Hide/order out the window and clear first responder before dropping it, so AppKit invalidates its Touch Bar observations while the responder is still alive.
- Exit the process right after `eframe::run_native…

author: mittooboy
body:
## Summary
On macOS, double-clicking a `.dwg` file in Finder starts CADCraft but doesn't open the drawing. macOS shows this error instead:

> The document "Trolley.dwg" could not be opened. CADCraft cannot open files in the "Drawing" format.

The file itself is fine. It opens normally with File ▸ Open, and also when its path is passed to CADCraft on the command line. This is the bug reported in #995 and #158, and it is still present in 0.9.0.

## Environment
| | |
|---|---|
| CADCraft | 0.9.0, build `b23d362f6af1dd77e319728f1d85882b098626fe` |
| macOS | 27.0.1 (26A434) |
| Mac | Apple Silicon (arm64) |
| File | `Trolley.dwg`, AutoCAD 2000 format (`AC1015`), 142 KB |

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install CADCraft 0.9.0 from the macOS DMG.
2. In Finder, double-click a `.dwg` file (running `open Trolley.dwg` in Terminal does the same).

## Expected
CADCraft opens the drawing, as it does with File ▸ Open.

## Actual
CADCraft starts with an empty drawing, and macOS shows the error above.

## What I checked
- **File ▸ Open:** opening the same file from inside CADCraft works.
- **App log:** `~/Library/Application Support/CADCraft/logs/cadcraft.log` contains only the two startup lines. CADCraft never tries to open the file.
- **Path argument:** `CADCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/CADCraft ~/Desktop/Trolley.dwg` opens the drawing. `drawing.inspect` on the control port reports 24 objects (8 polylines, 16 texts), 0 skipped, `dirty: false`.
- **File type:** `mdls` gives `kMDItemContentType = "ai.storyteller.cadcraft.dwg"`, which is CADCraft's own type, so the competing-type problem described in #158 doesn't apply here.

## Cause
In 0.9.0, `apps/cadcraft/src/main.rs` opens only files given on the command line (lines 236–245, then `app.open_path` at line 357). Finder doesn't pass files that way. It sends an "open documents" Apple event (`kAEOpenDocuments` / `application:openURLs:`), and nothing in CADCraft handles that event. AppKit then shows its own generic error, taking the name "Drawing…

title: Feature request: an extension API so add-ons can register commands and panels without forking
author: Eng-JulioFerreira
body:
## Summary

I'm building an add-on on top of CADCraft and would like to ship it without forking CADCraft. Today that isn't possible. I'd like to propose a small extension API that lets an add-on register commands, panels and settings when the app starts.

## Context

[FREE-ELETRICA](https://github.com/Eng-JulioFerreira/FREE-ELETRICA) is a GPL-3.0 add-on for low-voltage electrical design under the Brazilian standard NBR 5410. It handles circuits, conduit routing, wiring symbols, load schedules and utility demand tables. It adds a docked "Electrical" palette, a few windows, and about 20 engine commands, all reachable from the command line, the control port, the CLI and MCP.

It works well, but only as a fork. CADCraft is vendored as a git subtree, and these lines are patched into CADCraft's own files:

| File | What the add-on has to patch |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Cargo.toml`, `crates/engine/Cargo.toml`, `crates/ui-egui/Cargo.toml` | the add-on crate as a dependency |
| `crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs` | its `CommandSpec`s added to `command_specs()` |
| `crates/ui-egui/src/docking.rs` | a new `Panel` variant (id, label, zone, on-demand, draw, size limits) |
| `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs` | a Window menu item and routing of its UI-only commands |
| `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` | a per-frame hook to draw its windows |
| `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/*.tsv` | labels of its commands and panel |
| `apps/cadcraft/src/main.rs` | loading and saving its settings in the app storage, and opening its panel on first run |
| `xtask/src/layers.rs` | its crate in the layering table |

The patch is small, but each upstream release can conflict with it. Every add-on author would also have to maintain a fork, which splits the ecosystem. Issue #897 (BIM plugin ecosystem) points the same way.

Fillet command breaks circle when linking to a line

SUMMARY
Filleting a circle and a line with radius 30 modifies and breaks the original circle instead of adding a smooth connecting arc between them.

title: Proposal: an in-app AI Assistant (gaps A2)
author: lucabyte42-lab
body:
## What I'm proposing

An AI Assistant palette (Window ▸ AI Assistant) that carries out drafting requests on the active drawing with CADCraft's own commands, plus `cadcraft-cli ask` for the same thing headless. Row A2 of `docs/gaps.md` lists this as "an in-app assistant (AutoCAD has Autodesk Assistant)".

I have a working implementation on a fork (branch `assistant-headless` of `lucabyte42-lab/cadcraft-ai-assistant-features`, three commits). Before opening pull requests I'd like to agree on the design here, because one part of it is a judgement call for the maintainers.

## Why FANTASTICO, and a disclosure

The implementation uses a FANTASTICO account (fantastico.cc) as its default model endpoint. I proposed it because I know well how it works and I'm integrating it in several other projects: it is a prepaid, pay-as-you-go credit, with no subscription, that gives one key for every major model. The service and its `fantastico-sdk` crate (crates.io, MIT OR Apache-2.0) are made by Byte42, my company, so you know where the proposal comes from.

The feature is optional and never in the way: without an account key the panel only says how to get one, nothing else in CADCraft changes, and a user who doesn't want it simply never opens it.

## How it works

- **Everything is a command.** The assistant's tools are CADCraft's MCP tools at command level (`command_line`, `execute`, `inspect_drawing`, `query_entities`, `list_commands`, `new_drawing`, `open`, `save`, `cancel`). No pointer, no screenshots. `new_drawing`, `open` and `save` run only after the user confirms in the panel.
- **One turn is one undo step.** The panel wraps a turn in an undo group through the engine, so one U takes back whatever the assistant did.
- **Never crash.** Model output is hostile input: bounded steps per turn (20, then one last call without tools so the model says what it did), bounded tool calls per step and result sizes, tools run on the UI thread through the control methods with a timeout, the …

title: Missing important Plot settings
author: RazorCMV
body:
### Description
The current **Plot** dialog in CADCraft already covers the core settings (`Paper size`, `Orientation`, `Plot area`, `Fit to paper`, `Center the plot`, `X/Y offset`, `Scale`, `Plot style table`, and `Preview`). However, comparing it to the standard AutoCAD (Mac) Plot workflow, several important features are still missing to make page setup and plotting complete.

### High-Priority Missing Features
1. **`Apply to Layout` Button (Persisting Paper Size & Plot Settings):** 
   * Currently, there is no `Apply to Layout` button at the bottom of the dialog. This feature is essential because it saves the selected **Paper size**, orientation, scale, and offsets directly to the active Model/Layout tab without having to execute a plot first.
2. **Direct `Save as PDF` Button:** 
   * A dedicated `Save as PDF` button right next to `Preview` at the bottom of the dialog for quick PDF exporting without changing the system printer/plotter dropdown.

### Additional Important Missing Settings (Compared to AutoCAD Mac)
* **Page Setup Management:** 
  * Ability to save, load, and import named **Page Setups** (plus a `Default to previous plot` checkbox to quickly reuse the last configuration).
* **Enhanced Scale Controls (Standard Presets & Ratio Mapping):** 
  * Currently, `Scale` is just a single numeric input field (`1`). It should support a dropdown with standard CAD scale presets (e.g., `1:10`, `1:50`, `1:100`, `Custom`) and explicit unit mapping (`[X] mm / inches = [Y] drawing Units`).
* **Number of Copies:** 
  * A `Copies` numeric input field when a printer/plotter is selected.
* **Plot Style Table Editor & Toggle:** 
  * A quick checkbox to toggle `Print with plot styles` on/off, alongside a button to edit/inspect the selected `.ctb` / `.stb` table.
* **Enhanced Paper Preview Thumbnail:**

title: revcloud: saved cloud has no RevcloudProps XDATA, so it is not recognised as a revision cloud (0.8.0)
author: philipp-tch
body:
**Version:** cadcraft 0.8.0 (linux-x86_64 tarball), `cadcraft-cli`

**What happens:** `revcloud` (Rectangular `{p1, p2}`) draws a closed LWPOLYLINE with arc segments, but writes no `RevcloudProps` XDATA. AutoCAD (2016+) and other readers use that XDATA to tell a revision cloud from a plain polyline, so the saved cloud is not recognised as a revision cloud: REVCLOUD's object edits do not apply to it, and tools that look for clouds do not find it.

**Expected:** a cloud created by `revcloud` is saved with the same `RevcloudProps` XDATA (registered AppID) that AutoCAD writes, so it round-trips as a revision cloud.

**Reproduce (synthetic, no input file):**

```sh
cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'revcloud {"p1":[0,0],"p2":[100,50]}' --save /tmp/w.dxf
python -c "import ezdxf, ezdxf.revcloud; d=ezdxf.readfile('/tmp/w.dxf'); print([ezdxf.revcloud.is_revcloud(e) for e in d.modelspace().query('LWPOLYLINE')])"
# prints [False]; an AutoCAD-made cloud prints [True]
```

(ezdxf 1.4.5; `ezdxf.revcloud.is_revcloud` checks for the `RevcloudProps` XDATA.)

**Context:** we draw revision clouds with `revcloud` around each change before saving a new revision of a plan. As a workaround our check counts closed arc polylines on the revision layer instead of looking for real revision clouds.

title: feat(cli): `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` for `cadcraft-cli mcp`
author: S3Serv
body:
`cadcraft-cli mcp` has no way to confine which files the agent's commands may read and write.
PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already solve this with `--automation-read-root <dir>` /
`--automation-write-root <dir>`, where omitting a root deliberately denies that direction of
access. This asks for the same two flags here, with the same semantics.

### Why

The README invites agent use ("let an agent drive it over MCP"), but without roots the MCP server
runs with the full permissions of the user who launched it. An agent driving it can read and write
anything that user can — SSH keys, `.env` files, password-manager exports, cloud-synced
directories. That is a lot of trust to extend to a tool whose job is to open and save files, and it
is the one thing standing between `cadcraft-cli mcp` and an unattended agent workflow.

PhotoCraft's enforcement is exactly the right shape in practice: a save outside the root returns

    automation path rejected: absolute paths must be inside the automation root: `/path/outside`

...and nothing is written. Having the same guarantee in `cadcraft-cli` would make the five CLIs
consistent and let the same agent configuration work across the suite.

### Current workaround, and why it is not sufficient

On macOS I wrap the server in the kernel sandbox:

    /usr/bin/sandbox-exec -D ROOT=/path/to/project -f craft.sb cadcraft-cli mcp

This works, and it actually catches a little more than a path check would — it blocked a temp file (in a sibling app, DesignCraft)
written to `$HOME` during a save (`~/.designcraft-save-*.tmp`) that an in-app check on the target
path would have missed. But:

- `sandbox-exec` is formally deprecated by Apple.
- It is macOS-only. There is no equivalent for Linux or Windows users, so on those platforms there
  is no way to confine `cadcraft-cli mcp` at all.
- It is per-user configuration rather than something the tool guarantees, so a careless launch
  silently has no boundary.

title: feat(desktop): `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` for `CADCraft --control`
author: S3Serv
body:
`CADCraft --control 7982` has no way to confine what the control channel may read and write.
PhotoCraft and VectorCraft take `--automation-read-root <dir>` / `--automation-write-root <dir>` on
the **desktop app**, not only on the CLI, and enforce them on control requests. This asks for the
same two flags on `CADCraft`, with the same semantics.

### Why it has to be on the app, not the CLI

`cadcraft-cli mcp --connect` only relays: the app process does the actual opening and saving. So any
boundary passed to the CLI is irrelevant in that mode, and the app's own roots are the only thing
that can confine an attached agent.

On macOS I confine the *headless* path with the kernel sandbox (`/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`), but that
cannot help here — the app is launched from the Dock, outside the sandbox, and is the process doing
the I/O. The result is that an agent attached to a live CADCraft window can read and write anything the
user can, with no way to narrow it. VectorCraft documents exactly this split and solves it:

    vectorcraft --control 7979 --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

and a save outside the write root comes back as an ordinary error reply instead of being written —
which I verified on 0.12.0.

### Request

`--automation-read-root <dir>` and `--automation-write-root <dir>` on `CADCraft`, honoured for every
control request, with a root left out granting none of that access. Environment-variable
equivalents (as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft have) would be welcome but are secondary.

This is the desktop-app counterpart of the CLI request; filing it separately so the two can be
tracked on their own.

Happy to test a build.

Environment: macOS 27.0 (arm64), CADCraft 0.8.0

title: Drafting Settings: POLARMODE bit 8 (Shift to Acquire) has no UI control
author: william-wwh
body:
## Summary

`POLARMODE` bit 8 (`SHIFT_ACQUIRE`, "Shift to Acquire") is implemented in the engine but has no control in the Drafting Settings dialog. The other three `POLARMODE` bits are all exposed there, so this one looks like an oversight rather than a deliberate omission.

## Current state

The engine constant and its use exist:

- `crates/engine/src/snap/tracking.rs:41` — `pub const SHIFT_ACQUIRE: u32 = 8;` (doc: "Points are acquired by holding Shift, not by resting the cursor on them.")
- `crates/engine/src/snap/tracking.rs:273` — `shift_acquire: s.polar_flags & polarmode::SHIFT_ACQUIRE != 0`
- `crates/engine/src/snap/tracking.rs:391` / `:401` — `hover(..., shift_acquire, shift)` branches on it when deciding whether to acquire a point.
- `crates/engine/src/sysvars.rs:236` — `POLARMODE` accepts `0..=15`, so bit 8 is settable and persists.

The dialog does not expose it. `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:177-186` (`tracking_options`) has:

- bit 1 `RELATIVE` — "Absolute" / "Relative to last segment"
- bit 2 `TRACK_POLAR` — "Track orthogonally only" / "Track using all polar angle settings"

and bit 4 `ADDITIONAL` is exposed separately at `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:156-160` ("Additional angles" checkbox). Bit 8 has no widget anywhere in the UI: `rg SHIFT_ACQUIRE` matches only the two lines in `tracking.rs`.

## Impact

Object snap tracking always acquires points by resting the cursor on a snap point, with no way to switch to shift-only acquisition from the interface. The only workaround is typing `POLARMODE` at the command line and adding 8 by hand (e.g. `0` → `8`, or `2` → `10`).

## Expected

A radio pair under "Object Snap Tracking Settings" in Drafting Settings, matching the existing `flag(...)` pattern used for bits 1 and 2:

- "Automatic" (bit 8 clear)
- "Shift to Acquire" (bit 8 set)

AutoCAD has the equivalent setting under Options ▸ Drafting ▸ Alignment Point Acquisition.

## Note on related work

PR #450 ("... tracking options in Drafting Settings", fixe…

title: Diameter symbol (%%c) shows as an unreadable character
author: benandez
body:
Reported by a tester: the diameter symbol in drawing text shows as an unreadable character instead of Ø.

**Likely cause (unverified):** `%%c` is turned into U+2300 `⌀` (`crates/fonts/src/lib.rs:57`). Our stroke font draws it (`stroke.rs:110`), but many TrueType fonts used by text styles (Arial, Times…) have no U+2300 glyph, so it falls to a missing-glyph box. Files from other software may also store the symbol as U+2205 or `\U+2205`.

**Suggested fix:** when the text font has no U+2300, fall back to U+2205 / U+00D8 in that font, or draw the stroke font glyph; add a test with a TrueType style.

Needs: a sample file or the text style/font the tester used.

title: Double-clicking a block opens the Block Editor away from the drawing; edit in place instead

Reported by a tester: double-clicking a block reference opens the Block Editor separately, so the rest of the drawing can't be seen while editing the block.

AutoCAD's Block Editor also hides the drawing, so this is a "better than AutoCAD" request: REFEDIT already edits a reference in place with the rest of the drawing faded (#813, gaps.md F2).

title: OFFSET ignores objects selected before the command

AutoCAD's OFFSET also ignores the pre-selection, so this is parity, but users coming from other tools expect it. **Proposal:** when exactly one offsettable object is selected before OFFSET, use it and go straight to "Specify point on side to offset" (keep the prompt loop for further objects).

title: Viewport twist angle (51) and view target (17) are dropped on load/save; no way to set a viewport twist (0.8.0)
author: philipp-tch
body:
**Version:** cadcraft-cli 0.8.0 (linux-x86_64)

**What happens:** A paper-space VIEWPORT with a view twist angle (DXF group 51) and a view target (group 17) loses both when cadcraft loads the drawing (DXF and DWG). `entget`/`LIST` show only the un-twisted view centre (group 12), and after `--save` the viewport has neither twist nor target, so the layout shows a different part of the model, unrotated. There is also no way to set a twist: `viewport.set` / `mview` have no twist parameter, and there is no `DVIEW TWist`.

**Why it matters:** site plans in national grid coordinates are commonly shown with twisted viewports (e.g. tracks drawn horizontal on the sheet). Opening and saving such a drawing in cadcraft silently changes every twisted layout view.

**Synthetic repro (ezdxf 1.x, no customer data):**
```python
import ezdxf
doc = ezdxf.new("R2018")
doc.modelspace().add_line((1000, 2000), (1010, 2000))
vp = doc.layout("Layout1").add_viewport(center=(100, 100), size=(150, 100), view_center_point=(0, 0), view_height=20)
vp.dxf.view_target_point = (1005, 2000, 0)
vp.dxf.view_twist_angle = 30.0
doc.saveas("twist.dxf")
```
```
cadcraft-cli run twist.dxf --cmd 'lisp {"code":"(entget (handent \"30\"))"}'
→ (... (10 100.0 100.0 0.0) (40 . 150.0) (41 . 100.0) ... (12 0.0 0.0) (45 . 20.0) ...)   ; no 17, no 51

→ ezdxf: twist None, target None (input: 30.0, (1005, 2000, 0))
```

title: Feature request: set a viewport view twist (viewport.set twist / DVIEW TWist)
author: philipp-tch
body:
**Version:** cadcraft-cli 0.8.0

**Request:** a way to set a paper-space viewport's view twist, e.g. a `twist` parameter (degrees) for `viewport.set` (and optionally `mview`), like AutoCAD's `DVIEW` → `TWist`.

title: import drops the block records' extension dictionary (dynamic blocks lose their data) (0.8.0)
author: philipp-tch
body:
**Version:** cadcraft-cli 0.8.0 (linux-x86_64)

**What happens:** `import {path}` drops the extension dictionary of the block records it brings in. Opening and saving the same file keeps it. Dynamic blocks keep their parameters (e.g. visibility states) in that dictionary, so a dynamic block imported from a library drawing arrives as a plain block showing all states at once.

**Synthetic repro (ezdxf 1.x):**
```python
import ezdxf
doc = ezdxf.new("R2018")
blk = doc.blocks.new("SYM"); blk.add_circle((0, 0), 1)
xr = blk.block_record.new_extension_dict().add_xrecord("OTTO_TEST"); xr.reset([(1, "kept?")])
doc.modelspace().add_blockref("SYM", (0, 0))
doc.saveas("lib_syn.dxf")
```
```
cadcraft-cli run lib_syn.dxf --save own_syn.dxf                                  → SYM block record: extension dict kept
cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'import {"path":"lib_syn.dxf"}' --save imp_syn.dxf  → SYM block record: no extension dict
```
(checked with `ezdxf.readfile(f).blocks.get("SYM").block_record.has_extension_dict`: `True` / `False`)

**Expected:** `import` keeps the block record's extension dictionary (as the own load/save does), so dynamic block definitions stay dynamic, like copying them between drawings in AutoCAD.

I searched for an existing ticket; #185 is about implementing dynamic block parameters, this one is only about the data being dropped on `import`.

title: [Bug] Crash on launch on older macOS: wgpu requested invalid value 'metal3.2' (Device Lost)
author: siramin
body:
### Describe the bug
CADCraft 0.8.0 fails to launch on an older Intel Mac (MacBook Pro 11,5). The application crashes instantly with a `wgpu` error because it attempts to compile shaders using the `metal3.2` standard, which is unsupported by this hardware/macOS version.

### To Reproduce
1. Run `/Applications/CADCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/CADCraft` on a MacBook Pro 11,5 (Mid-2015).
2. The application crashes immediately in the terminal.

### Terminal Output & Logs
```text
2026-10-19T13:53:14.073Z INFO  [main] cadcraft: cadcraft 0.8.0 (714111d528acc86dc6b41e03f9a82cabc1066dca) (macos x86_64)
2026-10-19T13:53:14.833Z ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'
...
note: use 'macos-metal2.4' or 'osx-metal2.4' for 'Metal 2.4 (macOS)' standard
note: use 'metal3.0' for 'Metal 3.0' standard
...
2026-10-19T13:53:14.834Z ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
Error: Wgpu(RequestDeviceError(RequestDeviceError { inner: Core(Device(Lost)) }))
```

### Expected behavior
The application should either fallback to an older Metal standard (e.g., Metal 2.4, which is the maximum supported on macOS 12 Monterey for this hardware) or gracefully degrade to an OpenGL/Vulkan backend rather than hard-crashing on `metal3.2`.

### Environment & Hardware

- **OS:** macOS 12 Monterey (Max official version for this model)
- **GPU:** Intel Iris Pro / AMD Radeon R9 M370X (Supports up to Metal 2.4)

### Additional Context
Attempting to force the backend using `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` or `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` did not resolve the issue, suggesting the `metal3.2` requirement might be explicitly set or hardcoded in the current `wgpu` / shader compilation setup. (Note: PhotoCraft works fine on this same machine).

title: ACAD_TABLE: the table's *T block is written in absolute coordinates while the table also carries its insertion point, so AutoCAD draws the table shifted by that point (a table at 200,100 shows at 400,200)
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy) — black-box observation only. Synthetic drawing generated by CADCraft; no AutoCAD-produced file attached. Reproduced on v0.8.0; main at `0b32c2e` reads the same in the lines under Hint.

_Commands are bash (Git Bash on Windows); PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'table {"at": [200, 100], "rows": 3, "cols": 2, "rowHeight": 8, "colWidth": 20, "cells": [["A1", "B1"], ["A2", "B2"], ["A3", "B3"]]}' \
  --cmd 'entities {"type": "Table"}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path": "case.dwg", "version": 2018}' \
  --save case.dxf
```
In AutoCAD (a copy of each file): `entget` of the ACAD_TABLE (groups 2 and 10), the LINEs of its block definition (`tblobjname "BLOCK"` + `entnext`), then `ZOOM E` and `EXTMIN`/`EXTMAX`. The table is the only object in the drawing.

## Expected
The table occupies x 200–240, y 76–100 (2 columns of 20, 3 rows of 8, top-left at the insertion point), as `entities` reports it in CADCraft (`"insert":{"x":200.0,"y":100.0}`, `colWidths [20,20]`, `rowHeights [8,8,8]`).

## Actual (AutoCAD 2026)
| file | ACAD_TABLE group 10 | block `*T1` base | LINEs inside `*T1` | drawing extents in AutoCAD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| case.dxf | 200, 100 | 0, 0 | x 200–240, y 76–100 | **400,176 → 440,200** |
| case.dwg | 200, 100 | 0, 0 | x 200–240, y 76–100 | **400,176 → 440,200** |

The block content already sits at the table's final position, and the table reference adds the insertion point again, so the table appears exactly (200, 100) away from where it was placed. The farther from the origin a table is placed, the farther it lands; a table placed in the lower-right part of a sheet lands off the paper.

Tables at the origin are not affected, which is likely why the AutoCAD check in #1220 (a table at 0,0) does not show it.

author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy, never saving) — black-box observation only. The drawing is synthetic and generated by CADCraft.

```bash

  --cmd 'style {"name":"R","font":"romans.shx","current":true}' \
  --cmd 'dimstyle {"name":"D","current":true,"DIMTXSTY":"R","DIMTXT":5,"DIMASZ":5,"DIMDEC":0}' \
  --cmd 'circle {"center":[0,0],"radius":30}' \
  --cmd 'dimdiameter {"handle":"100","at":[40,40]}' \
  --cmd 'circle {"center":[100,0],"radius":30}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path":"case.dwg","version":2018}' --save case.dxf
```
(`100` is the handle the first `circle` returns.) In AutoCAD, read the MTEXT inside the dimension's `*D` block, then draw a diameter dimension on the second circle with `DIMDIAMETER` (style D current) and read its `*D` MTEXT too. Plot model space to PDF (DWG To PDF, monochrome.ctb).

The CADCraft dimension plots with the diameter sign, like the one AutoCAD draws on the second circle.

| file | dimension | text in the `*D` MTEXT | char code | plotted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| case.dxf | CADCraft (handle 101) | `⌀60` | U+2300 | **"60"**, no sign |
| case.dxf | drawn by AutoCAD, style D | `∅60` | U+2205 | sign + "60" |
| case.dwg | CADCraft (handle 101) | `⌀60` | U+2300 | **"60"**, no sign |

title: Page setup: a landscape layout is saved as portrait paper (297 x 420) with plot rotation 90, so AutoCAD reads it as Portrait; AutoCAD saves the same layout as 420 x 297 with rotation 0
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy, never saving over it) — black-box observation only. All drawings are synthetic and generated by CADCraft; no AutoCAD-produced file is attached. Reproduced on v0.8.0; main at `0b32c2e` reads the same in the lines quoted under Hint.

Not covered by #1085 (merged): that PR fixes group 72 (paper units) only. This issue is about groups 44/45/73, which #1085 does not touch. Keeping device papers in portrait internally is the documented convention (`docs/plotters.md`); the problem is only how 44/45/73 are written for AutoCAD. Related, not duplicates: #1232/#1266 (margin axes) and the open #1086 (offsets 46/47).

_Commands are bash (Git Bash on Windows); PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'plottermanager {"action": "new", "name": "DWG To PDF.pc3", "from": "CADCraft PDF", "output": "pdf"}' \
  --cmd 'plottermanager {"action": "set", "name": "DWG To PDF.pc3", "paper": {"name": "ISO full bleed A3 (420.00 x 297.00 MM)", "width": 420, "height": 297, "margins": [0, 0, 0, 0]}}' \
  --cmd 'layout.set {"name": "Layout1"}' \
  --cmd 'pagesetup {"device": "DWG To PDF.pc3", "paper": "ISO full bleed A3 (420.00 x 297.00 MM)", "landscape": true, "scale": 1, "plotStyleTable": "acad.ctb", "plotArea": "layout", "margins": [0, 0, 0, 0]}' \
  --cmd 'rectang {"p1": [10, 10], "p2": [410, 287]}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path": "case.dwg", "version": 2018}' \
  --cmd 'plottermanager {"action": "delete", "name": "DWG To PDF.pc3"}' \
  --save case.dxf
```

title: dimangular {lines: [h1, h2]} saves a 3-point angular dimension (type 5) instead of a 2-line angular dimension (type 2)
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. Interop observed in Autodesk AutoCAD 2026 (`accoreconsole`, opening a copy, never saving) — black-box observation only. The drawing is synthetic and generated by CADCraft.

_Commands are bash (Git Bash on Windows); in PowerShell 5.1 the inner double quotes are lost._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'line {"points":[[0,0],[100,0]]}' \
  --cmd 'line {"points":[[0,0],[80,60]]}' \
  --cmd 'dimangular {"lines":["100","101"],"at":[60,20]}' \
  --cmd 'line {"points":[[200,0],[300,0]]}' \
  --cmd 'line {"points":[[200,0],[280,60]]}' \
  --cmd 'saveas {"path":"case.dwg","version":2018}' --save case.dxf
```
In AutoCAD, `entget` the CADCraft dimension; then run `DIMANGULAR` picking the two lines on the right and `entget` that one.

## Expected
A dimension made from two lines is saved as a 2-line angular dimension, as AutoCAD saves one made the same way.

## Actual (AutoCAD 2026)
| file | dimension | type (group 70 & 7) | subclass | text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| case.dwg and case.dxf | CADCraft `dimangular {lines}` | **5** | **AcDb3PointAngularDimension** | 37° |
| case.dwg and case.dxf | AutoCAD `DIMANGULAR`, two lines picked | 2 | AcDb2LineAngularDimension | 37° |

The angle and the text are the same, so nothing looks wrong on paper; what differs is the kind of object AutoCAD receives (a vertex and two points instead of two lines). Together with the missing DIMASSOC for angular dimensions (separate report), nothing ties the dimension to the two lines once the file is in AutoCAD.

## Hint
Reproduced on v0.8.0; main at 0b32c2e reads the same. `angular_from_lines` builds `DimKind::Angular3P` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/annotate.rs#L186-L203`), and so does the interactive two-line path (L1235-L1238). The writer already maps `DimKind::Angular` to type 2 (`crates/io/src/dxf_write.rs#L907`), but no command creates that kind.

title: Scripting gaps for a full sheet from the CLI: attdef justify/style, LISP dictionary access, entmake BLOCK, entnext over ATTRIBs, handent on non-graphic objects, chaining handles in a --cmd batch
author: Rickpixell
body:
This ticket was split, as the triage bot asked, into one ticket per gap:

1. #1658 — attdef has no justification or text style parameters; a justified attribute definition needs a LISP entmod afterwards
2. #1659 — LISP: namedobjdict, dictsearch, dictnext and tblobjname are not defined, so routines cannot reach LAYOUT and other non-graphic objects
3. #1660 — LISP: entnext from an INSERT with attributes skips its ATTRIBs and goes to the next entity
4. #1661 — LISP: handent returns nil for non-graphic objects (layer, layout), so entget cannot reach them by handle
5. #1662 — LISP: entmake of BLOCK / ENDBLK returns nil, and the entities in between go to the current space instead of a block definition
6. #1663 — CLI: a --cmd cannot use a handle returned by an earlier --cmd in the same run (e.g. viewport.set right after mview)

Context kept here: independent runs built an A1 sheet (title block with attributes, viewports with per-viewport layers, materials table) purely through `cadcraft-cli run --cmd …`; each gap above forced a workaround, or had none (entnext over ATTRIBs, handent on non-graphic objects). Related, not duplicates: #648 (AutoLISP conformance corpus), #1039 (agent contract), #1225 / #1252 (unknown keys accepted silently), #1335 (LISP follow-up).

The original table is in this ticket's edit history. This ticket can be closed in favour of the six above, or kept as a tracking list — whichever the maintainers prefer.

title: SpaceMouse on macOS: works with hidapi's C backend; measurements for SpaceMouse Wireless (256f:c63a)
author: firedevil79
body:
Follow-up to #650 / #623 / #983 (macOS is still listed as missing). Tested on macOS 27, Apple Silicon,
SpaceMouse Wireless (3Dconnexion 256f:c63a, connected by USB cable), no 3DxWare installed.

I'd like to contribute macOS support for the SpaceMouse and would open a PR once #983 is merged
(it touches the same lines). Before I do, one decision is yours: see the question below.

**What works.** With the `cfg` gate widened to `target_os = "macos"` and `hidapi` added to the macOS
dependencies (`default-features = false`), the reader from #650 works unchanged: detection,
pan/zoom, both buttons. The diff is small: 4 lines in `apps/cadcraft/Cargo.toml`, the `cfg` conditions
in `spacemouse.rs` (15 places) and the hardware-parity row.

**Question.** `hidapi` has pure-Rust backends only for Windows (`windows-native`) and Linux
(`linux-native-basic-udev`). On macOS it compiles the bundled C hidapi with the `cc` crate and links
IOKit, which conflicts with the comment "no proprietary SDK or C HID library" in `apps/cadcraft/Cargo.toml`.
Is that acceptable for macOS, or would you prefer a small pure-Rust IOKit backend
(`objc2-io-kit` has an `hid` feature with IOHIDManager/IOHIDDevice)? I can do either.

**Measurements (SpaceMouse Wireless):**
- Two HID interfaces: usage page 1 / usage 8 (the multi-axis one) and usage page 1 / usage 0x30 (ignored).
- Report 1: 13 bytes, report ID + six int16 LE in one report (the `payload.len() >= 12` branch in
  `decode` handles it). About 63 reports/s while the cap is deflected. Silent at rest (2-3 zero reports
  after release), so the calibration problem from #983 applies here too.
- Range is about +-350 counts, so `FULL_SCALE = 500` gives roughly 70 % of full speed.
- Report 3 = buttons (bit 0 = 0x01, bit 1 = 0x02). Report 0x17 = 3 bytes, looks like battery
  (percent + a flag that changed while charging over USB); currently ignored.
- Signs: p0 right +, p1 away from user -, p2 push down +, p3 tilt away -, p4 tilt right -,
  p5 twist clockwise…

title: LISP: entnext from an INSERT with attributes skips its ATTRIBs and goes to the next entity
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. CLI output only; no other program involved. Reproduced on v0.8.0; main at `0b32c2e` reads the same in the lines under Hint. Split out of #1654 (one gap per ticket, as the triage bot asked).

_Commands are bash; PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'attdef {"tag": "TAG", "default": "x", "at": [0, 0], "height": 2.5}' \
  --cmd 'line {"points": [[0, -5], [20, -5]]}' \
  --cmd 'block {"name": "B", "base": [0, 0], "handles": ["100", "101"], "keep": "delete"}' \
  --cmd 'insert {"name": "B", "at": [50, 50], "attribs": {"TAG": "VALUE"}}' \
  --cmd 'line {"points": [[100, 0], [120, 0]]}' \
  --cmd 'entities {"type": "Insert"}' \
  --cmd 'lisp {"code": "(setq e (handent \"104\")) (list (cdr (assoc 0 (entget e))) (cdr (assoc 66 (entget e))) (if (entnext e) (cdr (assoc 0 (entget (entnext e))))))"}'
```
(The insert is handle 104 in this sequence.)

## Expected
As in AutoLISP: `("INSERT" 1 "ATTRIB")`, then the remaining ATTRIBs and a SEQEND, so attribute values can be read and `entmod`-ed.

## Actual (0.8.0)
`("INSERT" 1 "LINE")`: the insert has attributes (66 = 1, and `entities` lists `TAG = VALUE`), but `entnext` goes straight to the next LINE. No workaround was found for editing an ATTRIB from LISP. (The `attedit` command can change values; this ticket is about reaching ATTRIBs from LISP.)

## Hint
`entnext` walks `handles_in_order`, i.e. top-level entities; ATTRIBs live inside the insert ([crates/engine/src/lisp/drawing.rs#L439-L450](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/0b32c2e6a14c761835ea62c01e7b20845971d781/crates/engine/src/lisp/drawing.rs#L439-L450)).

title: CLI: a --cmd cannot use a handle returned by an earlier --cmd in the same run (e.g. viewport.set right after mview)
author: Rickpixell
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. CLI output only; no other program involved. Reproduced on v0.8.0; main at `0b32c2e` reads the same in the lines under Hint. Split out of #1654 (one gap per ticket, as the triage bot asked).

_Commands are bash; PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes._

## Steps to reproduce
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'layout.set {"name":"Layout1"}' \
  --cmd 'mview {"p1":[20,20],"p2":[200,150]}' \
  --cmd 'viewport.set {"scale":1}'
```

## Expected
Some way to act on the result of the previous command in the same batch, for example a "last created" target, or a placeholder that the runner fills with a handle returned earlier.

## Actual (0.8.0)
`mview` returns `{"viewports":["100"]}`, then `viewport.set` fails with RC 1: ``invalid parameters for `viewport.set`: no viewport given (pass `handle` or select a viewport)``.

Workarounds found: guess the handle in advance, select the viewport by a point on its border (`select {"at":[x,y]}`) or with `qselect`, or run `mspace {}` before `viewport.set` — but `mspace` activates the last active or the first viewport, not the one just created (after two `mview` calls in a row it activates `100`, not `101`).

## Hint
`viewport.set` adds only one fallback, the active viewport inside MSPACE ([crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs#L532-L539](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/0b32c2e6a14c761835ea62c01e7b20845971d781/crates/engine/src/cmd/layout.rs#L532-L539)). `targets` reads `handles`, `handle` or the current selection only ([crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs#L297](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft/blob/0b32c2e6a14c761835ea62c01e7b20845971d781/crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs#L297)). Related, not duplicates: #1039 (agent contract: strict addressing, errors as data); the open PR #1043 rewrites the same `targets`.

As a SolidWorks user, I would really appreciate the ability to **open and import native SolidWorks files directly in CADCraft**, without having to export them to STEP or another intermediate format first.

**Requested functionality:**
- Native support for `.SLDPRT` (SolidWorks Part)
- Native support for `.SLDASM` (SolidWorks Assembly)
- Preserve assembly structures, component positioning and geometry when importing
- Ideally support importing complete assemblies with their referenced part files

**Why this matters:**

We use SolidWorks extensively for mechanical engineering and industrial 3D printer development at CR-3D. Being able to open existing SolidWorks projects directly would significantly simplify our workflow and eliminate unnecessary file conversions.

Even read-only import with accurate geometry and assembly structure would already be a valuable first step.

Thanks for considering this feature!

title: Embedded hub: post cadcraft:opened after a hub-supplied document finishes loading
author: ChristianGrubbs
body:
## Summary
When CADCraft runs embedded in the SCC Space Creative Hub, the host has no signal that a document handed to the app has finished opening. The hub's host agent waits for an `cadcraft:opened` (or `cadcraft:loaded`) message and gives up after 5 s. The document is really open 1.8–2.4 s after it is handed over, so every launch with a file shows "Opening…" about 5 s longer than it needs to.

## Evidence
Measured on 2026-10-19 against the served build, headless Chromium, 3 cold and 3 warm launches per app across two runs:
- PdfCraft: `opened` reported at 7.4 s against a true delivery of 2.4 s.
- CADCraft: 6.9 s against 1.9 s.
- GridCraft: 6.7 s against 1.8 s.
- The gap was 5002–5003 ms in every one of the 36 runs.

## Request
The hub hands the file to the app with a `{ type: 'cadcraft:open', name, bytes }` message on `window.parent`. After the app has finished loading that document and is showing it, it should post one reply:

```js
window.parent.postMessage({ type: 'cadcraft:opened', name }, location.origin);
```

If the open fails, post `{ type: 'cadcraft:open-failed', name, error }` instead. The hub will treat that as a failed open rather than waiting out the timeout.

## Workaround on our side
Until this ships, the hub will resolve the open shortly after the hand-off. That works but can't detect a failed open.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Saving clears a layout's plot window corners (page setup plot type Window): 48/49/140/141 written as 0
author: philipp-tch
body:
## Summary

Saving a drawing whose layout page setup plots a **window** (DXF `LAYOUT` group 74 = 4) keeps the plot type,
but writes the window corners (groups 48/49 and 140/141) as zero. After a plain open → save, the layout's
page setup therefore plots an empty window `(0,0)–(0,0)` in programs that honour it, so the sheet no
longer plots there. The rest of the page setup stays the same.

Related: #491 covers layout plot areas inside CADCraft, and layout region plotting was out of scope there.
This report is only about losing the stored values on save.

## Steps to reproduce

Generate the synthetic file `win.dxf` with ezdxf 1.4.5. It contains layout `WIN`: paper 420 × 297 mm,
plot type 4, window (0, −297)–(420, 0), and a frame inside that window.

```python
import ezdxf
d = ezdxf.new("R2018"); d.header["$INSUNITS"] = 4
L = d.layouts.new("WIN"); L.page_setup(size=(420, 297), margins=(0, 0, 0, 0), units="mm")
x = L.dxf_layout.dxf
x.plot_type = 4
x.plot_window_x1, x.plot_window_y1, x.plot_window_x2, x.plot_window_y2 = 0, -297, 420, 0
L.add_lwpolyline([(5, -292), (415, -292), (415, -5), (5, -5)], close=True)
d.saveas("win.dxf")
```

```sh
cadcraft-cli run win.dxf --save win_rt.dxf
```

## Expected

In `win_rt.dxf`, layout `WIN` keeps the values it was opened with: 74 = 4, 48 = 0, 49 = −297, 140 = 420, 141 = 0.

## Actual

In `win_rt.dxf`, layout `WIN` has 74 = 4, 48 = 0, 49 = 0, 140 = 0, 141 = 0.

`layout.list` reports `"plotArea": "window"` for this layout, but the page setup has no field for the corners,
so they cannot survive the save.

## Environment

cadcraft-cli 0.8.0 (linux-x86_64 release build); group codes compared in the DXF text.

title: Extents: an MTEXT without a wrap width is measured by its raw contents, formatting codes included
author: MadsHolten
body:
**Version:** `main` at `0b32c2e`.

### What happens

`mtext_box` in `crates/doc/src/extents.rs` (lines 52–56) sizes an MTEXT that has no wrap width (group 41 = 0) by the character count of its raw `contents`:

```rust
let lines = t.contents.split("\\P").count().max(1);
let longest = t.contents.split("\\P").map(|l| l.chars().count()).max().unwrap_or(1);
let mut w = if t.width > 0.0 { t.width } else { t.height * 0.8 * longest as f64 };
```

Inline formatting codes count as characters: `{\fArial|b0|i0|c0|p34;…}`, `\H0.8x;`, `\W0.9;`, `\C1;`, `\A1;`, `\S1/2;` and so on. Drawings written by AutoCAD and most add-ons put a font switch in front of nearly every MTEXT. A two-character label then measures as ~40 characters wide. Since `Drawing::extents` → `entity_bounds` → `mtext_box` is used for ZOOM Extents, plot extents and our model-space framing, a short label near the edge of a drawing can push the extents far out.

The `blank()` check above it has the same gap: an MTEXT whose contents are only formatting (e.g. `{\fArial|b0|i0|c0|p34;}`) is not blank and gets a box.

### Reproduction

`mtext.dxf`, a 10-unit LINE and an MTEXT "AB" with a font switch:

```

  0

  8

0.0

0.0

10.0

0.0
  0
MTEXT
  8
0

0.0

10.0
 30
0.0
 40
2.5
 71
1
  1
{\fArial|b0|i0|c0|p34;\H0.8x;\W0.9;AB}
  0
ENDSEC
  0
EOF
```

```rust
let d = cadcraft_io::read_dxf(&std::fs::read("mtext.dxf")?)?;
let b = d.extents(&cadcraft_doc::Space::Model);
```

| MTEXT contents | Model extents X |
|---|---|
| `{\fArial\|b0\|i0\|c0\|p34;\H0.8x;\W0.9;AB}` | 0.00 .. 76.00 |
| `AB` | 0.00 .. 10.00 (the LINE) |

The text itself draws about 4 units wide in both cases.

The box is measured from the text the MTEXT shows, as the renderer lays it out. AutoCAD's extents follow the drawn text.

title: Font substitution by name (FONTMAP): Windows fonts in text styles never resolve to metric-compatible installed fonts
author: MadsHolten
body:
**Version:** `main` at `0b32c2e`. **Type:** feature request.
**Related:** #130 (SHX → TTF fallback, which added FONTALT/FONTFALLBACK); #1004 (writes the reverse mapping, Liberation → Arial, on save).

### Situation

On Linux (servers, containers, most desktops) the Windows core fonts named by text styles (`arial.ttf`, `arialbd.ttf`, `times.ttf`, `cour.ttf`, …) are usually not installed. Their metric-compatible substitutes are (Liberation Sans/Serif/Mono, `fonts-liberation` / `fonts-liberation2`). CADCraft never uses them for those names:

- `ttf::find` → `Db::lookup` (`crates/fonts/src/ttf.rs`, around line 306) tries the file stem (`arial`, `arial regular`, …) and then `by_family`, which matches the family or full name. Liberation's families are "Liberation Sans" etc., so `arial` does not resolve.
- `TextFont::resolve` (`crates/fonts/src/lib.rs`, around line 288) then falls back to FONTALT if set, else the single-stroke font. Text in Arial styles draws in the thin stroke font. It is too light at plot weight and has different widths, so line breaks and alignment move.
- FONTALT cannot serve as a TrueType-only substitute. `resolve` uses it for every font that is not found, and `find` returns `None` for all `.shx` names, so setting FONTALT to Liberation Sans also turns every SHX style (`romans.shx`, `isocp.shx`, …) into Liberation Sans. AutoCAD keeps FONTALT for missing fonts generally and maps names one by one through FONTMAP.
- FONTFALLBACK (`fallback_for`) works per missing glyph, not per missing font, so it does not help either.

### Request

A name → font substitution table, applied in `ttf::find` before the "not found" path. AutoCAD has FONTMAP for this: a font mapping file (`acad.fmp`, `original;substitute` per line) that it consults before FONTALT. Any of these would do:

1. A built-in default table of metric-compatible substitutes, used only when the original is not installed. For example `arial*` → Liberation Sans, `arialn*` → Liberation Sans Narrow, `times*`…

title: MTEXT Editor Does Not Open When Double-Clicking Existing Text

When I use the `MTEXT` command for the first time to create text, an editor window opens where I can enter and format the text.

title: Snap: TAN and PER snaps can resolve into an arc's gap (outside its sweep)
author: william-wwh
body: ### Problem An arc is snapped as its full circle. When resolving a tangent (`TAN`) or perpendicular (`PER`) snap against an arc, the solver returns points on the circle even if they fall outside the arc's start/end angles. This means a tangent can be offered where the arc doesn't actually exist, drawing a line that points into blank paper (or snapping to a virtual point in the gap). It can be off by a small margin, making it look almost correct, or completely miss the arc. ### Steps to reproduce **Method 1: Tangent as the second point** 1. Draw an arc with a visible gap (e.g., a quarter-circle) using the `ARC` command. 2. Start a `LINE` command (`L`) and click to specify the **first point** somewhere outside the arc. 3. At the "Specify next point" prompt, type `tan` and press Enter. 4. Move the cursor toward the **blank space in the arc's gap**. 5. A snap marker (`Tangent`) appears on the imaginary circle, even though there is no line drawn there. 6. Click to place the point, then finish the line. The resulting line will point into the blank space and won't touch the visible arc. **Method 2: Deferred tangent as the first point** 1. Start a `LINE` command (`L`). 2. At the "Specify first point" prompt, type `tan` and press Enter. 3. Move the cursor toward the blank space in the arc's gap. 4. A snap marker (`Deferred Tangent`) appears on the imaginary circle. 5. Complete the line; it will not touch the visible arc. ### Expected behavior Tangent and perpendicular snaps should only resolve to points that lie within the arc's `start` and `end` angles. If the solution falls in the gap, it should be discarded. Deferred snaps should also preserve the arc's sweep so they resolve correctly later. ### Cause…

title: Feature request: read the stored text of a dimension's *D block (LISP / CLI), and keep it on save
author: dmaru2s
body:
**Use case:** We use dimension blocks to catch scale errors in incoming drawings. We compare the text stored in each dimension's anonymous *D block with the distance between its defpoints. In a side-by-side run of 1,872 drawings, CADCraft 0.8.0 matched our reference CAD on 1,869. The 3 differences were exactly the cases where the stored *D text was needed.

**What is missing in 0.8.0**
- LISP: `tblobjname` is not available, `(tblsearch "BLOCK" "*D1")` has no `-2` group, and `bedit "*D1"` reports not found. So a script cannot walk the entities inside a *D block.
- CLI: `cadcraft-cli info` does not report a dimension's stored block text.
- Save: writing DXF/DWG rebuilds *D blocks from the defpoints. The originally stored text is lost.

**Request:** any one of these would cover it:
1. LISP access to *D block contents (`tblobjname` + `entnext`, or the `-2` group from `tblsearch`).
2. In `cadcraft-cli info` (JSON), for each dimension: the stored block text next to the measured value.
3. An option to keep the original *D blocks when saving.

**Minimal reproduction (synthetic):** Create one linear dimension, then move one defpoint without regenerating the block, or change DIMLFAC and keep the old block. Rendering shows the stored text (good). LISP and the CLI cannot read that text, and saving replaces it.

Related: #1599 (the same blocks must keep being drawn as cached).

title: BricsCAD parametric blocks: drawn correctly, but their parameters aren't shown and the data is dropped on save (findings and a staged proposal)
author: ohagmann
body:
## What happens

BricsCAD (V21+) has its own "parametric blocks" instead of AutoCAD's dynamic blocks. Block libraries made in BricsCAD
use them a lot, typically for visibility: a parameter like `BAS_2` with the states "Sichtbar"/"Unsichtbar" shows or
hides a group of objects. Public test file: `02-ahu-schema-a.dwg` from the CC0 corpus offered in #1592
(https://github.com/ohagmann/cadcraft-sample-dwgs), a BricsCAD V26 drawing (AC1032) with 28 references in changed
states and 18 anonymous blocks.

CADCraft (0.9.0, main 0b32c2e):

- **Drawing is right.** For every reference whose state differs from the block's default, BricsCAD writes an anonymous
  copy (`*U11`) in which the hidden objects sit on a layer `*SUPPRESS` (frozen and off). CADCraft honours the layer, so
  the picture matches BricsCAD and AutoCAD.
- **Parameters aren't shown.** The Properties palette has nothing like BricsCAD's "Parameters" section; AutoCAD
  shows nothing either, so this is only a wish.
- **The data is dropped on save, without a word.** The parametric data lives in BricsCAD's own objects
  (`BDMDBFEATUREDATA`, `BDMDBCONFIGURATIONTABLE`, `BDMDBOBJECTDEPENDENCY`, `BDMOBJECT`, … — 3,900 of them in the
  sample) plus standard `ACDBASSOCVARIABLE`s. The DWG bridge keeps the AssocVariables but not one of the BDM objects
  (acadrust reads them as `Unknown` with raw bytes; they never reach the DXF rendition), and the blocks' `BDM_DATABASE`
  dictionary entries are left dangling. After a CADCraft save, BricsCAD shows every one of these blocks as a plain block:
  nothing can be switched any more, and the user isn't told. This is the "custom-class objects lost through DWG" part
  of gap 1 / FF1, with a concrete and common case.

## What the data looks like (no public spec; read structurally)

Only the DWG object framing is needed, not BricsCAD's field layout: R2010+ objects store the handle stream's size, so
the handles (and the UTF-16 string stream before them) of an unknown object can be read without…

title: STRETCH with a crossing polygon or window moves an MLINE as a whole or not at all, instead of moving only the vertices inside
author: Flowgwirzard
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. CLI output only; no other program involved.

_Commands are bash; PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes._

**Steps to reproduce**
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'mline {"points":[[0,0],[3000,0],[3000,2000]],"scale":200}' \
  --cmd 'stretch {"polygon":[[2500,1500],[3500,1500],[3500,2500],[2500,2500]],"delta":[610,0]}' \
  --cmd 'entities {"type":"MLine"}'
```
The polygon covers only the last vertex (3000,2000).

**Expected:** as with a LINE or a polyline, only the vertex inside the polygon moves: vertices `(0,0) (3000,0) (3610,2000)`.

**Actual (0.8.0):** `{"stretched":1}` is reported, but the MLINE is unchanged: `(0,0) (3000,0) (3000,2000)`.
- Polygon over the last two vertices: also unchanged.
- Polygon over only the **first** vertex: the whole MLINE moves 610 (`(610,0) (3610,0) (3610,2000)`), i.e. all vertices, not one.
- Polygon over all three vertices: all move (correct).
- Dragging that last vertex with its grip does what is expected: `grip.stretch {"grips":[["100",2]],"delta":[610,0]}` gives `(0,0) (3000,0) (3610,2000)`.

So STRETCH seems to decide for the MLINE as one object (first vertex only?) instead of vertex by vertex. A LINE with its end in the same polygon stretches correctly (`(0,0) (3610,0)`), so this is specific to MLINE.

**Why it matters:** moving one wall of a plan drawn with MLINE walls (a normal way to draw walls) with STRETCH leaves the wall where it was, with the count saying 1 was stretched.

title: REVCLOUD from LISP/script: Arc length takes one value (maximum becomes minimum), and Object has no "Reverse direction" prompt
author: Flowgwirzard
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. CLI output only.

_Commands are bash; PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes._

**Steps to reproduce**

(a) Arc length:
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'lisp {"code":"(command \"_.REVCLOUD\" \"_A\" \"200\" \"800\" \"_R\" \"0,0\" \"2000,1000\")"}' \
  --cmd 'lisp {"code":"(command \"_.REVCLOUD\" \"_R\" \"5000,0\" \"6000,500\")"}'
```
(b) Reverse direction:
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'lisp {"code":"(progn (entmake (list (cons 0 \"LWPOLYLINE\") (cons 100 \"AcDbEntity\") (cons 8 \"0\") (cons 100 \"AcDbPolyline\") (cons 90 4) (cons 70 1) (list 10 0.0 0.0) (list 10 1000.0 0.0) (list 10 1000.0 1000.0) (list 10 0.0 1000.0))) (command \"_.REVCLOUD\" \"_O\" (list 500.0 0.0) \"_N\"))"}'
```

**Expected (AutoCAD 2021):**
(a) Arc length asks "Specify minimum length of arc" and then "Specify maximum length of arc", so the second REVCLOUD reports minimum 200 and maximum 800.
(b) After Object picks the polyline, REVCLOUD asks "Reverse direction [Yes/No] <No>:", and `"_N"` answers it.

**Actual (0.8.0):**
(a) The second REVCLOUD prints `Minimum arc length: 200.0000   Maximum arc length: 200.0000`. The 800 is lost; the maximum follows the minimum.
(b) The cloud is finished at once ("Revision cloud finished."), then `unknown command `_N``. The same happens with `"_Y"`. A routine written for AutoCAD therefore sends an extra token that is run as a command.

**Why it matters:** an AutoCAD routine that sets the arc size or answers the reverse prompt cannot run unchanged. If this is a deliberate simplification, the prompt flow could be listed in the docs; if not, it is a gap.

title: LISP: (getvar "DWGPREFIX"), "DWGTITLED", "CDATE", "FILEDIA" (and more) return nil
author: Flowgwirzard
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. CLI output only.

_Commands are bash; PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes._

**Steps to reproduce**
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'lisp {"code":"(list (getvar \"DWGPREFIX\") (getvar \"DWGTITLED\") (getvar \"CDATE\") (getvar \"FILEDIA\") (getvar \"DWGNAME\") (getvar \"CLAYER\"))"}'
```
and on a saved file, to see that it is not only about a new drawing:
```bash
cadcraft-cli run some.dxf --cmd 'lisp {"code":"(list (getvar \"DWGPREFIX\") (getvar \"DWGTITLED\") (getvar \"DWGNAME\"))"}'
```

**Expected:** as in AutoCAD: `DWGPREFIX` the drawing's folder with a trailing backslash, `DWGTITLED` 1 for a saved/named drawing and 0 for an unnamed one, `CDATE` the date and time as a real (e.g. `20261020.1342`), `FILEDIA` 1 (and `SETVAR` of it remembered).

**Actual (0.8.0):** `(nil nil nil nil "Drawing1" "0")` for a new drawing, and `(nil nil "some.dxf")` for the saved file. `DWGNAME` and `CLAYER` work.

Also returning nil in the same test: `DATE`, `TDUPDATE`, `CMDECHO`, `CMDACTIVE`, `LASTPROMPT`, `TILEMODE`, `VISRETAIN`, `PLATFORM`, `LOGINNAME`. `SETVAR`/`GETVAR` of `USERS1`, `USERI1` and `FILEDIA` do round-trip (set then read), so the variable store exists; these names are simply not provided by `getvar`.

**Why it matters:** an ordinary routine uses `DWGPREFIX` to find files that sit next to the drawing, `DWGTITLED` to know whether the drawing has been saved, `CDATE` to stamp a revision date, and `FILEDIA` / `CMDECHO` to switch dialogs and echo off around a script. With nil, such routines fail or write to the wrong place.

title: LISP: tblsearch "BLOCK" of an attached or overlaid xref gives flags 0 and no path, so a routine cannot tell it from a normal block
author: Flowgwirzard
body:
**Environment:** CADCraft 0.8.0 (release MSI, `cadcraft-cli 0.8.0`), Windows 11 Pro. CLI output only.

_Commands are bash; PowerShell 5.1 strips the inner quotes._

**Steps to reproduce**
```bash
cadcraft-cli run --metric --cmd 'line {"points":[[0,0],[1000,0]]}' --save x_src.dxf
cadcraft-cli run --metric \
  --cmd 'xattach {"path":"x_src.dxf","overlay":true}' \
  --cmd 'lisp {"code":"(tblsearch \"BLOCK\" \"x_src\")"}'
```
(`xattach` with `"overlay":false` gives the same.)

**Expected (AutoCAD):** the block table record of an xref has bit 4 set in group 70 (external reference), bit 8 as well for an overlay, bit 32 when it is resolved, and group 1 holds the xref path. So a routine can tell `x_src` is an xref and where it comes from.

**Actual (0.8.0):** `((0 . "BLOCK") (2 . "x_src") (70 . 0) (10 0.0 0.0 0.0))`. It is identical to the record of an ordinary block made with `block`. CADCraft itself knows it is an overlay (the `xattach` reply says `"type":"Overlay"`, `"status":"Loaded"`), so the information exists, it is not passed to LISP.

**Why it matters:** a routine that purges, explodes, binds, counts or inserts blocks has to skip xrefs, and cannot.

title: Web build: report the open document in the viewport title
author: robertcsakany
body:
The web build sends no `ViewportCommand::Title` naming the open document (eframe would log it as `Unhandled egui viewport command: Title(…)` on the web). WordCraft, GridCraft, PhotoCraft and VectorCraft do (`<document>[ •] — <App>`).

An embedding host (pi-agent-dashboard runs the web build in a sandboxed iframe and delivers the document as a synthetic drop) uses that title to confirm WHICH document the app opened and whether it has unsaved changes. Without it the host can only assume the drop worked after a delay; when a drop is refused, the app's default document is mistaken for the file (seen with CADCraft 0.8.0 and a `.dwg`: it showed `Drawing1`).

Ask: send `Title("<file name>[ •] — <App>")` on open, rename and dirty change, like WordCraft.

title: Viewport contents: a block reference that reaches into the viewport is drawn whole, then clipped
author: MadsHolten
body:
**Version:** `main` at `0b32c2e`.

### What happens

`contents()` in `crates/render/src/lib.rs` (around line 706) draws model space through a layout viewport. It culls model-space objects against the viewport's model window with slack (the `seen` filter, lines 728–737): an object whose `entity_bounds` miss the window is skipped. Only top-level model-space objects are culled, though. A block reference whose bounds reach the window goes to `insert()` (line 1538), which draws every entity of the block (and of its nested blocks) before the result is clipped to the viewport.

Drawings that keep a whole site or building in one block and show details of it through small viewports make that very expensive. In a real project (a 63 MB DWG), one model-space INSERT of a block with about 470 000 objects (250 000 LINEs, 112 000 LWPOLYLINEs, 14 000 hatches, 27 000 3DFACEs and more, spread over several kilometres) is shown through viewports that each cover 13–15 m at 1:50. Building the plot of one sheet allocated about 9.3 GB transiently for that INSERT alone, to keep a display list of about 0.2 GB after clipping. Hatch patterns are generated across the whole site at the viewport's tolerance before most of them are clipped away.

### Expected

Objects inside a block that cannot reach the viewport's window are skipped like top-level ones, so the cost of a viewport follows what it shows rather than the size of the blocks that reach into it.

### Reproduction (synthetic)

1. A block `SITE` holding many objects spread far apart, for example 100 000 LINEs, each 1 unit long, 10 units apart along X.
2. One INSERT of `SITE` in model space.
3. A layout with a viewport whose model window covers a few of those lines (for example 20 × 20 units).
4. Plot the layout (`build_plot` with `Space::Paper`): every line of the block is built, not just the few in the window.

### Possible fix

Carry the model window (block coordinates are reached through `ctx.xf`) into the sub-contexts that `insert()` cr…

title: `properties.set` ignores `thickness` (reports `changed`, writes no DXF group 39); `properties` never shows thickness
author: chazmaniandinkle
body:
**Version:** cadcraft-cli 0.8.0. **OS:** Windows 11 Pro (x64), CLI headless.

**Summary:** `properties.set {"handles":[...],"thickness":8}` on an LWPOLYLINE and a CIRCLE returns `{"changed":2}` but leaves the thickness at 0: the saved DXF has no group 39 on either entity.
