title: Crash on startup (black window) since v0.7.0 with Intel Core i5-3330 (Ivy Bridge GPU)
author: bddmaster
body:
### Description
The application crashes/shows a black window immediately on startup on a Linux system with an older Intel Ivy Bridge integrated GPU. 

The issue appeared starting from version `0.7.0`. Older version `cadcraft-0.6.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage` works perfectly fine. Versions `0.7.0` and `0.8.0` fail with a black screen. 

The crash is caused by `wgpu`/`egui` requesting a specific stencil buffer format (`GL_STENCIL_INDEX8`) which is not fully supported by the older Mesa driver for this architecture. The application successfully starts only when forcing software rendering via `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

### Log Output (from v0.8.0)
2026-10-20T14:27:09.205Z INFO [main] cadcraft: cadcraft 0.8.0 (714111d528acc86dc6b41e03f9a82cabc1066dca) (linux x86_64), log file /home/user/.config/cadcraft/logs/cadcraft.log
MESA-INTEL: warning: Ivy Bridge Vulkan support is incomplete
Mesa: error: GL_INVALID_ENUM in glTexStorage2D(internalformat = GL_STENCIL_INDEX8)
2026-10-20T14:27:09.603Z INFO [main] cadcraft_ui_egui::gpu: gpu canvas: target Rgba8Unorm, stencil Some(Stencil8)
Mesa: error: GL_INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION in glClearBufferfv(incomplete framebuffer)
Mesa: error: GL_INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION in glClear(incomplete framebuffer)
Mesa: error: GL_INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION in glDrawElementsInstanced
Mesa: error: GL_INVALID_FRAMEBUFFER_OPERATION in glDrawElementsInstanced

### Environment
* **OS:** Linux
* **CPU/GPU:** Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-3330 CPU @ 3.00GHz (Intel Ivy Bridge GT1 integrated graphics)
* **Cadcraft Version:** 0.7.0 & 0.8.0 AppImage (regression since 0.7.0, 0.6.2 works)

### Possible Solution / Suggestion
It seems the graphics backend strictly requires `Stencil8` since v0.7.0, causing a framebuffer failure (`incomplete framebuffer`) on older Ivy Bridge hardware. Would it be possible to implement a fallback mechanism during graphics initialization if `GL_STENCIL_INDEX8` fails, or automatically fall back to software rendering/alternative formats?

title: Proposal: Interactive Auxiliary Guide Lines System for Precision Drafting
author: olesme
body:
## Description

### Context & CAD Workflow Requirements
Visual 2D and 3D drafting in modern CAD systems (such as Kompas-3D) heavily relies on auxiliary/construction lines to establish precise geometry before drawing actual structural entities. Currently, precise alignment and layout planning can be tedious without dedicated infinite reference lines.

Adding an **Auxiliary Guide Lines System** will dramatically improve speed and visual accuracy during technical drawing and modeling.

### Core Functionality
1. **Guide Line Types (Kompas-style):**

   - **Specialized Geometry Guides:** Tangent lines to arcs/circles, perpendiculars, and angle bisectors.

2. **Smart Snapping & Interaction:**
   - Automatic snapping to intersections between two guide lines, guide-to-object intersections, and midpoints.
   - Dynamic visual highlight when cursor aligns with guide intersections.

title: Proposal: OpenSCAD Parametric Scripting Engine & Live Preview
author: olesme
body:
## Description

### Context & Parametric 3D Modeling Needs
With planned 3D support (inherent to DWG/DXF standards), programmatic CSG (Constructive Solid Geometry) modeling offers a powerful complement to manual GUI modeling. OpenSCAD is the de facto industry standard for code-based parametric modeling.

Integrating an **OpenSCAD Scripting Environment** unlocks two major advantages:
1. **AI-Agent & Automation Friendliness:** Code-based CAD is uniquely suited for LLM/AI agents. Generating and refactoring structured `.scad` text parameters is significantly easier and more deterministic for AI models than manipulating complex visual UI state trees or direct mesh topology.
2. **Reusability & Rapid Implementation:** Instead of building a CSG engine from scratch, CadCraft can leverage existing open-source ecosystems. Depending on CadCraft's architecture, this can be implemented either via a lightweight **bridge layer** to existing tools or by **porting/using pure-Rust CSG/OpenSCAD execution modules** (e.g., leveraging Rust-native CAD/CSG libraries or AST parsers).

---

1. **Embedded Script Editor & Live Viewport:**

title: Proposal: Universal 3D Import & Mesh-to-CAD Conversion Engine (STEP & STL)
author: olesme
body:
## Description

### Context & Interoperability Requirements
To support modern engineering, manufacturing, and 3D printing workflows, CadCraft needs robust import and conversion capabilities for external 3D data formats. Users frequently work with two distinct paradigms:
1. **STEP (`.step` / `.stp`):** Exact mathematical boundary representations (B-Rep) used in professional CAD, requiring parsing into true CAD solids.
2. **STL (`.stl`):** Polygonal mesh representations (triangulated surfaces) standard for 3D printing and 3D scanning. 

Crucially, handling STL files goes beyond mere visualization: engineers and makers frequently need a **"Convert to Exact Geometry" (Mesh-to-CAD / Reverse Engineering)** pipeline to transform dumb triangular meshes back into clean, editable analytical surfaces, planes, cylinders, and solid bodies.

---

### Core Functionality
1. **STEP File Processing & B-Rep Import:**
   - Import ISO 10303 STEP files containing solid bodies and assembly hierarchies.
   - Parse topology directly into native CadCraft parametric solid geometry (faces, edges, analytical surfaces, NURBS).

2. **STL Import & Lightweight Mesh Handling:**
   - Fast import of high-poly or low-poly triangular meshes (`.stl`).
   - Direct mesh manipulation mode for positioning, slicing inspection, and quick preparation for 3D printing.

3. **Core Feature: "Convert to Exact Geometry" (Mesh-to-CAD Engine):**
   - **Feature & Surface Recognition:** Algorithms to analyze triangulated meshes, detect sharp edges, planar regions, cylindrical/spherical faces, and fillets.
   - **Analytical Fitting:** Fit mathematical primitives (planes, cylinders, cones, splines) over clustered mesh regions.
   - **Solid Reconstruction:** Stitch fitted surfaces into a watertight B-Rep solid body, enabling full parametric editing (filleting, extrusions, boolean modifications) on previously raw STL/scanned models.

title: Mouse stuttering with 1000 Hz polling rate mouse (Maxexcel ATR 41260) in v0.7.0+, not present in v0.5.0
author: Torcente
body:
## Description

When using a Maxexcel ATR 41260 gaming mouse (1000 Hz polling rate, no companion software) via USB, the cursor stutters and occasionally freezes inside CADCraft v0.7.0 and v0.8.0. The touchpad works perfectly, and other USB mice work fine on the same port.

The issue is 100% reproducible:
- CADCraft v0.5.0: mouse works perfectly
- CADCraft v0.7.0 / v0.8.0: mouse stutters
- Close CADCraft: mouse works perfectly again
- Reopen CADCraft v0.8.0: stuttering returns

## Hypothesis

This appears to be related to a change in the mouse input handling between v0.5.0 and v0.7.0. If the newer versions use `GetRawInputData` (or an equivalent egui/winit path that polls per-frame), the 1000 Hz report rate from the mouse may overflow the input buffer, causing dropped frames and stuttering. The touchpad (typically ~125 Hz) is unaffected.

This is a known class of issue with high-polling-rate mice and raw input APIs (see SDL issue #8756, Valorant's switch to `GetRawInputBuffer`).

## Environment

- OS: Windows (version: 11 23H2)
- CADCraft version: 0.8.0 (also reproducible on 0.7.0, not on 0.5.0)
- Mouse: Maxexcel ATR 41260 (gaming, 1000 Hz polling, plug-and-play, no driver)
- Connection: USB (tried multiple ports, same result)
- Touchpad: works perfectly in all versions

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect Maxexcel ATR 41260 via USB
2. Launch CADCraft v0.8.0
3. Move the mouse — observe stuttering/freezing
4. Close CADCraft — mouse is smooth again
5. Reopen CADCraft — stuttering returns

## Workaround

Downgrading to v0.5.0 resolves the issue.

## Suggested fix

- Switch from `GetRawInputData` to `GetRawInputBuffer` (non-blocking), or
- Add a setting to disable raw input / fall back to standard Windows mouse messages
